# MASTER PROMPT — Medical Scoring Systems Platform (Formulas · Calculators · Converters)

> **You are receiving this file as a complete, self-contained build brief.** It merges five source
> documents (an agent operating protocol, a 297-row scoring-systems catalog, a ~440-entry JSON
> encyclopedia of scoring systems, a formula-corrections dossier, and a cognitive-scales dossier)
> into one instruction set plus its data appendices. Everything you need to build the product is in
> this file. Do not wait for further input unless this file explicitly tells you to pause.

---

## 0. How to read and use this file

| Part | What it is | How to use it |
|---|---|---|
| **Part 1 — Mission & Product Spec** | What to build, feature set, data model, calculator engine spec | Your requirements baseline. |
| **Part 2 — Agent Operating Protocol** | The owner's working agreement (phases, gates, rules) + autonomy override | Governs HOW you work. Read first, follow always. |
| **Part 3 — Data Sources & Precedence** | The five merged sources, their IDs, and conflict-resolution order | Governs WHICH data wins when sources disagree. |
| **Part 4 — Correction & Completion Work Orders** | Explicit orders to fix missing formulas, blocked calculators, converters, links, and registry gaps | Your backlog. Execute every work order. |
| **Part 5 — Verification & Test Vectors** | Known-correct values, QA checklist, Definition of Done | Your acceptance criteria. Nothing ships without passing. |
| **Part 6 — Deliverables & Kickoff** | Repo layout, artifacts, first tasks | Your output contract. |
| **Appendix A** | Master catalog — 297 scores (Excel row-numbered), tiers, flags, cross-refs | Primary inventory. Row numbers are the canonical IDs used by corrections ("Row 139" = Appendix A row 139). |
| **Appendix B** | Formula corrections dossier (verbatim) | Overrides Appendix A/C on any conflict. |
| **Appendix C** | Cleaned encyclopedia — unique scoring-system entries as JSON (IDs `E001…`), indexed by category | Primary detail source: variables, formulas, interpretation bands, citations, limitations, copyright, confidence. |
| **Appendix D** | Cognitive & neurological scales dossier (verbatim, items #203–#222 + brief-mention table) | Authoritative for MMSE/MoCA/SLUMS/Mini-Cog/CDT/CAM/FAB/ACE-III/TMT/RAVLT/RUDAS/Blessed etc. |
| **Appendix E** | Data audit & provenance report | Known defects, discrepancies, merge log, unresolved items. Treat every item here as a flagged risk. |
| **Appendix F** | Source transcript's own final coverage summary | Reference only — actual content may deviate; Appendix E documents deviations. |

**Handling rules for the data appendices:**

1. Appendices A–D are **data, not suggestions**. Ingest them programmatically (parse the markdown
   tables and the fenced `json` blocks) into your unified registry. Never paraphrase or "improve"
   clinical content silently — every change must trace to a work order in Part 4 or a logged decision.
2. Where a value is marked `[MISSING IN SOURCE]`, `?`, `verify`, `UNDECIDED`, or `skip`, it is an
   **open item** — resolve it via the work orders (Part 4). Never fabricate coefficients, cutoffs,
   PMIDs, or URLs. If you cannot verify something (no web access / not in sources), ship it flagged
   `needs-verification` or as an external-link card, per Part 4.3.
3. Precedence on conflict (Part 3.3): **Appendix B (corrections) > Appendix D (cognitive dossier) >
   Appendix C (encyclopedia) > Appendix A (catalog)**. The catalog remains the canonical *inventory*
   (what must exist); the corrections remain the canonical *formula fixes*.
4. Every registry entry keeps provenance: catalog row(s), encyclopedia `E###` id(s), corrections
   section/row refs, Appendix D item numbers. Provenance is displayed in the UI ("Sources" panel).

**Scale of the job (for planning):** ~297 catalog rows + ~278 encyclopedia entries + ~20 cognitive
dossier items, deduplicated into one registry (expect ≈ 350–420 unique scoring systems after
cross-merge), of which the large majority are implementable as local calculators, a minority are
categorical/dropdown tools, and ~10 are hard-blocked models that ship as external-link cards.

# PART 1 — MISSION & PRODUCT SPECIFICATION

## 1.1 Mission

Build a **comprehensive, offline-capable clinical scoring & calculations platform** ("the Platform")
that turns the merged reference data in this file into a working product:

- **Calculators** for every implementable medical scoring system in the registry (point-of-care style:
  enter values → get score → get interpretation bands → see citations).
- **Converters** — a clinical unit-conversion suite wired into calculator inputs (so a lab value can
  be entered in either unit system) and available standalone.
- **Bedside calculations** — the quick formula module (anion gap, corrected calcium, osmolality,
  QTc, MELD family, etc. — Appendix A category "Bedside calculations" + Part 4.5).
- **Reference cards** — for categorical classifications (CCS angina, Fontaine, Rutherford, Forrest,
  BI-RADS…) and for hard-blocked models (EuroSCORE II, QRISK3, STS, APACHE IV…) that ship with
  formula summaries + verified external links instead of local computation.
- **Full provenance** — every score shows purpose, formula, interpretation, limitations, copyright
  status, confidence badge, citations with PubMed links, and its source rows/IDs from this file.

**Product name:** UNDECIDED (working slug: `medscores`). Do not block on this; use the slug and log
the naming decision as pending user input.

**Primary users:** clinicians and medical students at the bedside/desk. **Non-negotiable:** a
persistent "educational/decision-support, not a substitute for clinical judgment" disclaimer
(app-level banner + per-calculator footer), and no patient-identifiable data stored anywhere.

## 1.2 Platform & stack

- **Form factor:** responsive web app, static-first (no server needed for v1), PWA-capable so it
  works offline after first load. Favorites/recents persist in `localStorage` only.
- **Recommended stack** (re-validate in Phase 3 per protocol, present trade-offs, but this is the
  default recommendation): **Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS**, all scoring data compiled
  into versioned static JSON; a small calculation engine in pure TypeScript (fully unit-testable,
  no eval of free-form strings — compile formula specs to typed functions or a sandboxed expression
  evaluator with an allow-list).
- Alternatives to weigh in Phase 3: Next.js static export (heavier, but path to SSR later);
  SvelteKit (smaller bundle). Either is acceptable if justified.

## 1.3 Feature set (v1)

1. **Unified Score Registry** — one JSON dataset (schema in 1.4) compiled from Appendices A–D with
   the corrections from Appendix B applied, per the work orders in Part 4.
2. **Browse & search** — by category (21 catalog categories) → subcategory; instant fuzzy search on
   name, acronym, and aliases (e.g., "chads", "cha2ds2", "glasgow blatchford"); filter by tier
   (1 = core daily use, 2 = common, 3 = specialized) and by engine/status; recents + favorites.
3. **Calculator pages** — auto-generated from the registry:
   - typed inputs with units, ranges, validation, and inline unit conversion (Part 4.5);
   - live score + interpretation band highlight as inputs change;
   - support for: numeric inputs, boolean toggles, single-select (points mapped), multi-select,
     mutually-exclusive option groups (e.g., ABCD² weakness vs speech — Appendix B Row 186),
     conditional/algorithmic flows (e.g., PERC → Wells gating — Appendix B Row 164), categorical
     selectors with no arithmetic (e.g., CCS class, Fontaine stage), clamping rules (e.g., MELD
     creatinine floor 1.0 / cap 4.0, dialysis → Cr = 4 — Appendix A Row 47);
   - "What this means" panel: bands, caveats, limitations;
   - "Sources & evidence" panel: formula (human-readable), citations → PubMed links, official
     links, confidence badge, copyright note, provenance IDs.
4. **Unit converter module** — standalone converter UI covering the suite specified in Part 4.5.
5. **Bedside calculations module** — the quick-formula cards listed in Part 4.5.
6. **External-calculator cards** — for `external-only`/`blocked` entries: what the model predicts,
   its inputs, why it can't run locally, and verified links to official calculators (Part 4.3).
7. **Coverage & data-quality report** — generated at build time: every registry entry's status
   (`ready` / `needs-verification` / `external-only` / `blocked`), missing-field audit, link-check
   results, test results. This is a shipped artifact, not just CI output.
8. **Print/export** — print-friendly single-score sheet (score, inputs, result, interpretation,
   citations, disclaimer).

## 1.4 Registry entry schema (contract)

Every scoring system in the Platform is one registry object. Extend only via logged decisions.

```json
{
  "id": "MSC-0001",
  "name": "CHADS2-VASc (full name)",
  "acronym": "CHA2DS2-VASc",
  "aliases": ["CHADS-VASC", "CHA₂DS₂-VASc"],
  "category": "Cardiovascular",
  "subcategory": "atrial fibrillation / stroke risk",
  "tier": 1,
  "purpose": "…",
  "engine": "points-sum | weighted-sum | logistic | equation | categorical | algorithm | questionnaire | external-only | display-only",
  "inputs": [
    {
      "key": "age_band",
      "label": "Age",
      "type": "select | number | boolean | multiselect",
      "unit": "years",
      "allowed_units": ["years"],
      "options": [{ "value": "65-74", "label": "65–74 y", "points": 1 }],
      "min": null, "max": null,
      "required": true,
      "clamp": null,
      "group": "age",
      "mutually_exclusive_with": ["age_ge75"]
    }
  ],
  "formula": {
    "human": "CHF(1) + HTN(1) + Age≥75(2) + DM(1) + Stroke/TIA(2) + Vascular(1) + Age 65–74(1) + Female(1)",
    "machine": "sum of selected option points",
    "min": 0, "max": 9
  },
  "output": {
    "kind": "score | class | probability | band",
    "bands": [{ "range": "0", "label": "Low risk", "meaning": "…" }]
  },
  "interpretation_notes": "OAC if ≥2 (men) / ≥3 (women) …",
  "citations": [{ "text": "Lip GYH et al. Chest 2010;137:263-72", "pmid": "20047988", "doi": null }],
  "links": [{ "type": "pubmed | official | mdcalc-search | guideline", "url": "…", "verified": false }],
  "limitations": "…",
  "copyright": "free for clinical use | restricted (e.g., MMSE/PAR) — display structure + license note",
  "confidence": "high | medium | low",
  "status": "ready | needs-verification | external-only | blocked",
  "provenance": {
    "catalog_rows": [15],
    "encyclopedia_ids": ["E012"],
    "corrections_refs": ["B/Row 139"],
    "cognitive_dossier_items": []
  }
}
```

Rules:
- `engine: points-sum/weighted-sum/equation/questionnaire` must be **locally computable** with a
  machine-checkable formula. `logistic` only when coefficients are fully present in the sources
  (or verified from the cited paper with the verification logged). `categorical/algorithm` =
  selector/decision-flow tools. `external-only` = Part 4.3 cards. `display-only` = formula shown,
  value comes from a machine (e.g., base excess — Appendix B Row 135).
- `status: ready` requires: complete inputs, machine formula, bands, ≥1 citation, passing tests.
  Anything sourced only from `confidence: medium/low` encyclopedia entries, or carrying a
  `[MISSING IN SOURCE]`/`verify` marker, ships as `needs-verification` until checked.
- `copyright` restricted tools (e.g., MMSE — Psychological Assessment Resources): implement the
  scoring structure for educational use with a prominent license notice; never imply redistribution
  rights.

## 1.5 Explicitly out of scope for v1 (log as backlog)

- User accounts, cloud sync, EHR integration, FHIR.
- Patient-data persistence beyond anonymous favorites/recents in `localStorage`.
- Multilingual UI (English only; UNDECIDED beyond that).
- Scores whose instruments are fully proprietary and un-sourceable beyond a link card.

The section below is the project owner's working agreement (`AGENTS.md`), merged nearly verbatim.
It governs how you execute this build. Two kinds of modifications were made during the merge, both
clearly marked inline:

   those facilities, follow the note: keep the *intent* (structured delivery, checkpoints, decision

## 2.0 Autonomy Override (added for this build — takes precedence over conflicting protocol text)

This build runs **fully autonomous**. The original protocol requires user approval at every phase
and gate. For this run:

- **Self-approve gates** by writing a `GATE DECISION` entry (gate name, options considered, choice,
  one-line rationale) into `DECISIONS.md`, then proceed. Do not halt waiting for a human.
- **Default decision policy** when choosing between options: prefer (a) the more conservative
  clinical data handling, (b) standards-compliant / published-source-backed behavior, (c) the
  reversible option, (d) the simpler architecture. Never silently drop or delete source data —
  archive with a logged reason.
- **Halt only if** one of these hard stops triggers (write a `BLOCKED.md` entry with context and
  continue on everything else):
  1. Two sources conflict on a **Tier 1** score and Appendix B does not resolve the conflict and
     you cannot verify against the cited literature.
  2. A legal/copyright red flag (e.g., a restricted instrument's content appears to require a
     license you cannot satisfy — mitigate per Part 1.4 copyright rule and continue; halt only if
     mitigation is impossible).
  3. Any action that would destroy data or ship unflagged fabricated clinical values.
- **Locked decisions so far** (do not re-litigate; recorded here per the protocol's "flag and lock"
  rule): single merged master file as source of truth (this document); five-source precedence order
  (Part 3.3); static-first web app (Part 1.2); registry schema (Part 1.4). Product name remains
  UNDECIDED.

## 2.1 The protocol (merged `AGENTS.md`)

## Role
Senior full-stack engineer on the Aeternis team. I own problems end-to-end. User brings the vision. I handle design, architecture, and execution.

## Project Phases (Mandatory — All Software, SaaS, Apps)

Every project goes through all 6 phases in order. No skipping. No compressing. Each phase requires user's approval before the next begins.

### Phase 1 — Discovery & Requirements
Define the problem, the users, the scope, what's in and what's out. Lock decisions. Nothing is designed until this is done.

### Phase 2 — UX/UI Design
Design the full experience before writing a single line of code. Page layouts, interaction models, user flows, edge cases. Written specs minimum. Wireframes when complexity demands it. user approves every page before Phase 3.

### Phase 3 — Architecture & Tech Planning
Stack selection, data model, API choices, system architecture, how components connect, where state lives. Full build spec assembled and approved before any code is written.

### Phase 4 — Development (Build)
Session-based sprints. Incremental delivery. Small working pieces. Frontend and backend can run in parallel — do not mix database changes into a parallel track until the schema is fully stable. Builder + Reviewer pattern on every non-trivial change.

#### Execution Workflow Gates: CLARIFY → DESIGN VALIDATION → SPEC → BUILD → REVIEW → VERIFY → DELIVER

These seven gates govern each sprint inside Phase 4. They are not a parallel track to the six phases — they are the sprint-level execution protocol that runs within Phase 4 for every session.

• **CLARIFY** — 3-5 targeted questions if needed. No assumptions. Sprint scope confirmed before anything moves.
• **DESIGN** — Not Phase 2. No UX/UI design here. Data model first: types, schemas, relationships. Then confirm the architecture still holds for this sprint: how components connect, what talks to what, where state lives. Validation, not creation. Present for approval before spec is written.
• **SPEC** — Technical spec from the design. Endpoints, components, data flow, state management, edge cases. Tests written here define done. Spec is the contract: BUILD executes against it, REVIEW validates against it. Present for approval.
• **BUILD** — Spawn Builder sub-agent with the spec. One change at a time. One commit per working state. Three consecutive failed fixes = stop. Revert to last good commit. Bring back to main agent and rethink before continuing. Load relevant skills.
• **REVIEW** — Spawn Reviewer sub-agent with Builder output + original spec. Reviewer validates independently: spec match, edge cases handled, logic errors, security gaps, regressions. No stake in the output being correct. Main agent does not integrate until Reviewer clears it. Issues flagged = route back to BUILD.
• **VERIFY** — Main agent runs final validation. Code runs. Tests pass. Linter clean. UI has screenshots. Endpoints tested with actual requests. Every spec edge case covered. If anything fails, run through fixer/reviewer sub-agents until VERIFY passes. user never sees a broken output.
• **DELIVER** — Always the main agent. Always visual. Screenshot or link — never just a summary. user verifies with his own eyes. Sprint closed on pass. Routes back through gates on fail.

Stack selection: always evaluate fresh. Present 2-3 options with trade-offs. Recommend one. Justify it.
Cascade prevention: one change at a time. Three failed fixes = revert to last good commit. Rethink from scratch.
Full gate detail: `reference/operations.md`

### Phase 5 — Quality Assurance & Testing
Functional, regression, performance, security, UAT. Testing runs throughout Phase 4 but intensifies here. Nothing ships until this passes.

### Phase 6 — Deployment & Launch
Production environment, domains, SSL, final smoke tests, go live.

## Core Rules
- Nothing ships without user's approval on design + spec.
- Nothing gets written to a project folder without user's explicit approval first.
- When user makes a decision (tool, API, rule, name) — flag it immediately and lock it. Don't wait for later.
- When user says "suggest something" — own the opinion. Present a concrete recommendation with reasoning. Do not punt it back.
- Nothing presented without passing verification.
- Archive, never delete. Propose before acting outside scope.
- Never commit or push without user approval.
- Spawn sub-agents for token-heavy tasks. Never inline massive file reads.
- Don't fill in blanks. Undecided = leave undecided.
- One change at a time. Three failed fixes = revert and rethink.
- Data model first. Always. No exceptions.

## Delivery Protocol

> [!ADAPTATION] The voice + Telegram-button mechanics below (edge-tts, message actions, NO_REPLY) exist only in the original runtime. If your runtime lacks them: deliver as normal structured text/UI, keep every reply self-contained and skimmable, and treat CHECKPOINT as "write the decision/state logs described in the Checkpoint Protocol". The sequence itself is runtime-conditional; the discipline (complete standalone replies, explicit checkpoints) always applies.


Every reply = voice + text + buttons. One unit. Never split across turns.

**Sequence (non-negotiable):**
1. `edge-tts --voice "en-US-SteffanNeural" --text "..." --write-media /home/openclaw/.openclaw/media/kai-voice.mp3` (90s timeout — wait for full completion)
2. `message(action="send", filePath="/home/openclaw/.openclaw/media/kai-voice.mp3", asVoice=true)`
3. `rm /home/openclaw/.openclaw/media/kai-voice.mp3`
4. `message(action="send", message="...", buttons=[[...]])`
5. `NO_REPLY`

**Voice:** Conversational. Complete standalone. user can walk away without reading the text.
**Text:** Complete standalone. Structured for scanning. Not a transcript of the voice.
**Buttons:** Always present on every message. Two persistent buttons on every reply:
- `{"text": "🔊 Read It Out Loud", "callback_data": "read_aloud", "style": "primary"}`
- `{"text": "💾 CHECKPOINT", "callback_data": "checkpoint", "style": "primary"}`
Context-aware action buttons go above these — change based on what's being discussed. All buttons use color + emoji. Multi-word labels get their own row. Persistent buttons can share a row or sit alone — readability wins.
Styles: `success` = confirm/approve (green) · `primary` = navigate/select (blue) · `danger` = destructive (red)

**read_aloud callback:** Read the last text message verbatim as audio. Voice only. No text. No buttons. `NO_REPLY`.

## Model Routing

> [!ADAPTATION] Model names (opus46/sonnet46/haiku45) map to your runtime's model tiers. Apply the rule generically: strongest available model for architecture/review/complex debugging; mid-tier for implementation; cheapest tier only for mechanical tasks (search, summarization, checkpoint filing). Never run complex clinical-data reasoning on the weakest tier.

- **`opus46`** — Architecture decisions, code review, complex debugging, anything where a wrong call is expensive. Use when depth matters more than speed.
- **`sonnet46`** — Daily implementation, writing code, testing, refactoring. Default for BUILD and VERIFY gates.
- **`haiku45`** — Research, discovery, search tasks, summarization, checkpoint sub-agents. Fast and cheap. Never use for heavy reasoning or architectural decisions.

Rule: Never run complex reasoning on haiku45. Never waste opus46 on boilerplate.

## Checkpoint Protocol

Trigger: `checkpoint` keyword or `💾 CHECKPOINT` button.

**Efficiency:** Read `memory/.last-checkpoint` for timestamp. Process only since that timestamp. No file = process full session. Write current timestamp back after execution.

**Parallel execution — two tracks run simultaneously:**

**Track A — haiku45 sub-agent (L1 / L2 / L3)**
Spawn with session transcript + last-checkpoint timestamp. Sub-agent filters and routes:

Filter test: *"Would a future session waste meaningful time without this?"* Already in L1/L2/L3 → discard. Max 5 items.

| Content | Layer | Route |
|---|---|---|
| Behavioral rule / instruction | L1 | AGENTS.md |
| Tool / command / workaround | L1 | TOOLS.md |
| Preference / communication change | L1 | USER.md |
| Active state (what's live now) | L1 | MEMORY.md — one line |
| Completed work / decisions / history | L2 | memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md |
| Domain knowledge / breadcrumb | L2 | memory/[topic].md |
| Architecture decision | L3 | reference/architecture.md |
| API surprise / bug root cause | L3 | reference/lessons.md |
| Reusable pattern | L3 | reference/patterns.md |
| Recoverable from code or context | — | Discard |

Before writing: read target file first. Exists → skip. Outdated → update in place. New → append.

**Track B — Kai (L4 / Project State Sync)**
Kai owns L4 directly. For every active project touched since last checkpoint:

Freshness test per file: *"If I loaded fresh tomorrow, does this accurately reflect where the project stands?"* No → update. Yes → skip.

| File | What to update |
|---|---|
| `projects/[name]/STATE.md` | Phase, status, next action — must reflect end-of-checkpoint state |
| `projects/[name]/DECISIONS.md` | New locked decisions (date + D-ID). Pending → locked promotions. |
| `projects/[name]/TRACKER.md` | Check off completed items. Update phase row. Update blockers. |
| `projects/[name]/specs/` | Modified specs reflect final approved state |
| `projects/[name]/reference/` | Architecture decisions, lessons, patterns from this session |

Then append to L2 → `memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md`: project name, phase, D-IDs locked, what changed, what's blocked, next action.

**Completion:** Review haiku output + Kai's L4 plan. Flag errors. Present full combined plan (L1–L4) to user. Do not write until approved. After approval and execution, write timestamp to `memory/.last-checkpoint`.

**Auto-Sync Rule (no trigger needed)**
At end of any reply where a decision locked or a project file changed: update that project's STATE.md and DECISIONS.md in the same turn. Only what changed. Checkpoint = full reconciliation. Auto-sync = lightweight write between checkpoints.

## 3.2 What each source is best for

- **S2/Appendix A** = the *inventory contract*: what must exist, its category, and its usage tier.
- **S3/Appendix B** = the *formula authority*: wherever it speaks, its values win (it was written
  specifically to fix S2's flagged defects, with published citations).
- **S4/Appendix C** = the *detail authority*: input variables with points/coefficients, score
  ranges, interpretation bands, validation populations, citations (many with PMIDs), limitations,
  copyright status, confidence rating.
- **S5/Appendix D** = the *cognitive/neuro authority*: administration detail (serial 7s, WORLD
  backwards, clock-drawing scoring systems, education adjustments) that S4's psychiatry entries only
  sketch. For MMSE/MoCA/SLUMS/Mini-Cog/CDT/CAM/FAB/ACE-III etc., merge S5 detail into the registry
  entry structured on S4's schema (provenance lists both).

## 3.3 Precedence on conflict (locked decision)

**Appendix B (corrections) > Appendix D (cognitive dossier) > Appendix C (encyclopedia) >
Appendix A (catalog).**

Additional rules:
1. Appendix B **Section D** items are deliberate deviations — keep the described behavior; do not
   "correct" them (Lille score implementation, Pediatric Appendicitis Score max=8 hardcode, CDAI
   extraintestinal ×20 term).
2. Where Appendix C entries disagree with each other (they were written in multiple passes), the
   merge already kept the most complete copy; Appendix E logs every merge and every known residual
   discrepancy (e.g., Full Rockall stigmata points, DKA anion-gap threshold >10 vs >12, CAPRA
   0–12 vs the commonly cited 0–10). Those specific items must be verified against the cited
   primary literature before shipping as `ready`; until then they ship `needs-verification`.
3. Encyclopedia entries carry a `confidence` field: `high` (the large majority), `medium`, `low`.
   Entries below `high` ship `needs-verification` with a visible badge until checked against the
   original citation (see Part 4.8 verification workflow).
4. Never average or blend conflicting clinical values. Pick per precedence, log the choice with
   both source refs in `DECISIONS.md`, and flag for verification if confidence < high.

## WO-6 — Unit converter suite + bedside calculations module

**6a. Standalone converter module** (bidirectional, with the exact factors below; each conversion
gets a round-trip unit test):

| Analytic / quantity | Conversion (factor from → to) |
|---|---|
| Temperature | °C → °F: ×9/5 + 32 |
| Weight | kg → lb: ×2.20462 |
| Length | cm → in: ÷2.54 (plus ft/in helper) |
| Pressure (BP, PaO₂, PaCO₂) | mmHg → kPa: ×0.133322 |
| Glucose | mg/dL → mmol/L: ×0.0555 (bedside convention ÷18 — support both, label them) |
| Creatinine | mg/dL → µmol/L: ×88.4 |
| Urea | BUN mg/dL → urea mmol/L: ×0.357 |
| Total cholesterol / HDL / LDL | mg/dL → mmol/L: ×0.0259 |
| Triglycerides | mg/dL → mmol/L: ×0.0113 |
| Bilirubin | mg/dL → µmol/L: ×17.1 |
| Albumin, total protein | g/dL → g/L: ×10 |
| Calcium | mg/dL → mmol/L: ×0.25 |
| Hemoglobin | g/dL → g/L: ×10; g/dL → mmol/L: ×0.6206 |
| Lactate | mg/dL → mmol/L: ×0.111 |
| CRP | mg/dL → mg/L: ×10 |
| Na⁺/K⁺/Cl⁻/HCO₃⁻ | mEq/L = mmol/L (display equivalence note) |
| WBC / platelets | ×10⁹/L = K/µL = G/L (display equivalence note) |
| FiO₂ | fraction ↔ %: ×100 |
| Volume | mL ↔ L: ÷1000 |
| Urine output | mL/h ↔ mL/kg/h (needs weight input) |

Wiring rule: every numeric registry input declares `unit` + `allowed_units`; when a calculator
expects conventional units (e.g., creatinine mg/dL for MELD) and the user enters SI, convert
inline, show the converted value, and record which unit was used.

**6b. Bedside calculations module** (quick cards; formulas verbatim from Appendix A "Bedside
calculations" category, rows 2–11 and 134–137 area, + corrections):
Anion gap (+ albumin-corrected AG = AG + 2.5×(4 − albumin)); corrected calcium
(Ca + 0.8×(4 − albumin)); serum osmolality (2×Na + glucose/18 + BUN/2.8); QTc (all four formulas
from Row 24); base excess (`display-only` per Appendix B Row 135); renal failure index (WO-3);
plus derived helpers with published formulas: BSA (Du Bois: 0.007184 × weight^0.425 × height^0.725;
Mosteller: √(height_cm × weight_kg / 3600)), IBW (Devine: men 50 + 2.3 kg/inch over 60; women
45.5 + 2.3), adjusted body weight (IBW + 0.4×(actual − IBW)), osmolar gap (measured − calculated
osmolality), corrected sodium for hyperglycemia (commonly +1.6 mEq/L per 100 mg/dL glucose over
100 — flag the 1.6 vs 2.4 debate as `needs-verification` with citation to resolve).

**Accept:** converter round-trip tests pass for all rows; bedside cards exist for every Appendix A
"Bedside calculations" row; unit wiring demonstrated on MELD (mg/dL vs µmol/L creatinine) and
glucose-based scores.

## 5.2 Property tests (apply across the whole registry)

1. **Schema validation** — every entry validates against the Part 1.4 schema (CI gate).
2. **Min/max** — for every `points-sum`/`weighted-sum` engine: all-negative inputs = documented
   min; all-positive = documented max. Any mismatch fails the build (this is how the HATCH 0–12
   error class gets caught automatically).
3. **Band coverage** — interpretation bands must tile the score range contiguously (no gaps,
   no overlaps) unless the source documents gaps intentionally (log those).
4. **Converter round-trip** — `to(from(x)) ≈ x` within 1e-6 relative for every conversion.
5. **Clamp tests** — every input with `clamp` rules (MELD family etc.) tests the clamp boundaries.
6. **Mutual exclusion** — mutually-exclusive groups (e.g., ABCD² weakness/speech, age bands) can
   never sum together.
7. **Provenance completeness** — every entry has ≥1 provenance ref (catalog row, E-id, corrections
   ref, or Appendix D item) and ≥1 citation or an explicit citation-less flag.

## 5.3 Spot-check protocol (Phase 5)

- Randomly select 20 calculators across tiers/categories; for each, recompute one worked example
  by hand from the source text in this file (not from your implementation) and compare.
- Select 10 `needs-verification` entries; confirm the UI badge and the open question render.
- Confirm disclaimers render app-wide and per-calculator; confirm no patient-data persistence
  beyond favorites/recents.

# PART 6 — DELIVERABLES, REPO LAYOUT & KICKOFF

## 6.1 Shipped artifacts

1. **Repository** with the working application (static build output included or reproducible via
   one command).
2. **`data/registry.json`** — the unified registry (Part 1.4 schema), versioned, with a generated
   `data/registry.report.md` (coverage + data-quality report, WO-7/WO-8).
3. **`DECISIONS.md`** — every gate decision, data-conflict resolution, tier assignment, removal,
   and verification outcome (dated, with source refs).
4. **`TESTS.md` / test suite** — golden vectors + property tests, runnable in CI.
5. **`README.md`** — setup, architecture, how to add a score, disclaimer text, license notes
   (including restricted instruments like MMSE).
6. **Screenshots** of key flows (search, a points-sum calculator, a categorical card, an external
   card, converter, bedside module, mobile view) for the DELIVER gate.

## 6.2 Suggested repo layout (adjust with a logged decision if needed)

```
/ apps/web            # Vite + React + TS app
/ packages/engine     # calculator engine (pure TS, unit-tested, no DOM)
/ packages/registry   # registry JSON + schema + validation scripts
/ data                # compiled registry.json, converters.json, reports
/ scripts             # ingestion scripts that parse THIS file's appendices (keep them!)
/ docs                # DECISIONS.md, TESTS.md, coverage report, link-check report
```

The ingestion scripts matter: they make the registry reproducible from this master file, so future
corrections re-run cleanly instead of being hand-patched.

## 6.3 Kickoff sequence (maps to the Part 2 phases)

1. **Phase 1 (Discovery):** ingest appendices → draft unified registry + coverage report → this is
   your requirements artifact. GATE DECISION logged; proceed.
2. **Phase 2 (UX/UI):** page specs for: home/search, category browse, calculator page (all engine
   types), reference card, external card, converter, bedside module, sources panel, disclaimers.
   Written specs; proceed on self-approval.
3. **Phase 3 (Architecture):** confirm stack (default per Part 1.2), data pipeline (markdown
   appendices → ingestion scripts → registry.json → typed engine), state management, testing
   strategy. Build spec; proceed.
4. **Phase 4 (Development):** sprints in this order —
   S1: registry ingestion + schema validation + coverage report;
   S2: engine (points-sum, categorical, equation) + golden vectors;
   S3: app shell (search/browse/calculator page) wired to Tier 1;
   S4: converters + bedside module + unit wiring;
   S5: Tier 2/3 rollup, external cards, links (WO-5), provenance panels;
   S6: verification pass (WO-8), property tests, data-quality report.
   Builder/Reviewer pattern per the protocol; one change at a time; 3-failed-fixes revert rule.
5. **Phase 5 (QA):** vectors, property tests, spot-checks, accessibility/mobile pass.
6. **Phase 6 (Launch):** static deploy (any static host), smoke tests, screenshots, final
   coverage + decision reports.

## 6.4 Standing reminders

- This file is the single source of truth. If you believe a source value is clinically wrong,
  **flag it** (needs-verification + DECISIONS.md + data-quality report) — do not silently change it.
- Appendix E lists every known defect and discrepancy in the merged data. Read it before Phase 1

# Corrected Formulas for All Flagged Issues

Below is a comprehensive correction for every formula conflict, ambiguous/missing score, and hard-blocked item in the document. Where the original data source requires an external calculator or published coefficient table that cannot be reduced to a simple formula, I note this explicitly.

---

## SECTION A — FORMULA CONFLICTS (5 items)

---

### Row 14 — CCS Angina Classification (Cardiovascular)

**Conflict:** "I-IV by exertional threshold" is descriptive; thresholds not defined.

**Correction:** This is inherently a categorical classification — no numeric formula exists. The correct definitions:

| Class | Definition |
|---|---|
| I | Angina only with strenuous, rapid, or prolonged exertion |
| II | Slight limitation — ordinary activity causes angina (walking >2 blocks on level ground or climbing >1 flight of stairs) |
| III | Marked limitation — less-than-ordinary activity causes angina (walking 1–2 blocks or climbing 1 flight) |
| IV | Inability to carry out any physical activity without discomfort; angina may be present at rest |

**Implementation note:** This score cannot be implemented as a numeric calculator. It requires clinician judgment to assign a class based on the patient's symptomatic description of exertional tolerance. Consider implementing as a dropdown selector (Class I–IV) rather than an arithmetic formula.

---

### Row 138 — ABI / Rutherford / Fontaine / WIfI (Cardiovascular)

**Conflict:** Descriptive classifications with incomplete arithmetic.

**Correction:** These are four separate tools:

**1. ABI (Ankle-Brachial Index) — arithmetic formula:**
```
ABI = max(posterior_tibial_systolic, dorsalis_pedis_systolic) [per leg]
      ÷ max(right_brachial_systolic, left_brachial_systolic)
```

| ABI Value | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| ≥1.0 | Normal |
| 0.91–0.99 | Borderline |
| 0.41–0.90 | Mild-to-moderate PAD |
| ≤0.40 | Severe PAD |
| >1.40 | Non-compressible (medial calcification — unreliable) |

**2. Fontaine Classification (descriptive):**
| Stage | Description |
|---|---|
| I | Asymptomatic |
| IIa | Intermittent claudication, pain-free walking distance >200 m |
| IIb | Intermittent claudication, pain-free walking distance ≤200 m |
| III | Ischemic rest pain |
| IV | Ulceration or gangrene |

**3. Rutherford Classification (descriptive):**
| Category | Clinical Description |
|---|---|
| 0 | Asymptomatic |
| 1 | Mild claudication |
| 2 | Moderate claudication |
| 3 | Severe claudication |
| 4 | Ischemic rest pain |
| 5 | Minor tissue loss (non-healing ulcer, focal gangrene with diffuse pedal ischemia) |
| 6 | Major tissue loss (extending above transmetatarsal level) |

**4. WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, Foot Infection) — three components scored independently:**
| Component | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wound | No wound or healed | Small, shallow ulcer | Deeper ulcer with bone/joint exposure | Extensive, deep; extensive deep abscess or gangrene |
| Ischemia | ABI ≥0.80, TP ≥60, ankle pressure ≥100 | ABI 0.60–0.79, TP 40–59, ankle pressure 70–100 | ABI 0.40–0.59, TP 30–39, ankle pressure 50–70 | ABI ≤0.39, TP <30, ankle pressure <50 |
| Foot Infection | No symptoms or signs | Mild: cellulitis ≤2 cm, limited to skin/subcutaneous | Moderate: cellulitis >2 cm, abscess, deep tissue, osteomyelitis | Severe: SIRS, sepsis |

Combined WiFI stage determines amputation risk (low, moderate, high, very high).

**Implementation note:** These should be implemented as separate categorical tools rather than a single arithmetic calculator.

---

### Row 139 — ATRIA Stroke Score (Cardiovascular)

**Conflict:** Ambiguous age weighting ("Age>=75=2? weighting: age 65-74=2? published: age>75=2?").

**Correction:** The published ATRIA stroke risk score (Singer DE et al., *Am J Med* 2013):

| Risk Factor | Points |
|---|---|
| CHF | 1 |
| Hypertension | 1 |
| Diabetes mellitus | 1 |
| Prior ischemic stroke or TIA | 6 |
| Age 65–74 | 2 |
| Age ≥75 | 3 |
| Female sex | 1 |

**Total range: 0–13**

| Risk Category | Score | Annual Stroke Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 0–3 | 0.6–1.4% |
| Intermediate | 4–5 | 2.2–2.7% |
| High | 6–14 | 3.7–14.2% |

Age categories are mutually exclusive (patient receives points for 65–74 OR ≥75, not both). Prior ischemic stroke/TIA (6 points) is the dominant predictor.

---

### Row 274 — HATCH Score (Cardiovascular)

**Conflict:** "Sum of components (8) does not match listed total (0–12)."

**Correction:** The published HATCH score (de Vos CB et al., *Europace* 2008):

| Factor | Points |
|---|---|
| **H**ypertension | 1 |
| **A**ge ≥75 | 1 |
| **T**IA or stroke | 2 |
| **C**OPD | 1 |
| **H**eart failure | 2 |

**Correct total range: 0–7** (1+1+2+1+2 = 7)

- The Excel total of 0–12 is incorrect.
- The component sum of 8 is also incorrect.
- The correct maximum is **7**.
- Score ≥5 predicts >50% risk of progression from paroxysmal to persistent AF within 1 year.

---

### Row 152 — 4AT Delirium Screen (Critical Care)

**Conflict:** "Excel lists AMT4 0-4 and acute change 0-2, which do not match the standard 4AT scoring (AMT4 0-2, acute change 0-4)."

**Correction:** Published 4AT (Bellelli G et al., *Age Ageing* 2014; MacLullich AMJ et al., *BMC Med* 2014):

| Item | Description | Scoring | Max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alertness | Assess immediately | 0 = normal; 1 = mild sleepiness, prompt awakening; 2 = clearly abnormal; 4 = unarrousable or only responds to physical stimulation | 0 or 1 or 2 or **4** |
| AMT-4 | Age, date of birth, place (name/type), current year | 0 = no errors; 1 = 1 error; 2 = ≥2 errors or untestable | 0–**2** |
| Attention | Ask to recite months of year backwards (Jul → Jan) | 0 = ≥7 months correct; 1 = starts but <7 correct; 2 = untestable or refuses | 0–**2** |
| Acute change or fluctuating course | Evidence of acute change in mental status or fluctuating course in preceding 2 weeks and/or past 24 hours | 0 = absent; **4** = present | 0 or **4** |

**Total: 0–14. Score ≥4: possible delirium (high specificity). Score 1–3: possible cognitive impairment.**

The Excel has the AMT-4 and Acute change maximums **swapped**:
- AMT-4 max should be **2** (not 4)
- Acute change max should be **4** (not 2)

---

### Row 163 — FeverPAIN Score (Emergency/Respiratory)

**Conflict:** "components sum to 5, but guidance says '5-6 prescribe'."

**Correction:** Published FeverPAIN (Little P et al., *Br J Gen Pract* 2013):

| Criterion | Points |
|---|---|
| **F**ever (during previous 24 hours) | 1 |
| **P**urulence (pharyngeal exudate or pus) | 1 |
| attend **A**pidly (within ≤3 days of symptom onset) | 1 |
| severely **I**nflamed tonsils | 1 |
| **N**o cough or coryza | 1 |

**Maximum: 5 (not 6)**

| Score | Likely Strep A | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 0–1 | 13–18% | No antibiotic |
| 2–3 | 34–38% | Consider delayed prescription |
| 4–5 | 62–65% | Consider immediate antibiotic |

The "5–6 prescribe" guidance in the Excel is wrong — the maximum achievable score is 5, not 6. The correct guidance is "4–5 prescribe (or consider prescribing)."

---

### Row 281 — ROSIER Score (Emergency/Neurology)

**Conflict:** "weights for glucose/BP missing."

**Correction:** Published ROSIER (Nor AM et al., *Lancet Neurol* 2005):

| Criterion | Score |
|---|---|
| Loss of consciousness | −1 |
| Convulsive activity (fits) | −1 |
| Facial weakness (onset/sudden) | +1 |
| Arm weakness (onset/sudden) | +1 |
| Leg weakness (onset/sudden) | +1 |
| Speech disturbance (onset/sudden) | +1 |
| Visual field defect (onset/sudden) | +1 |

**Total range: −2 to +5**

**Critical note on glucose and BP:**
- **Blood glucose** is NOT a scored component. It is a **mandatory exclusion criterion**: if blood glucose is <3.5 mmol/L (<63 mg/dL), stroke mimic (hypoglycemia) must be excluded BEFORE applying the ROSIER score. Glucose is required to be measured but does not receive points.
- **Blood pressure** is NOT a scored component in the ROSIER. It may be recorded for clinical purposes but does not contribute to the score.

| Score | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| ≥1 | Stroke likely — proceed to imaging |
| ≤0 | Stroke less likely — consider other diagnoses |

### Row 67 — MEOWS (Obstetrics/Gynecology)

**Corrected formula:** Modified Early Obstetric Warning Score (Swanton RDJ et al., 2009; various institutional adaptations exist):

| Parameter | Score 0 | Score 1 | Score 2 | Score 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Respiratory rate (breaths/min) | 11–20 | 9–10 or 21–25 | 6–8 or 26–30 | <6 or >30 |
| Heart rate (bpm) | 50–100 | 101–110 or 40–49 | 111–120 or 30–39 | >120 or <30 |
| Temperature (°C) | 36.0–37.4 | 37.5–38.4 | <36.0 or 38.5–39.0 | >39.0 |
| Systolic BP (mmHg) | 90–149 | 80–89 or 150–160 | <80 or >160 | |
| Diastolic BP (mmHg) | 50–89 | 90–100 | 40–49 or >100 | <40 |
| SpO₂ (%) | ≥95 | 92–94 | <92 | |
| Neurological response | Alert | Responds to voice | Responds to pain | Unresponsive |
| Urine output (mL/hr) | ≥30 | 20–29 | 10–19 | <10 (or <100 mL/4 hr) |

**Score range: 0–24 (varies by institutional version)**

**Trigger criteria (most common):**
- Any single parameter scored **3** → immediate urgent clinical review
- Aggregate score **≥4** → urgent clinical review within 30 minutes
- Aggregate score **≥6** → emergency assessment

**Note:** Multiple published versions exist with slight threshold variations. The above represents the most commonly used consensus thresholds. Institutions should calibrate to local guidelines.

### Row 115 — Revised Geneva Score, Simplified (Respiratory)

**Corrected formula:** Simplified Revised Geneva Score (Klok FA et al., *J Thromb Haemost* 2009):

| Risk Factor | Points |
|---|---|
| Age >65 years | 1 |
| Previous DVT or PE | 1 |
| Surgery (under general anesthesia) or lower-limb fracture within 1 month | 1 |
| Active malignant condition (active or cured <1 year) | 1 |
| Unilateral lower-limb pain | 1 |
| Hemoptysis | 1 |
| Heart rate 75–94 bpm | 1 |
| Heart rate ≥95 bpm | 2 |
| Pain on lower-limb deep venous palpation AND unilateral edema | 1 |

**Total range: 0–10** (the Excel's "0–12" is incorrect)

**Interpretation:**

| Score | Clinical Probability |
|---|---|
| 0–1 | Low (8–10%) |
| 2–5 | Intermediate (23–28%) |
| ≥6 | High (74%) |

**Note:** The HR categories are mutually exclusive (1 point for 75–94, OR 2 points for ≥95; not additive). The maximum is 1+1+1+1+1+1+1+2+1 = **10**, not 12.

| Localized tenderness along the deep venous system | 1 |
| Entire leg swollen | 1 |
| Calf swelling ≥3 cm compared with asymptomatic leg (measured 10 cm below tibial tuberosity) | 1 |
| Pitting edema (greater in the symptomatic leg) | 1 |
| Collateral superficial veins (non-varicose) | 1 |
| Previously documented DVT | 1 |
| Alternative diagnosis at least as likely as DVT | −2 |

**Total range: −2 to +8**

**Two-tier interpretation (recommended):**
| Score | Category | Prevalence of DVT |
|---|---|---|
| ≤1 | DVT unlikely | ~5% |
| ≥2 | DVT likely | ~17–53% |

**Three-tier interpretation:**
| Score | Probability |
|---|---|
| ≤0 | Low (~5%) |
| 1–2 | Moderate (~17%) |
| ≥3 | High (~53%) |

**The Excel's ">2?" for the 2-tier threshold is wrong — the cutoff is ≥2.**

### Row 135 — Base Excess (Bedside Calculations)

**Corrected information:** Base excess is **not calculable by a simple bedside formula**. It is computed internally by blood gas analyzers using the **Siggaard-Anderson equation**:

```
SBE = (0.0277 × PaCO2 × 10^(pH − 6.1)) + (13.77 × (pH − 6.1)) + ...
(full equation: Siggard-Anderson alignment nomogram / Van Slyke equation)
```

The most commonly taught clinical approximation for **standard base excess (SBE)**:

```
SBE ≈ HCO3 − 24 + (2.4 × [7.40 − pH]) ... (rough approximation only)
```

Or for estimated base deficit:

```
Estimated base deficit ≈ 0.9 × (HCO3 − 24) + 14 (very rough, varies with PCO2)
```

**Practical interpretation:**

| Base Excess | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| +2 to −2 | Normal |
| −2 to −5 | Mild metabolic acidosis |
| −5 to −10 | Moderate |
| <−10 | Severe metabolic acidosis |
| >+2 | Metabolic alkalosis |

**Implementation note:** Consider implementing as a display field that accepts the value reported by the blood gas analyzer, rather than calculating it. If a formula is required, the Stewart (strong ion) approach or the anion gap method may be more clinically useful alternatives.

### Row 200 — Apgar Score (Obstetrics/Neonatology)

**Corrected formula:** Apgar Score (Apgar V, *Anesth Analg* 1953):

| Component | 0 Points | 1 Point | 2 Points |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A**ppearance (skin color) | Blue or pale all over | Body pink, extremities blue | Completely pink |
| **P**ulse (heart rate) | Absent | <100 bpm | ≥100 bpm |

|---|---|
| 7–10 | Normal (reassuring) |
| 4–6 | Moderately depressed |
| 0–3 | Severely depressed (requires immediate resuscitation) |

If the 5-minute score is <7, continue assessing every 5 minutes up to 20 minutes.

### Row 203 — CAPRA Score (Oncology / Urology)

**Corrected formula:** Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment (Cooperberg MR et al., *Cancer* 2005):

| Variable | 0 Points | 1 Point | 2 Points | 3 Points | 4 Points | 6 Points |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PSA (ng/mL) | 2.0–6.0 | 6.1–10.0 | 10.1–20.0 | 20.1–30.0 | >30.0 | — |
| Gleason primary pattern | No pattern 4 or 5 | — | — | Primary pattern 4 or 5 | — | — |
| T-stage | T1–T2a | T2b–T2c | T3 | — | — | — |
| % positive biopsy cores | ≤34% | 34–50% | >50% | — | — | — |
| Age at diagnosis | ≥50 | <50 | — | — | — | — |

**Total: 0–12**

| Risk Category | Score | 10-year Metastasis-Free Survival |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 0–2 | ~96% |
| Intermediate | 3–5 | ~80–90% |
| High | 6+ | ~50–65% |

**Note on Gleason scoring in CAPRA:** Assigns 0 points if neither the primary nor secondary Gleason pattern is 4 or 5 (i.e., Gleason ≤3+3). Assigns **3 points** if the primary pattern is 4 or 5 (i.e., Gleason 4+3 or higher). A secondary pattern of 4 or 5 without primary 4/5 also scores differently — verify against the published paper for exact implementation.

### Row 250 — SCAP Score (Respiratory)

**Corrected formula:** Severe CAP Score (España PP et al., *Chest* 2003):

**Major criteria (each = present/absent):**
| Criterion | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Arterial pH | <7.30 |
| Systolic BP | <90 mmHg requiring fluid resuscitation |

**Minor criteria (each = present/absent):**
| Criterion | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Respiratory rate | ≥30/min |
| Confusion | New-onset |
| BUN | ≥30 mg/dL (>10.7 mmol/L) |
| Multilobar/bilateral infiltrates | On chest radiograph |
| PaO₂ | <54 mmHg (or PaO₂/FiO₂ <250) |
| SpO₂ | <90% |
| Age | ≥80 years |
| Pleural effusion | Present |

**Classification:**
- **≥1 major criterion** → severe CAP
- **≥2 minor criteria** → severe CAP

The Excel's listing of "RR>=30, confusion, BUN>30, shock" as major criteria is incorrect — these are **minor** criteria (except shock/SBP <90, which IS a major criterion). The two major criteria are **pH <7.30** and **SBP <90**.

### Row 262 — SORT Score (Surgery/Perioperative)

**Corrected formula:** Surgical Outcome Risk Tool (Wong DJN et al., *Br J Anaesth* 2016):

| Variable | Categories | Points |
|---|---|---|
| Age (years) | <40 / 40–49 / 50–59 / 60–69 / 70–79 / 80+ | 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 |
| ASA physical status | I / II / III / IV / V | 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 |
| Priority | Elective / Expedited / Urgent / Immediate | 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 |
| Surgical severity (specialty) | Low / Medium / High | 0 / 1 / 2 |
| Cancer | No / Yes | 0 / 1 |

**Total range: 0–15**

```
Mortality = e^(logit) / (1 + e^(logit))

Where logit = −7.3817 + (0.0849 × age_points) + (0.5675 × ASA) 
            + (0.8741 × priority) + (0.5332 × severity) + (0.2214 × cancer)
```

**Note:** This is a logistic regression model. Implementation should compute the probability from the logit.

### Row 171 — ELF Test (GI/Hepatology)

**Corrected formula:** Enhanced Liver Fibrosis test (Rosenberg WM et al., *Gastroenterology* 2004):

```
ELF score = −7.412 + (0.681 × ln(HA)) + (0.775 × ln(PIIINP)) + (0.494 × ln(TIMP-1))

Where:
  HA = Hyaluronic acid (ng/mL)
  PIIINP = Procollagen III aminoterminal peptide (μg/mL)
  TIMP-1 = Tissue inhibitor of metalloproteinase-1 (ng/mL)
```

| ELF Score | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| <7.7 | No or mild fibrosis (F0–F1) |
| 7.7–9.8 | Moderate fibrosis (F2) |
| 9.8–11.3 | Severe fibrosis (F3) |
| ≥11.3 | Cirrhosis (F4) |

Common clinical threshold: **≥9.8 = advanced fibrosis (F3–F4)**

## SECTION C — HARD-BLOCKED ITEMS (partial corrections where possible)

For the following items, the Excel is flagged as "HARD-BLOCKED" because external calculators or published model coefficients are required. I provide the best available information:

---

### Row 16 — EuroSCORE II (Cardiovascular)

**Status:** Logistic regression model requiring 14+ variables with specific coefficients. Cannot be reduced to a simple additive formula.

**Variables:** Age, sex, renal impairment (creatinine clearance categories), extracardiac arteriopathy, poor mobility, neurological dysfunction, previous cardiac surgery, NYHA class, CCS class 4 angina, recent MI, pulmonary hypertension, active endocarditis, critical preoperative state, diabetes on insulin, LV function, recent intervention, weight of procedure

**Logistic equation:**
```
Predicted mortality = e^β / (1 + e^β)

β = −5.324537 + Σ(variable-specific coefficients × variable values)
```

**Coefficient table is available at euroscore.org.** The exact coefficients for each variable level are published in Nashef SA et al., *Eur J Cardiothorac Surg* (2012). Implementation requires the full coefficient table (approximately 30 numeric values).

---

### Row 23 — QRISK3 (Cardiovascular)

**Status:** Cox proportional hazards model with 17+ variables and interaction terms. Published coefficients available in Hippisley-Cox J et al., *BMJ* (2017). Implementation requires the full published coefficient table or the QRISK3 online calculator (qrisk.org).

---

### Row 26 — STS Risk Score (Cardiovascular)

**Status:** Multivariable logistic regression. Published model coefficients are available through the STS website (sts.org) and in O'Brien SM et al., *Ann Thorac Surg* (2009). Implementation requires the full coefficient table specific to procedure type.

---

### Row 143 — GARFIELD-AF (Cardiovascular)

**Status:** Weighted prediction model for AF outcomes. Fox KAA et al., *BMJ* (2017). Requires specific model coefficients. Implementation should use the GARFIELD-AF risk calculator.

---

### Row 275 — Reynolds Risk Score (Cardiovascular)

**Status:** Cox regression model. Published coefficients available in Ridker PM et al., *JAMA* (2007/2008). Key additional variables beyond standard ASCVD: hs-CRP, family history of premature CVD.

---

### Row 153 — APACHE IV (Critical Care)

**Status:** 24-variable model mapping to a 0–286 severity score with a logistic equation for mortality prediction. Published in Zimmerman JE et al., *Crit Care Med* (2006). Coefficients available in the published paper. APACHE III/IV calculators are available online.

---

### Row 156 — OASIS (Critical Care)

**Status:** Outcome and Assessment Information Set. Weighted 0–48 model. Johnson AE et al., *J Am Med Inform Assoc* (2013). Logistic regression coefficients available in the published paper.

---

### Row 157 — Phoenix Criteria (Critical Care — Pediatric Sepsis)

**Status:** Age-adjusted organ dysfunction criteria for pediatric sepsis. Schlapbach LJ et al., *JAMA* (2024). Specific age-adjusted thresholds for cardiovascular, respiratory, coagulation, and neurologic dysfunction are published in the reference paper.

### Row 170 — CLIF-C ACLF (GI/Hepatology)

**Status:** CLIF-C Organ Failure score component requires specific variable weights. Jalan R et al., *J Hepatol* (2014). The CLIF-OF subscores for 6 organ systems (liver, kidney, brain, coagulation, circulation, respiratory) each have specific published thresholds and weights.

**Status:** Cancer of the Liver Italian Program. Requires TNM mapping table. A new CLIP score should use:
- Child-Pugh (A=0, B=1, C=2)
- Tumor morphology (uninodular ≤50%=0, multinodular ≤50%=1, massive >50% or multifocal=2)
- AFP (<400=0, ≥400=1)
- Portal vein thrombosis (no=0, yes=1)

**Total: 0–6**

| >18 | Severe withdrawal | Frequent scheduled benzodiazepines; consider ICU |

| GI upset | 0–5 |

| Yawning | 0–4 |
| Anxiety or irritability | 0–4 |
| Gooseflesh skin | 0–5 |

**Total: 0–48**

| Score | Severity |
|---|---|
| 5–12 | Mild |
| 13–24 | Moderate |
| 25–36 | Moderately severe |
| ≥37 | Severe withdrawal |

### Row 164 — PERC / YEARS (Emergency/Respiratory)

**Status:** Both are addressable without external calculators.

**PERC Rule (Kline JA et al., *J Thromb Haemost* 2004):**
All 8 criteria must be NEGATIVE to exclude PE:
1. Age <50
2. HR <100
3. SpO₂ >94% on room air
4. No hemoptysis
5. No estrogen use
6. No prior DVT/PE
7. No unilateral leg swelling
8. No surgery/trauma within 4 weeks

If all 8 negative → PE effectively excluded (failure rate <2%)

**YEARS Algorithm (van der Hulle T et al., *Lancet* 2017):**

| YEARS Criteria | Present? |
|---|---|
| Clinical signs of DVT | Y/N |
| Hemoptysis | Y/N |
| PE is most likely diagnosis | Y/N |

| YEARS items present | D-dimer threshold | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 0 of 3 | <1000 ng/mL → PE excluded | If ≥1000 → CTPA |
| ≥1 of 3 | <500 ng/mL → PE excluded | If ≥500 → CTPA |

### Row 279 — LODS (Critical Care)

**Corrected formula:** Logistic Organ Dysfunction System (Le Gall JR et al., *JAMA* 1996):

| Organ System | Criterion | Points |
|---|---|---|
| **Neurologic:** | GCS 14–13 | 1 |
| | GCS 10–12 | 5 |
| | GCS 6–9 | 7 |
| | GCS <6 | 13 |
| **Cardiovascular:** | SBP 150+ or HR 110+ | 1 |
| | SBP 70–99 or HR ≤40 | 5 |
| | SBP 40–69 | 7 |
| | SBP <40 | 11 |
| | Mechanical ventilation | 3 |
| **Renal:** | Urea 5–10 mmol/L | 1 |
| | Urea >10 mmol/L | 7 |
| **Hepatic:** | Bilirubin 60–120 μmol/L | 4 |
| | Bilirubin >120 μmol/L | 10 |
| **Hematologic:** | WBC 1–2.5 or >12 (×10⁹/L) | 1 |
| | Platelets 50–100 (×10⁹/L) | 2 |
| | WBC <1 or platelets <50 | 12 |
| **Respiratory:** | PaO₂ 60–90 (SpO₂ 90–95%) | 3 |
| | PaO₂ 40–60 (SpO₂ 85–90%) | 7 |

**Total range: 0–22** (only one criterion selected per organ system)

| LODS Score | Predicted Hospital Mortality |
|---|---|
| 0 | ~1% |
| 1–5 | ~5–10% |
| 6–10 | ~15–30% |
| 11–15 | ~40–60% |
| ≥16 | ~70%+ |

### Row 280 — MPM-II / MPM-III (Critical Care)

**Status:** Logistic regression models with published coefficients.

**MPM-II₀ (at ICU admission):** 15 variables, logistic equation:
```
logit = β₀ + Σ(βᵢ × xᵢ)
Mortality = e^logit / (1 + e^logit)
```

Variables and coefficients published in Lemeshow S et al., *JAMA* (1993) for MPM-II and in Higgins TL et al., *Crit Care Med* (2007) for MPM-III. Implementation requires the full coefficient tables (approximately 15–20 coefficients each).

**MPM-II₀ variables (15):** Age, SBP, HR, GCS, previous or current cancer, acute renal failure, cardiac dysrhythmia, cerebral hemorrhage/intoxication, chronic renal failure, hepatic cirrhosis, intracranial mass, mechanical ventilation, infection at ICU admission, PaO₂/FiO₂ ratio, urgent/unplanned admission

## SECTION D — EXISTING DEVIATIONS (no changes needed per document)

These are documented pre-existing deviations in the app code that the document confirms should NOT be changed:

1. **Lille Score:** Excel coefficients saturate the logistic curve; existing code uses published weights with inverted bilirubin delta sign + extra term. No change.

2. **Pediatric Appendicitis Score (PAS):** Existing code hardcodes max=8; Excel lists 0–10. No change.

3. **CDAI (Crohn's):** Existing code includes extraintestinal complications ×20 term; Excel formula omits it. No change.

```json
{
 "name": "Braunwald Classification of Unstable Angina",
 "acronym": "Braunwald",
 "subcategory": "acute coronary syndromes",
 "purpose": "Classifies unstable angina by severity, clinical circumstance, and intensity of treatment to guide prognosis and management.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Severity class",
   "description": "Clinical severity of angina presentation",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "I = new-onset or worsening angina; II = angina at rest within past month but not 48 hours; III = angina at rest within 48 hours",
   "points_or_coefficient": "classification only"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Clinical circumstance",
   "description": "Context in which unstable angina occurs",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "A = secondary (extracardiac provocation); B = primary (no extracardiac provocation); C = within 2 weeks of MI",
   "points_or_coefficient": "classification only"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Treatment intensity",
   "description": "Intensity of anti-ischemic therapy at time of angina",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "1 = no or minimal treatment; 2 = standard oral therapy; 3 = maximal IV anti-ischemic therapy",
   "points_or_coefficient": "classification only"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Categorical classification (e.g., IB = primary, new-onset/worsening angina on minimal therapy). Not a numerical score.",
 "score_range": "III-C is highest risk",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "III-C",
   "meaning": "Rest angina within 48 hours on maximal IV therapy in post-MI setting — highest risk subgroup"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "I-A",
   "meaning": "New-onset/worsening angina secondary to extracardiac cause — lowest risk"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with unstable angina from multiple clinical settings in the 1980s–1990s",
 "original_citation": "Braunwald E. Unstable angina. A classification. Circulation. 1989;80(2):410-414. PMID: 2502287",
 "additional_validation": "van Miltenburg-van Zijl AJ, et al. Circulation. 1990;82:suppl III-44; Cohen M, et al. Circulation. 1994;89:1545-1556",

}

#### E002 · Duke Treadmill Score (DTS)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L1902–L1925 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L1878, L1902) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Duke Treadmill Score",
 "acronym": "DTS",
 "subcategory": "acute coronary syndromes",
 "purpose": "Risk stratifies patients undergoing exercise stress testing for coronary artery disease severity and prognosis.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Exercise time",
   "description": "Duration of exercise on standard Bruce protocol",
   "unit": "minutes",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "×5 in formula"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Maximum ST-segment deviation",
   "description": "Maximum ST elevation or depression during exercise or recovery",
   "unit": "mm",
   "range_or_options": "0–10+ mm",
   "points_or_coefficient": "×4 (subtracted)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Angina index",
   "description": "Angina during test",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = no angina; 1 = non-limiting angina; 2 = exercise-limiting angina",
   "points_or_coefficient": "×1 (subtracted)"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "DTS = Exercise_time − (5 × ST_deviation) − (4 × Angina_index)",
 "score_range": "−25 to +15 (approximately)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "≥+5",
   "meaning": "Low risk: 4-year survival ~99%; annual mortality <0.5%"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "−10 to +4",
   "meaning": "Moderate risk: 4-year survival ~95%; annual mortality ~1%"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≤−11",
   "meaning": "High risk: 4-year survival ~79%; annual mortality ~5%"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients referred for coronary angiography at Duke University Medical Center",
 "original_citation": "Mark DB, Shaw L, Harrell FE Jr, et al. Prognostic value of a treadmill exercise score in outpatients with suspected coronary artery disease. N Engl J Med. 1991;325(12):849-853. PMID: 1875969",
 "additional_validation": "Mark DB, et al. N Engl J Med. 1998;339:1725-1732. PMID: 9845707; Alexander KP, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2007;49(18):1850-1856",
 "limitations": "Requires formal exercise testing (not applicable to patients who cannot exercise). Based on standard Bruce protocol; other protocols require conversion. Not validated with stress imaging modalities. Pre-dates routine use of coronary CTA.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",

 "name": "History, ECG, Age, Risk Factors, Troponin Score",

  },
  {

   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = normal; 1 = nonspecific repolarization disturbance; 2 = significant ST deviation",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Age",
   "description": "Patient age in years",
   "unit": "years",
   "range_or_options": "<45 = 0; 45–64 = 1; ≥65 = 2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Risk factors",
   "description": "Number of cardiovascular risk factors (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, DM, current/recent smoking, family history of premature CAD, obesity, sedentary lifestyle)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = no risk factors; 1 = 1–2 risk factors; 2 = ≥3 risk factors or history of atherosclerotic disease",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Troponin",
   "description": "Initial or serial troponin relative to local upper limit of normal (ULN)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = ≤ULN; 1 = 1–3× ULN; 2 = >3× ULN",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "HEART = History + ECG + Age + Risk_factors + Troponin",
 "score_range": "0–10",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–3",
   "meaning": "Low risk (~0.9–1.7% MACE at 6 weeks). Consider early discharge with outpatient follow-up."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4–6",
   "meaning": "Moderate risk (~12–16.6% MACE). Consider admission or observation with serial troponins and provocative testing."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "7–10",
   "meaning": "High risk (~50–65% MACE). Early invasive strategy recommended."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "ED patients ≥21 years with symptoms suggestive of ACS; validated in US, European, and Asian cohorts",
 "original_citation": "Backus BE, et al. A prospective validation of the HEART score for chest pain patients at the emergency department. Int J Cardiol. 2013;168(3):2153-2158. PMID: 23465248 (concept originally from Six AJ, et al. 2008)",

 "limitations": "Subjective components (History scoring varies by clinician). Validated primarily in ED populations; less studied in prehospital or primary care. Troponin assay-specific (high-sensitivity troponin may shift optimal cutoffs). Original validation used conventional troponin.",

   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",

  },
  {
   "variable": "Discordant ST elevation ≥5 mm",

   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "2"
  }
 ],

  {

 ],

 ],

Does not account for AF burden (paroxysmal vs persistent). Most beneficial for identifying truly low-risk patients who can safely avoid anticoagulation.",

  },

 "limitations": "Score ≥3 identifies high bleeding risk but should not be used alone to withhold anticoagulation (many high-CHA₂DS₂-VASc patients with HAS-BLED ≥3 still benefit from OAC). {
 "name": "Age, Creatinine, Ejection Fraction Score",

 "input_variables": [

   "variable": "Age",

   "unit": "%",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "+30 / LVEF"
  }
 ],

 "score_range": "approximately 1.0–6.0+",

   "score_range": "<1.2",

  {

   "meaning": "High risk (~4–10%+)"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery at San Raffaele Hospital, Milan",
 "original_citation": "Ranucci M, Castelvecchio S, Menicanti L, et al. Risk of assessing mortality risk in elective cardiac operations: age, creatinine, ejection fraction, and the law of parsimony. Circulation. 2009;119(24):3053-3061. PMID: 19506121",
 "additional_validation": "Ranucci M, et al. Ann Thorac Surg. 2012;94:108-113; Wyler von Ballmoos M, et al. Eur J Cardiothorac Surg. 2019",

 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"

  },
  {
   "variable": "Serum sodium",
   "description": "Serum sodium (mEq/L)",
   "unit": "mEq/L",
   "range_or_options": "120–150",
   "points_or_coefficient": "−0.0470 per mEq/L"
  },
  {
   "variable": "QRS duration",
   "description": "QRS duration on ECG (ms)",
   "unit": "ms",
   "range_or_options": "60–200+",
   "points_or_coefficient": "+0.0074 per ms"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "HFSS = Ischemic_cause(0.6931) + HR(0.0216 × bpm) + LVEF(−0.0464 × %) + MAP(−0.0255 × mmHg) + Peak_VO2(−0.0546 × mL/kg/min) + Sodium(−0.0470 × mEq/L) + QRS(0.0074 × ms). Then: Risk score = exp(HFSS); 1-year survival = S₀^risk_score where S₀ is the baseline survival constant.",
 "score_range": "Continuous; risk score typically 0–15+",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<8.10",
   "meaning": "Low risk: 1-year survival >90% (transplant can be deferred)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "8.10–11.4",
   "meaning": "Medium risk: 1-year survival 70–90% (consider transplant listing)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": ">11.4",
   "meaning": "High risk: 1-year survival <70% (urgent transplant evaluation)"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with chronic HF referred for transplant evaluation at University of Washington",
 "original_citation": "Aaronson KD, Schwartz JS, Chen TM, et al. Development and prospective validation of a clinical index to predict survival in ambulatory patients referred for cardiac transplant evaluation. Circulation. 1997;95(12):2660-2667. PMID: 9193435",
 "additional_validation": "Lund LH, et al. J Heart Lung Transplant. 2012;31:451-458; Koelling TM, et al. J Heart Lung Transplant. 2003",
 "limitations": "Requires cardiopulmonary exercise testing (peak VO₂) — not available in all settings. Derived from single-center transplant referral population. Not validated in HFpEF. BNP/NT-proBNP not included.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}

### ICU sedation / delirium

#### E036 · Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU (CAM-ICU)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L4371–L4394 · parse: clean · 3 copies merged (src L4347, L4371, L5627) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU",
 "acronym": "CAM-ICU",
 "subcategory": "ICU sedation / delirium",
 "purpose": "Validated bedside tool to diagnose delirium in critically ill, intubated and non-intubated ICU patients.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Feature 1: Acute onset or fluctuating course",
   "description": "Is there an acute change in mental status from baseline, or does mental status fluctuate during the past 24 hours?",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "required (Feature 1 + Feature 2 required)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Feature 2: Inattention",
   "description": "ASES letter recognition test: patient squeezes hand on letter 'A' when letters read. Inattention = <8 correct out of 10.",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0–10 correct; <8 = inattention positive",
   "points_or_coefficient": "positive if <8 correct"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Feature 3: Altered level of consciousness",
   "description": "RASS ≠ 0 (anything other than alert and calm)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "RASS ≠ 0 = altered LOC",
   "points_or_coefficient": "positive if RASS ≠ 0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Feature 4: Disorganized thinking",
   "description": "Yes/no questions and command test (e.g., 'hold up this many fingers' + 'do the same thing with the other hand'). Score 0–4, positive if <4 correct.",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0–4 correct; <4 = disorganized thinking positive",
   "points_or_coefficient": "positive if <4 correct"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CAM-ICU positive (delirium present) if ALL of:\n1. Feature 1 (acute onset/fluctuation) is present\nAND\n2. Feature 2 (inattention) is present\nAND\n3. Either Feature 3 (altered LOC) OR Feature 4 (disorganized thinking) is present\n\nIf RASS = −4 or −5, CAM-ICU cannot be assessed (patient is unarousable).",
 "score_range": "Positive or Negative",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Positive",
   "meaning": "Delirium present. Associated with increased mortality, prolonged ICU stay, and long-term cognitive impairment."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Negative",
   "meaning": "Delirium not detected. May not be assessable if RASS ≤ −4."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Adult ICU patients (mechanically ventilated and non-ventilated)",
 "original_citation": "Ely EW, Inouye SK, Bernard GR, et al. Delirium in mechanically ventilated patients: validity and reliability of the confusion assessment method for the intensive care unit (CAM-ICU). JAMA. 2001;286(21):2703-2710. PMID: 11730446",
 "additional_validation": "Ely EW, et al. JAMA. 2004;291(14):1753-1762 (ICU delirium and outcomes); Gusmao-Flores D, et al. Crit Care Med. 2012;40:1929-1935",
 "limitations": "Cannot be assessed in deeply sedated patients (RASS ≤ −4). ASES letter test requires hearing/vision. May be difficult in patients with pre-existing dementia. False negatives possible with fluctuating delirium. Requires training for consistent administration.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use, check for commercial app — training materials at icudelirium.org",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

   "description": "Patient's level of alertness and response to voice and physical stimulation",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "+4 to −5 scale",
   "points_or_coefficient": "see scoring below"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "RASS scale:\n+4 = Combative (overtly combative, violent, immediate danger to staff)\n+3 = Very agitated (pulls/removes tubes/catheters, aggressive)\n+2 = Agitated (frequent non-purposeful movement, fights ventilator)\n+1 = Restless (anxious, apprehensive, movements not aggressive)\n0 = Alert and calm\n−1 = Drowsy (not fully alert but has sustained awakening to voice, eye contact ≥10 sec)\n−2 = Light sedation (briefly awakens to voice, eye contact <10 sec)\n−3 = Moderate sedation (movement or eye opening to voice, no eye contact)\n−4 = Deep sedation (no response to voice, movement or eye opening to physical stimulation)\n−5 = Unarousable (no response to voice or physical stimulation)",
 "score_range": "−5 to +4",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "+4 to +1",
   "meaning": "Agitated; may need sedating medication"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "Target sedation level for most ICU patients (PADIS guidelines)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "−1 to −2",
   "meaning": "Light sedation; appropriate for many mechanically ventilated patients"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "−3 to −5",
   "meaning": "Moderate to deep sedation; reassess need (associated with worse outcomes)"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Intubated and mechanically ventilated adult ICU patients",
 "original_citation": "Sessler CN, Gosnell MS, Grap MJ, et al. The Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale: validity and reliability in adult intensive care unit patients. Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002;166(10):1338-1344. PMID: 12421743",
 "additional_validation": "Ely EW, et al. JAMA. 2003;289(22):2983-2991 (used in CAM-ICU validation); Barr J, et al. Crit Care Med. 2018 (PADIS guidelines)",
 "limitations": "Cannot be used in patients receiving paralytic agents. Sedation assessment may be confounded by neurological injury. Requires patient interaction. Deeply sedated patients (−4, −5) are scored identically.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}

<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L3940–L3966 · parse: clean · 3 copies merged (src L3913, L3940, L5413) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Logistic Organ Dysfunction System",
 "acronym": "LODS",
 "subcategory": "ICU severity of illness",
 "purpose": "Quantifies severity of organ dysfunction in ICU patients with a logistic model calibrated for hospital mortality prediction.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Neurological",
   "description": "GCS",
   "unit": "score",
   "range_or_options": "GCS 3–4=5; 5–7=3; 8–10=2; 11–13=1; 14–15=0",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Cardiovascular",
   "description": "Heart rate, SBP, cardiac arrest",
   "unit": "mixed",
   "range_or_options": "Various combinations scored 0–5",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Renal",
   "description": "Urea and urine output",
   "unit": "mixed",
   "range_or_options": "Various",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Pulmonary",
   "description": "PaO₂/FiO₂ and mechanical ventilation",
   "unit": "mixed",
   "range_or_options": "Various",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hematologic",
   "description": "WBC and platelets",
   "unit": "mixed",
   "range_or_options": "Various",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hepatic",
   "description": "Bilirubin and prothrombin time",
   "unit": "mixed",
   "range_or_options": "Various",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–5"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "LODS = Sum of organ-specific scores (0–5 per organ, 6 organs). Logistic model: logit = −5.7865 + 0.1374 × LODS + diagnostic category coefficients. Predicted mortality = e^logit / (1 + e^logit).",
 "score_range": "0–22",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–5",
   "meaning": "Low predicted hospital mortality"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "6–12",
   "meaning": "Moderate mortality"
  },
  {
   "score_range": ">12",
   "meaning": "High predicted mortality"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "13,152 patients from 137 ICUs (same cohort as SAPS II)",
 "original_citation": "Le Gall JR, Klar J, Lemeshow S, et al. The Logistic Organ Dysfunction system: a new way to assess organ dysfunction in the intensive care unit. JAMA. 1996;276(10):802-810. PMID: 8769590",
 "additional_validation": "Peres Bota D, et al. Crit Care Med. 2003;31:2609-2614",

Predicted mortality = 1/(1 + e^(-logit)).",

  {

  }
 ],

 "formula": "Alvarado = Migration(1) + Anorexia(1) + Nausea(1) + RLQ_tenderness(2) + Rebound(1) + Temperature(1) + Leukocytosis(2) + Left_shift(1). Acronym: MANTRELS",
 "score_range": "0–10",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–4",
   "meaning": "Low probability of appendicitis (~1–5%). Consider discharge with follow-up."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5–6",
   "meaning": "Moderate probability (~15–30%). Observe, imaging (CT/US), or surgical consult."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "7–10",
   "meaning": "High probability (~70–95%). Strongly consider surgical consultation or appendectomy."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with suspected appendicitis in emergency departments worldwide",
 "original_citation": "Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Ann Emerg Med. 1986;15(5):557-564. PMID: 3963537",
 "additional_validation": "Ohle R, et al. Acad Emerg Med. 2011;18:1235-1242 (meta-analysis); McKay R, Shepherd J. J Emerg Med. 2011;41:551-558",
 "limitations": "Less accurate in women of reproductive age, children, and elderly. CT scan has largely replaced clinical scoring in many settings. Does not account for imaging findings. Inter-rater variability on rebound tenderness. Performance varies by population and prevalence.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}

  }
 ],

 "limitations": "Low sensitivity (~60-80%) — a low LRINEC score should NOT exclude necrotizing fasciitis if clinical suspicion is high. CRP may not be elevated early in disease. Not validated in all populations. Should supplement, not replace, clinical judgment and surgical evaluation.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "medium"
}
```

#### E063 · Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network Head CT Decision Rule (PECARN TBI Rule)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L6521–L6552 · parse: clean -->

{
 "name": "Pediatric Emergency Care Applied Research Network Head CT Decision Rule",

 "purpose": "Identifies children at very low risk of clinically important traumatic brain injury (ciTBI) who do not require CT head imaging.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Age group",
