```json
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "<2 / ≥2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "separate decision pathways"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(For <2 years): GCS <15",
   "description": "Altered mental status",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "high-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(<2): Altered behavior per parent",
   "description": "Perception of parent that child's behavior is abnormal",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "high-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(<2): Palpable skull fracture",
   "description": "Physical exam finding",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "high-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(<2): Scalp hematoma (frontal/parietal/temporal/occipital)",
   "description": "Location and size of hematoma",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "higher-risk criterion (especially non-frontal, large)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(<2): Occipital/parietal/temporal scalp hematoma or large hematoma",
   "description": "High-risk hematoma features",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "high-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(≥2 years): GCS <15",
   "description": "Altered mental status",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "high-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(≥2): Signs of basilar skull fracture",
   "description": "Hemotympanum, CSF otorrhea/rhinorrhea, periorbital ecchymosis, post-auricular ecchymosis (Battle sign)",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "high-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(≥2): History of vomiting",
   "description": "≥2 episodes of vomiting after injury",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "higher-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(≥2): Severe headache",
   "description": "Severe or worsening headache",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "higher-risk criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "(Both): Dangerous mechanism of injury",
   "description": "Motor vehicle crash, fall from elevation >3 feet (or >5 feet for older children), struck by high-impact object, bicycle crash with no helmet",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "higher-risk criterion"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Decision algorithm:\nHIGH-RISK (any → CT recommended): GCS <15, palpable skull fracture, signs of basilar skull fracture, altered behavior/mental status\n\nHIGHER-RISK (observation vs CT based on clinical judgment): scalp hematoma, vomiting ≥2, severe headache, dangerous mechanism\n\nIf NO high-risk or higher-risk features → observation safe (no CT needed).\nSensitivity for ciTBI: 98–100%.",
 "score_range": "Binary (CT recommended / observation safe)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "No high-risk or higher-risk features",
   "meaning": "<0.1% risk of ciTBI. Observation and no CT."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Higher-risk features only",
   "meaning": "0.5–4% risk. Clinical judgment for CT vs observation."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "High-risk features present",
   "meaning": "CT head recommended. Higher risk of ciTBI and neurosurgical intervention."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "42,412 children with GCS 14–15 presenting to 25 PECARN EDs in the US",
 "original_citation": "Kuppermann N, Holmes JF, Dayan PS, et al. Identification of children at very low risk of clinically-important brain injuries after head trauma: a prospective cohort study. Lancet. 2009;374(9696):1160-1170. PMID: 19758692",
 "additional_validation": "Schonfeld D, et al. Ann Emerg Med. 2014;63:460-468; Easter JS, et al. Acad Emerg Med. 2015;22:940-946",
 "limitations": "Validated in children with GCS 14–15 (minor head trauma only). Parents may under/over-report symptoms. Clinical judgment still required for higher-risk group. External validation in non-US settings limited. CT avoidance must be balanced against missed ciTBI risk.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
{
 "name": "Revised Geneva Score",

   "points_or_coefficient": "2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Active malignancy",
   "description": "Active or recently treated cancer",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Unilateral lower-limb pain",

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hemoptysis",
   "description": "Hemoptysis",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Heart rate 75–94 bpm",
   "description": "Tachycardia (moderate)",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Heart rate ≥95 bpm",

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "5"

   "variable": "Pain on lower limb deep vein palpation and unilateral edema",
   "description": "Clinical signs of DVT",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "4"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Revised Geneva = Age>65(1) + Prior_VTE(3) + Surgery_fracture(2) + Active_cancer(2) + Unilateral_leg_pain(3) + Hemoptysis(2) + HR_75-94(3) + HR_≥95(5) + Clinical_DVT_signs(4)",
 "score_range": "0–25",
 "interpretation": [

  },

   "meaning": "Intermediate probability (~23%). D-dimer or imaging."

  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Emergency department patients with suspected PE at Geneva University Hospital",
 "original_citation": "Le Gal G, Righini M, Roy PM, et al. Prediction of pulmonary embolism in the emergency department: the revised Geneva score. Ann Intern Med. 2006;144(3):165-171. PMID: 16461960",
 "additional_validation": "Klok FA, et al. J Thromb Haemost. 2008;6:772-774; Penaloza A, et al. Thromb Haemost. 2012;108:1172-1177",
 "limitations": "Fully objective (advantage over Wells) but slightly lower discrimination than Wells with gestalt. Complex point system (non-integer values). Derived in European academic centers. D-dimer threshold may vary by age (age-adjusted D-dimer now recommended).",
```

#### E068 · YEARS Algorithm (YEARS)

```json
{
 "name": "YEARS Algorithm",
 "acronym": "YEARS",
 "subcategory": "pulmonary embolism",
 "purpose": "Stepwise diagnostic algorithm for PE combining Wells-like items with D-dimer thresholds to reduce unnecessary imaging.",
 "input_variables": [
  {

   "points_or_coefficient": "1 item"
  },

   "variable": "PE most likely diagnosis",

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 item"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "YEARS items = DVT signs + Hemoptysis + PE most likely.\n\nStep 1: Count YEARS items (0, 1, 2, or 3 positive).\nStep 2: If 0 YEARS items → PE excluded if D-dimer <1000 ng/L.\nIf 1–3 YEARS items → PE excluded if D-dimer <500 ng/L.\nIf D-dimer above threshold → proceed to CTPA.",

   "score_range": "0 items + D-dimer <1000",

  },
  {
   "score_range": "D-dimer above threshold",

  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "ED patients with suspected PE in 12 hospitals in the Netherlands",

 "limitations": "Higher D-dimer threshold (1000 ng/L) may cause concern for missing PE — absolute miss rate ~0.5%. Validated primarily in the Netherlands — external validation needed. Subjective 'PE most likely' item. Not applicable to pregnant patients. CTPA rate reduction ~14% vs conventional approaches.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
```

#### E079 · GOLD 2024 Classification (ABCD) (GOLD ABCD)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L7715–L7738 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "GOLD 2024 Classification (ABCD)",
 "acronym": "GOLD ABCD",
 "subcategory": "COPD",
 "purpose": "Groups COPD patients by symptom burden and exacerbation history to guide initial pharmacotherapy per Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "FEV1 % predicted (spirometric severity)",
   "description": "Post-bronchodilator FEV1 as percent predicted",
   "unit": "%",
   "range_or_options": "GOLD 1: ≥80%; GOLD 2: 50–79%; GOLD 3: 30–49%; GOLD 4: <30%",
   "points_or_coefficient": "used in old ABCD; now primarily for spirometric grade only in GOLD 2024"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Exacerbation history",
   "description": "Number of moderate-to-severe exacerbations in past year",
   "unit": "count/year",
   "range_or_options": "0 / 1 / ≥2 (or ≥1 requiring hospitalization)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "categorizes into A/B/E groups"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Symptom burden",
   "description": "CAT score or mMRC dyspnea score",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "CAT <10 or mMRC 0–1 = less symptoms; CAT ≥10 or mMRC ≥2 = more symptoms",
   "points_or_coefficient": "categorizes into A/B or E groups"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "2024 GOLD Groups:\nGroup A: 0–1 exacerbation/year (none hospitalized) + low symptoms (CAT <10 or mMRC 0–1)\nGroup B: 0–1 exacerbation/year (none hospitalized) + high symptoms (CAT ≥10 or mMRC ≥2)\nGroup E (Elevated risk): ≥2 exacerbations/year OR ≥1 hospitalized + either symptom level\nNote: GOLD 2024 simplified from ABCD to ABE grouping.",
 "score_range": "Group A / B / E",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "A",
   "meaning": "Low risk, low symptoms. Bronchodilator (SABA/SAMA or LABA or LAMA)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "B",
   "meaning": "Low risk, high symptoms. LABA + LAMA."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "E",
   "meaning": "High exacerbation risk. LABA + LAMA; consider LABA + LAMA + ICS if eosinophils ≥300."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Global expert consensus (GOLD Science Committee); based on evidence from multiple RCTs and observational cohorts",
 "original_citation": "Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD). Global Strategy for Prevention, Diagnosis and Management of COPD: 2024 Report. Available at goldcopd.org",
 "additional_validation": "Updated annually; see goldcopd.org for latest evidence summary",
 "limitations": "Classification scheme rather than a validated scoring system. Cutoffs are somewhat arbitrary. Does not capture frailty, comorbidities, or biomarkers (blood eosinophils now incorporated separately for ICS decisions). 2024 update changed from ABCD to ABE (confusing for those familiar with older versions).",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use, check for commercial app — GOLD guidelines available at goldcopd.org",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

### COPD / exacerbation

#### E080 · DECAF Score (DECAF)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L4891–L4916 · parse: clean · 3 copies merged (src L4865, L4891, L9810) · merged naming variants: DECAF Score for Acute COPD Exacerbation -->
```json
{
 "name": "DECAF Score",
 "acronym": "DECAF",
 "subcategory": "COPD / exacerbation",
 "purpose": "Predicts in-hospital mortality in acute exacerbations of COPD using five readily available clinical variables.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Dyspnea (eMRCD 5a or 5b)",
   "description": "Extended MRC Dyspnea scale: 5a = dyspnea after washing/dressing; 5b = housebound due to breathlessness",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "eMRCD 1–4=0; 5a=1; 5b=2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Eosinopenia (<0.05 × 10⁹/L)",
   "description": "Blood eosinophil count <50 cells/µL",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Consolidation",
   "description": "Radiographic consolidation on CXR",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Acidemia (pH <7.30)",
   "description": "Arterial pH <7.30",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "atrial Fibrillation",
   "description": "AF on ECG or known AF",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "DECAF = Dyspnea(0-2) + Eosinopenia(1) + Consolidation(1) + Acidemia(1) + atrial_Fibrillation(1)",
 "score_range": "0–6",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–1",
   "meaning": "Low risk of in-hospital death (~1%). Consider ward-level care."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "2",
   "meaning": "Moderate risk (~4%). Consider closer monitoring."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3–6",
   "meaning": "High risk (~10–50%). Consider HDU/ICU, palliative care discussion."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients hospitalized with acute exacerbation of COPD in UK",
 "original_citation": "Steer J, Gibson J, Bourke SC. The DECAF Score: predicting hospital mortality in exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Thorax. 2012;67(11):970-976. PMID: 22863759",
 "additional_validation": "Echevarria C, et al. Thorax. 2016;71(2):97-105 (validation); Mekov E, et al. COPD. 2019",
 "limitations": "Validated primarily in UK. Requires ABG. eMRCD 5a vs 5b may be difficult to assess acutely. Eosinopenia cutoff is laboratory-dependent. Not validated for non-COPD breathlessness.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

#### E081 · Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation Score (ISTH) (ISTH DIC Score)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L5842–L5865 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation Score (ISTH)",
 "acronym": "ISTH DIC Score",
 "subcategory": "critical care / coagulation",
 "purpose": "Diagnoses overt disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) using readily available coagulation parameters.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Platelet count",
   "description": "Platelet count (×10⁹/L)",
   "unit": "×10⁹/L",
   "range_or_options": ">100 = 0; <100 = 1; <50 = 2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Elevated fibrin marker (D-dimer or FDP)",
   "description": "D-dimer or fibrin degradation products",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "No increase = 0; moderate increase = 2; strong increase = 3",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Prolonged PT",
   "description": "PT seconds above normal (or INR)",
   "unit": "seconds",
   "range_or_options": "<3 seconds prolonged = 0; ≥3 but <6 = 1; ≥6 = 2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Fibrinogen",
   "description": "Serum fibrinogen level",
   "unit": "g/L",
   "range_or_options": ">1.0 g/L = 0; ≤1.0 g/L = 1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "ISTH DIC Score = Platelet(0–2) + Fibrin_marker(0–3) + PT_prolongation(0–2) + Fibrinogen(0–1). Total = 0–8.",
 "score_range": "0–8",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<5",
   "meaning": "Not consistent with overt DIC; repeat if clinically indicated"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥5",
   "meaning": "Compatible with overt DIC; initiate treatment"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with suspected DIC from multiple clinical settings (sepsis, trauma, malignancy, obstetric)",
 "original_citation": "Taylor FB Jr, Toh CH, Hoots WK, et al. Towards definition, clinical and laboratory criteria, and a scoring system for disseminated intravascular coagulation. Thromb Haemost. 2001;86(5):1327-1330. PMID: 11816725",
 "additional_validation": "Bakhtiari K, et al. Crit Care Med. 2004;32:2416-2421; Toh CH, et al. Thromb Haemost. 2005",
 "limitations": "Fibrinogen is an acute phase reactant and may be elevated despite DIC. D-dimer/FDP cutoffs vary by assay. Score designed for overt DIC — may miss early/chronic DIC. Does not capture clinical context. Multiple DIC scoring systems exist (ISTH, JMHW, JAAM).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",

   "unit": "mmol/L",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "coefficient"
  },

   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "coefficient"

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",

  },
  {
```

```json
   "description": "Age in years",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "≤44 = 0; 45–54 = 2; 55–64 = 3; 65–74 = 5; ≥75 = 6",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–6"
  },

   "variable": "Chronic Health Points",

  }

For general use: ln(R/(1−R)) = −3.517 + (APACHE_II × 0.146) + 0.603 (only if emergency surgery) + diagnostic category coefficient.",

 ],

  },
```

```json
   "variable": "Circumstances of ICU admission",

   "points_or_coefficient": "variable-specific points"
  }
 ],

  },

 ],
```

```json
 ],
 "formula": "Categorical classification:\n1 = Dead\n2 = Vegetative state\n3 = Lower severe disability (conscious but dependent on others for daily support)\n4 = Upper severe disability (independent at home but dependent outside)\n5 = Lower moderate disability (independent at home, limited outside; unable to return to work/school)\n6 = Upper moderate disability (independent at home and outside; reduced social/work participation)\n7 = Lower good recovery (resumption of normal life with minor neurological/psychological deficits)\n8 = Upper good recovery (fully recovered)",
 "score_range": "1–8",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "1–4",
   "meaning": "Unfavorable outcome (dead, vegetative, or severely disabled)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5–8",
   "meaning": "Favorable outcome (moderate disability to good recovery)"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "TBI patients; standard outcome measure in TBI research; validated in cardiac arrest and stroke",
 "original_citation": "Jennett B, Bond M. Assessment of outcome after severe brain damage: a practical scale. Lancet. 1975;305(7905):480-484. PMID: 46957 (original GOS); Wilson JTL, et al. J Neurotrauma. 1998;15:581-588 (extended version)",
 "additional_validation": "Wilson L, et al. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 2002;83:1201-1207; used in CRASH and IMPACT trials",
 "limitations": "Coarse scale even in extended form. Significant ceiling effect in mild TBI. Requires structured interview for reliable assessment. May not capture subtle cognitive deficits. Proxy-assessed versions may differ from self-report.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

### critical care / organ failure

#### E093 · Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score (MODS)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L5442–L5470 · parse: clean · 3 copies merged (src L3968, L3996, L5442) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Multiple Organ Dysfunction Score",

 "subcategory": "critical care / organ failure",

 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Respiratory: PaO₂/FiO₂",
   "description": "Oxygenation ratio",
   "unit": "mmHg",
   "range_or_options": "≥300 = 0; 225–299 = 1; 150–224 = 2; 75–149 = 3; <75 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Renal: Serum creatinine",
   "description": "Creatinine (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "<1.1 = 0; 1.1–2.3 = 1; 2.3–4.0 = 2; 4.0–5.7 = 3; >5.7 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hepatic: Bilirubin",
   "description": "Total bilirubin (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "<1.1 = 0; 1.1–2.3 = 1; 2.3–4.0 = 2; 4.0–5.7 = 3; >5.7 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Cardiovascular: Pressure-adjusted HR",
   "description": "PAR = HR × RAP / MAP",
   "unit": "bpm",
   "range_or_options": "<10 = 0; 10.1–15 = 1; 15.1–20 = 2; 20.1–30 = 3; >30 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hematologic: Platelets",
   "description": "Platelet count (×10³/µL)",
   "unit": "×10³/µL",
   "range_or_options": "≥120 = 0; 120–80 = 1; 80–51 = 2; 51–20 = 3; <20 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Neurologic: GCS",
   "description": "Glasgow Coma Scale",
   "unit": "score",
   "range_or_options": "15 = 0; 13–14 = 1; 10–12 = 2; 7–9 = 3; ≤6 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "MODS = Respiratory(0–4) + Renal(0–4) + Hepatic(0–4) + Cardiovascular(0–4) + Hematologic(0–4) + Neurologic(0–4). Total = 0–24.",
 "score_range": "0–24",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "No organ dysfunction"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1–4",
   "meaning": "Mild dysfunction"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5–9",
   "meaning": "Moderate dysfunction"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–14",
   "meaning": "Severe dysfunction"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥15",
   "meaning": "Critical multiorgan failure"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "ICU patients at a single center (original); validated in multiple ICU populations",
 "original_citation": "Marshall JC, Cook DJ, Christou NV, et al. Multiple organ dysfunction score: a reliable descriptor of a complex clinical outcome. Crit Care Med. 1995;23(10):1638-1652. PMID: 7587228",
 "additional_validation": "Peres B, et al. Intensive Care Med. 1998;24:40-46",
 "limitations": "Cardiovascular subscore uses Pressure-Adjusted Heart Rate (PAR = HR × RAP/MAP), requiring CVP measurement (invasive). Less commonly used than SOFA in current practice. Single-center derivation.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",

}
```

#### E095 · Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)

```json
{
 "name": "Sequential Organ Failure Assessment",
 "acronym": "SOFA",
 "subcategory": "critical care / organ failure",
 "purpose": "Assesses the degree of organ failure across six organ systems in critically ill patients; used to track organ dysfunction over time and define sepsis.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Respiratory: PaO₂/FiO₂",
   "description": "Ratio of arterial oxygen to inspired oxygen fraction",
   "unit": "mmHg",
   "range_or_options": "≥400 = 0; <400 = 1; <300 = 2; <200 (on vasopressors) = 3; <100 (on vasopressors) = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Coagulation: Platelets (×10³/µL)",
   "description": "Platelet count",
   "unit": "×10³/µL",
   "range_or_options": "≥150 = 0; <150 = 1; <100 = 2; <50 = 3; <20 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Liver: Bilirubin (mg/dL)",
   "description": "Total serum bilirubin",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "<1.2 = 0; 1.2–1.9 = 1; 2.0–5.9 = 2; 6.0–11.9 = 3; ≥12.0 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Cardiovascular: MAP and vasopressors",
   "description": "Mean arterial pressure and dose of vasopressors (µg/kg/min)",
   "unit": "mixed",
   "range_or_options": "MAP ≥70 = 0; MAP <70 = 1; dopamine ≤5 or dobutamine = 2; dopamine 5–15 or norepinephrine ≤0.1 = 3; dopamine >15 or norepinephrine >0.1 or epinephrine ≤0.1 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "CNS: GCS",
   "description": "Glasgow Coma Scale",
   "unit": "score",
   "range_or_options": "15 = 0; 13–14 = 1; 10–12 = 2; 6–9 = 3; <6 = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Renal: Creatinine or urine output",
   "description": "Serum creatinine or 24-hour urine output",
   "unit": "mg/dL or mL/day",
   "range_or_options": "Cr <1.2 = 0; 1.2–1.9 = 1; 2.0–3.4 = 2; 3.5–4.9 or UO <500 mL/day = 3; ≥5.0 or UO <200 mL/day = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "SOFA = Respiratory(0–4) + Coagulation(0–4) + Liver(0–4) + Cardiovascular(0–4) + CNS(0–4) + Renal(0–4). Total = 0–24.",
 "score_range": "0–24",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "No organ failure"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1–6",
   "meaning": "Mild organ dysfunction"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "7–9",
   "meaning": "Moderate organ failure"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–12",
   "meaning": "Severe organ failure; mortality ~50%"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥13",
   "meaning": "Critical organ failure; mortality >80%"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Change ≥2 in 24h",
   "meaning": "Acute worsening; SOFA increase ≥2 defines sepsis-related organ dysfunction"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "European/North American ICU patients (original ESICM consensus); >10,000 patients across multiple studies",
 "original_citation": "Vincent JL, Moreno R, Takala J, et al. The SOFA (Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment) score to describe organ dysfunction/failure. Intensive Care Med. 1996;22(7):707-710. PMID: 8844239",
 "additional_validation": "Ferreira FL, et al. JAMA. 2001;286(14):1754-1758; Singer M, et al. JAMA. 2016;315(8):801-810 (Sepsis-3)",
 "limitations": "Requires laboratory values (not instant). Cardiovascular subscore has changed definitions over time (vasopressor types/doses). GCS is subjective. Originally designed for sepsis but applied broadly. Sequential assessment more informative than single value.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
```

#### E101 · Trauma and Injury Severity Score (TRISS)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L6024–L6047 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Trauma and Injury Severity Score",
 "acronym": "TRISS",
 "subcategory": "critical care / trauma",
 "purpose": "Combines physiologic (RTS) and anatomic (ISS) severity with age to predict survival probability in trauma patients.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "RTS (Revised Trauma Score)",
   "description": "Physiologic severity from GCS, SBP, RR",
   "unit": "score",
   "range_or_options": "0–7.8408",
   "points_or_coefficient": "continuous variable in regression"
  },
  {
   "variable": "ISS (Injury Severity Score)",
   "description": "Anatomic severity from AIS",
   "unit": "score",
   "range_or_options": "1–75",
   "points_or_coefficient": "continuous variable in regression"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Age",
   "description": "Patient age",
   "unit": "years",
   "range_or_options": "<55 = 0; ≥55 = 1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "binary age variable"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "b = b₀ + b₁×RTS + b₂×ISS + b₃×Age_code\nP(survival) = 1/(1 + e^(−b))\n\nFor blunt trauma: b₀ = −1.2470, b₁ = 0.9544, b₂ = −0.0768, b₃ = −1.9052\nFor penetrating trauma: b₀ = −0.6029, b₁ = 1.1430, b₂ = −0.1516, b₃ = −2.6676",
 "score_range": "0–100% predicted survival probability",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": ">0.50 (50%)",
   "meaning": "Expected survivor"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≤0.50 (50%)",
   "meaning": "Expected non-survivor"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Individual probability interpretation",
   "meaning": "Higher P(survival) = better prognosis"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "MTOS database (US); validated in UK TARN, and international trauma registries",
 "original_citation": "Boyd CR, Tolson MA, Copes WS. Evaluating trauma care: the TRISS method. J Trauma. 1987;27(4):370-378. PMID: 3106646",
 "additional_validation": "Champion HR, et al. J Trauma. 1990;30:Supplement; Gabbe BJ, et al. Injury. 2005",
 "limitations": "Requires ISS coding (AIS specialists). Uses binary age cutoff (55) — misses age-related risk gradients. ISS known limitations apply. Blunt vs penetrating coefficients may not apply to mixed mechanisms. Pre-dates modern trauma systems (coefficients from 1980s MTOS).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
{
 "name": "CROP Index (Compliance, Rate, Oxygenation, Pressure)",

   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "multiplier"
  },
  {
   "variable": "PaO₂/PAO₂ ratio",

   "unit": "ratio",
   "range_or_options": "0–1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "multiplier"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Maximal inspiratory pressure (MIP/PImax)",
   "description": "Maximal negative inspiratory force (cmH₂O)",
   "unit": "cmH₂O",
   "range_or_options": "−1 to −120",
   "points_or_coefficient": "multiplier"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Respiratory rate",

   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator"
  }
 ],

   "score_range": "<13 mL/cmH₂O",

 ],
```

```json
  }
 ],
 "formula": "AKIN staging (within 48h window):\nStage 1: SCr ↑≥0.3 mg/dL or 1.5–1.9× baseline; UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × 6h\nStage 2: SCr 2.0–2.9× baseline; UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × ≥12h\nStage 3: SCr ≥3× or ≥4.0 mg/dL (with acute rise ≥0.5) or RRT; UO <0.3 mL/kg/h × ≥24h or anuria ≥12h",

 ],
```

#### E109 · Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes AKI Criteria (KDIGO AKI)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L10088–L10111 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L8015, L10088) · merged naming variants: Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes AKI Staging -->

```json
{
 "name": "Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes AKI Criteria",
 "acronym": "KDIGO AKI",

 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Serum creatinine change",
   "description": "Change in serum creatinine from baseline within 48 hours or 7 days",
   "unit": "mg/dL or relative change",
   "range_or_options": "Increase ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48h OR increase ≥1.5× baseline within 7 days OR UO criteria",
   "points_or_coefficient": "staging criteria"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Urine output",
   "description": "Urine volume per hour",
   "unit": "mL/kg/hour",
   "range_or_options": "Continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "staging criteria"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Staging system:\n\nStage 1: SCr increase ≥0.3 mg/dL (≥26.5 µmol/L) within 48h OR SCr increase ≥1.5–1.9× baseline within 7 days OR UO <0.5 mL/kg/h for 6–12 hours\n\nStage 2: SCr increase 2.0–2.9× baseline within 7 days OR UO <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥12 hours\n\nStage 3: SCr increase ≥3.0× baseline within 7 days OR SCr ≥4.0 mg/dL (≥353.6 µmol/L) OR initiation of RRT OR (if <18 years) eGFR decrease to <35 mL/min/1.73m² OR UO <0.3 mL/kg/h for ≥24 hours OR anuria for ≥12 hours",
 "score_range": "Stage 0–3",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "No AKI",
   "meaning": "No creatinine or urine output criteria met"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Stage 1",
   "meaning": "Mild AKI. Identify and treat underlying cause. Monitor closely."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Stage 2",
   "meaning": "Moderate AKI. Nephrology consultation recommended."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Stage 3",
   "meaning": "Severe AKI. Nephrology consultation mandatory. Evaluate for RRT. Mortality significantly increased."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "International consensus from KDIGO Work Group; validated in >1 million patients across hundreds of studies",
 "original_citation": "Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Acute Kidney Injury Work Group. KDIGO clinical practice guideline for acute kidney injury. Kidney Int Suppl. 2012;2(1):1-138. (Consensus guideline, no single PMID for the guideline itself)",
 "additional_validation": "Kellum JA, et al. Crit Care. 2013;17:R204 (AKI definitions comparison); Luo X, et al. Nephrol Dial Transplant. 2014;29:78-86",
 "limitations": "Requires baseline creatinine (may be unknown in 50% of cases). Creatinine-based criteria may not detect early AKI (biomarker lag). Urine output criteria require accurate measurement (difficult in non-catheterized patients). Non-specific — many causes of creatinine rise. Does not incorporate biomarkers (NGAL, KIM-1) which may detect AKI earlier.",
```

```json
{
 "name": "Renal Angina Index",
 "acronym": "RAI",
 "subcategory": "acute kidney injury",
 "purpose": "Pediatric tool combining AKI risk (baseline vulnerability) and AKI injury signals (creatinine/fluid overload) to predict severe AKI in critically ill children, analogous to 'angina' preceding 'infarction.'",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Risk tier (baseline vulnerability)",
   "description": "Patient's baseline risk: standard ICU, high-risk ICU, or bone marrow transplant/CPR",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Standard ICU = 1; High-risk ICU = 2; BMT/CPR = 3",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1, 2, or 3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Injury signal (creatinine change or fluid overload)",
   "description": "Creatinine rise from baseline or fluid overload percentage",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Creatinine ≥1.5× or FO 10–15% = 1; Creatinine ≥2× or FO ≥15% = 2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 or 2"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "RAI = Risk_tier(1–3) × Injury_signal(1–2). Range: 1–6.\nRenal Angina Fulfilled: RAI ≥8 at 12h or ≥6 at 24h (depending on version).",
 "score_range": "1–6 (product; threshold ≥8 or ≥6 depending on time point)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "RAI <8",
   "meaning": "Renal angina NOT fulfilled. Low probability of severe AKI (negative predictive value >95%)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "RAI ≥8",
   "meaning": "Renal angina fulfilled. High risk of severe AKI. Consider biomarkers (NGAL, KIM-1) for further stratification."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Critically ill children admitted to PICU (single-center derivation, multicenter validation)",
 "original_citation": "Basu RK, Zappitelli M, Brunner L, et al. Derivation and validation of the renal angina index to improve the prediction of acute kidney injury in critically ill children. Kidney Int. 2014;85(3):659-667. PMID: 23925279",
 "additional_validation": "Menon S, et al. Crit Care Med. 2018;46:e647-e654; Basu RK, et al. Pediatr Crit Care Med. 2018;19:524-532",
 "limitations": "Developed for pediatric ICU populations only. Thresholds for RAI fulfillment debated. Requires accurate fluid balance tracking. Not validated in adults. Injury signal definitions may vary by study. Requires baseline creatinine or estimated value.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "medium"
}
```

#### E111 · Risk, Injury, Failure, Loss, End-Stage Kidney Disease Criteria (RIFLE)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L8039–L8063 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L8039, L10113) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Risk, Injury, Failure, Loss, End-Stage Kidney Disease Criteria",
 "acronym": "RIFLE",
 "subcategory": "acute kidney injury",
 "purpose": "Earlier classification system for AKI severity based on serum creatinine change and urine output (predecessor to KDIGO AKI staging).",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Serum creatinine change",
   "description": "Change from baseline SCr",
   "unit": "mg/dL or fold",
   "range_or_options": "Risk: 1.5× baseline or ↑≥0.3 mg/dL; Injury: 2× baseline; Failure: 3× baseline or SCr ≥4 mg/dL with acute rise ≥0.5 mg/dL",
   "points_or_coefficient": "staging only"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Urine output",
   "description": "Urine output per kg per hour",
   "unit": "mL/kg/hr",
   "range_or_options": "Risk: <0.5 mL/kg/h × 6h; Injury: <0.5 mL/kg/h × 12h; Failure: <0.3 mL/kg/h × 24h or anuria × 12h",
   "points_or_coefficient": "staging only"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "RIFLE classification:\nR (Risk): SCr 1.5× baseline or ↑≥0.3 mg/dL or UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × 6h\nI (Injury): SCr 2× baseline or UO <0.5 mL/kg/h × 12h\nF (Failure): SCr 3× baseline or SCr ≥4 mg/dL + acute rise ≥0.5 mg/dL or UO <0.3 mL/kg/h × 24h or anuria × 12h\nL (Loss): Complete loss of kidney function >4 weeks\nE (End-stage): Complete loss of kidney function >3 months",
 "score_range": "R / I / F / L / E",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "R (Risk)",
   "meaning": "AKI risk identified. Monitor."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "I (Injury)",
   "meaning": "Kidney injury. Intervene."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "F (Failure)",
   "meaning": "Kidney failure. Consider RRT."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "L (Loss)",
   "meaning": "Persistent loss >4 weeks"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "E (End-stage)",
   "meaning": "End-stage kidney disease >3 months"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients from multiple ICU and hospital cohorts",
 "original_citation": "Bellomo R, Ronco C, Kellum JA, et al. Acute renal failure — definition, outcome measures, animal models, fluid therapy and information technology needs: the Second International Consensus Conference of the Acute Dialysis Quality Initiative (ADQI) Group. Crit Care. 2004;8(4):R204-R212. PMID: 15312219",
 "additional_validation": "Hoste EA, et al. Crit Care. 2006;10:R73; Kellum JA, et al. Crit Care Med. 2007;35:1250-1255",
 "limitations": "Largely superseded by KDIGO AKI criteria (2012). SCr rise threshold of 1.5× may miss small absolute increases in patients with low baseline SCr. L and E categories describe outcomes, not acute severity. UO criteria require accurate timing. Multiple versions exist (originally used different creatinine cutoffs).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

### GFR estimation

#### E112 · CKD-EPI Creatinine Equation (2021, Race-Free) (CKD-EPI 2021)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L9980–L10006 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "CKD-EPI Creatinine Equation (2021, Race-Free)",
 "acronym": "CKD-EPI 2021",
 "subcategory": "GFR estimation",
 "purpose": "Estimates glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) from serum creatinine without a race variable (replacing the 2009 version that included race).",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Serum creatinine",
   "description": "Serum creatinine (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "exponent κ in formula"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Age",
   "description": "Age in years",
   "unit": "years",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "exponent in formula"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Sex",
   "description": "Male or female",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Male/Female",
   "points_or_coefficient": "sex modifier in formula"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "eGFR = 142 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^(−1.200) × 0.9938^Age × (1.012 if female)\n\nWhere:\nκ = 0.9 (male), 0.7 (female)\nα = −0.302 (male), −0.241 (female)\nmin = minimum of Scr/κ or 1\nmax = maximum of Scr/κ or 1\n\neGFR in mL/min/1.73 m²",
 "score_range": "Continuous (0–200+ mL/min/1.73m²)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "≥90",
   "meaning": "Normal or high eGFR (G1)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "60–89",
   "meaning": "Mildly decreased (G2). Kidney damage markers should be assessed."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "45–59",
   "meaning": "Mildly to moderately decreased (G3a)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "30–44",
   "meaning": "Moderately to severely decreased (G3b)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "15–29",
   "meaning": "Severely decreased (G4)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "<15",
   "meaning": "Kidney failure (G5). Dialysis or transplant evaluation."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Pooled dataset from >8,000 participants across multiple research and clinical populations",
 "original_citation": "Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. New creatinine- and cystatin C-based equations to estimate GFR without race. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(19):1737-1749. PMID: 34554658",
 "additional_validation": "Levey AS, et al. Ann Intern Med. 2009;150:604-612 (original 2009 CKD-EPI with race); Delanaye P, et al. Nephrol Dial Transplant. 2022 (external validation of race-free equation)",
 "limitations": "Less accurate at extremes of muscle mass (bodybuilders, amputees, malnourished). Not valid for patients on dialysis. Does not perform well in acute kidney injury (non-steady-state creatinine). Race variable was removed due to health equity concerns but may affect accuracy in some populations. All GFR estimating equations have ~90% accuracy within ±30% of measured GFR. Cystatin C-based or combined equations may be more accurate for some patients.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

#### E114 · Cockcroft-Gault Equation (CG)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L10035–L10061 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L7962, L10035) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Cockcroft-Gault Equation",
 "acronym": "CG",
 "subcategory": "GFR estimation / drug dosing",
 "purpose": "Estimates creatinine clearance (not GFR) for drug dosing in adults. One of the oldest and most widely used equations for medication adjustment.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Age",
   "description": "Age in years",
   "unit": "years",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator in formula"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Weight",
   "description": "Body weight in kg (ideally ideal body weight; use actual weight if not obese)",
   "unit": "kg",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "numerator in formula"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Serum creatinine",
   "description": "Serum creatinine (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator in formula"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Sex (female)",
   "description": "Female sex",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "multiply result by 0.85 if female"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CrCl (mL/min) = [(140 − Age) × Weight(kg)] / (72 × Scr(mg/dL)) × 0.85 if female\n\nNote: Weight should be adjusted for obesity (use ideal body weight or adjusted body weight = IBW + 0.4 × (actual − IBW)).",
 "score_range": "Continuous (0–150+ mL/min)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "≥90",
   "meaning": "Normal renal function"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "60–89",
   "meaning": "Mild impairment"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "30–59",
   "meaning": "Moderate impairment. Drug dose adjustments may be needed."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "15–29",
   "meaning": "Severe impairment. Significant drug dose reductions required."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "<15",
   "meaning": "End-stage renal disease. Dialysis consideration."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "249 hospitalized male patients with stable creatinine at Memorial Sloan Kettering",
 "original_citation": "Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine. Nephron. 1976;16(1):31-41. PMID: 1244564",
 "additional_validation": "Levey AS, et al. Ann Intern Med. 2009;150:604-612; Stevens LA, et al. Am J Kidney Dis. 2007;50:922-933",
 "limitations": "Overestimates GFR at low GFR. Less accurate than CKD-EPI for estimating GFR (systematically biased). Original derivation in 249 hospitalized men (poor generalizability). Weight-dependent — problematic in obese, malnourished, or edematous patients. Still recommended for aminoglycoside and vancomycin dosing. Not recommended for GFR reporting by KDIGO (use CKD-EPI). Does not account for race (by design).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
 "formula": "2021 race-free equation:\neGFR = 135 × min(Scr/κ, 1)^α × max(Scr/κ, 1)^(−0.544) × min(Scys/0.8, 1)^(−0.323) × max(Scys/0.8, 1)^(−0.778) × 0.9961^Age × [0.963 if female]\n\nWhere: κ and α are sex-specific (same as CKD-EPI Cr 2021)",
 "score_range": "eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m²",
 "interpretation": [

   "score_range": "Same GFR staging as CKD-EPI Cr (G1–G5)",
   "meaning": "Same KDIGO GFR categories apply"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Pooled dataset of 3,960 participants with measured GFR",
 "original_citation": "Inker LA, Eneanya ND, Coresh J, et al. New creatinine- and cystatin C-based equations to estimate GFR without race. N Engl J Med. 2021;385(19):1737-1749. PMID: 34554658",
 "additional_validation": "Validated across racial/ethnic groups in US and international cohorts",
 "limitations": "Requires both creatinine and cystatin C (limited availability). More expensive. Same limitations of individual markers apply (though combination is more accurate). Not yet widely implemented in all laboratories.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
```

```json
{

  {
```

```json
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"

   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {

   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  }
 ],
```

#### E120 · Modified CT Severity Index / CT Severity Index (CTSI / MCTSI)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L8408–L8430 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Modified CT Severity Index / CT Severity Index",
 "acronym": "CTSI / MCTSI",
 "subcategory": "acute pancreatitis",
 "purpose": "Assesses severity of acute pancreatitis based on CT findings of pancreatic necrosis and peripancreatic fluid collections.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Pancreatic inflammation",
   "description": "CT appearance of pancreatic parenchyma",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Normal = 0; Focal/diffuse enlargement = 2; Peripancreatic inflammation = 4; Single peripancreatic fluid collection = 4; Two or more fluid collections or retroperitoneal gas = 6",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–6"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Necrosis",
   "description": "Percentage of pancreatic necrosis on contrast-enhanced CT",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "None = 0; <30% = 2; 30–50% = 4; >50% = 6",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–6"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CTSI = Inflammation(0–6) + Necrosis(0–6)\n\nModified CTSI (MCTSI):\n- Normal pancreas = 0\n- Intrinsic pancreatic abnormalities (with or without peripancreatic changes) = 2\n- Pancreatic/peripancreatic fluid collections or peripancreatic fat necrosis = 4\n- Necrosis: none = 0; <30% = 2; ≥30% = 4\nMCTSI = Inflammation(0–4) + Necrosis(0–4)\n\nExtrapancreatic complications (pleural effusion, ascites, vascular complications, GI tract involvement) = +2 in MCTSI",
 "score_range": "CTSI: 0–10; MCTSI: 0–10",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "CTSI 0–3",
   "meaning": "Mild pancreatitis. Low complication rate (~3%)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "CTSI 4–6",
   "meaning": "Moderate. Complication rate ~20%."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "CTSI 7–10",
   "meaning": "Severe. Complication rate ~60%. Mortality ~17%."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with acute pancreatitis undergoing contrast-enhanced CT",
 "original_citation": "Balthazar EJ, Robinson DL, Megibow AJ, Ranson JH. Acute pancreatitis: value of CT in establishing prognosis. Radiology. 1990;174(2):331-336. PMID: 2296641 (CTSI); Mortele KJ, et al. Radiology. 2004;233(1):63-72 (MCTSI)",
 "additional_validation": "Lecesne R, et al. Radiology. 1998;208:327-332; Raghuwanshi S, et al. Abdom Imaging. 2016",
 "limitations": "Requires contrast-enhanced CT (not indicated in mild pancreatitis). CT timing matters (early CT may underestimate necrosis). Inter-rater variability in assessing necrosis percentage. Necrosis scoring assumes CT performed at 72+ hours. Does not capture extrapancreatic complications well (addressed in MCTSI).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
 "formula": "Lille = exp(−R) / (1 + exp(−R))\n\nWhere R = 3.19 − 0.101×age(years) + 0.147×albumin_day0(g/L) + 0.0165×evolution_bilirubin(d0−d7)(µmol/L) − 0.206×renal_insufficiency(0/1) − 0.0065×bilirubin_day0(µmol/L) − 0.0096×bilirubin_day7(µmol/L)\n\nNote: The exact formula coefficients are from the 2007 publication. Verify exact formula and variable transformations (some publications use mg/dL, others µmol/L) from Louvet A, et al. 2007. Bilirubin and albumin in mg/dL conversions may differ from µmol/L formula.",
 "score_range": "0–1.0 (continuous probability)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<0.45",
   "meaning": "Complete response. 6-month survival ~85–95%. Continue corticosteroids."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "0.45–0.56",
   "meaning": "Partial response. 6-month survival ~50–60%. Consider stopping steroids and palliative care discussion."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥0.56",
   "meaning": "Non-response. 6-month survival ~10–25%. Corticosteroids should be stopped. Consider palliative care."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with severe alcoholic hepatitis (MDF ≥32) treated with corticosteroids in Lille, France and international cohorts",
 "original_citation": "Louvet A, Naveau S, Abdelnour M, et al. The Lille model: a new tool for therapeutic strategy in patients with severe alcoholic hepatitis treated with steroids. Hepatology. 2007;45(6):1348-1354. PMID: 17518367",
 "additional_validation": "Louvet A, et al. Hepatology. 2009;50:1857-1863; Mathurin P, et al. Hepatology. 2011;55:1152-1160 (STOPAH)",
 "limitations": "Should only be calculated after 7 days of corticosteroid treatment. Requires serial bilirubin (day 0 and day 7). Cannot be applied to patients not receiving steroids. Formula uses µmol/L (not mg/dL) for bilirubin in the original — conversion needed for US laboratories (1 mg/dL = 17.1 µmol/L). Thresholds may need calibration for different populations. Does not include encephalopathy at day 7 (which independently worsens prognosis).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

#### E125 · Maddrey Discriminant Function (MDF)

```json
{
 "name": "Maddrey Discriminant Function",
 "acronym": "MDF",
 "subcategory": "alcoholic hepatitis",
 "purpose": "Identifies patients with severe alcoholic hepatitis who may benefit from corticosteroid therapy.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Prothrombin time (patient)",
   "description": "Patient's prothrombin time in seconds",
   "unit": "seconds",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "numerator"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Prothrombin time (control)",
   "description": "Control prothrombin time in seconds",
   "unit": "seconds",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Serum bilirubin",
   "description": "Total serum bilirubin (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "multiplier"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "MDF = 4.6 × (PT_patient − PT_control) + Bilirubin(mg/dL)\n\nAlternative using INR (when INR is available instead of PT control):\nMDF = 4.6 × (INR − 1) + Bilirubin(mg/dL)",
 "score_range": "continuous (typically 0–100+)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<32",
   "meaning": "Non-severe alcoholic hepatitis. Steroids not routinely recommended. 28-day mortality ~10%."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥32",
   "meaning": "Severe alcoholic hepatitis. Consider corticosteroids (prednisolone 40 mg/day × 28 days). 28-day mortality ~30–50%."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with biopsy-proven alcoholic hepatitis",
 "original_citation": "Maddrey WC, Boitnott JK, Bedine MS, et al. Corticosteroid therapy of alcoholic hepatitis. Gastroenterology. 1978;75(2):193-199. PMID: 352788",
 "additional_validation": "Mathurin P, et al. J Hepatol. 2011;55:694-699; Louvet A, et al. Gastroenterology. 2009;137:1590-1598 (Lille model for early steroid response)",
 "limitations": "PT/INR and bilirubin can be elevated from causes other than alcoholic hepatitis (sepsis, cholestasis). Cutoff of 32 is somewhat arbitrary. Does not capture renal function, infection status, or nutritional status. INR-based formula is approximate (not identical to original PT-based version). Steroid response should be assessed early (Lille score at day 7).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
{

  },
```

```json
   "range_or_options": "10.0–11.9 = 1; <10.0 = 6",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–6"
  },
  {

   "description": "Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)",
   "unit": "mmHg",
   "range_or_options": "100–109 = 1; 90–99 = 2; <90 = 3",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Heart rate ≥100 bpm",
   "description": "Tachycardia",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Presentation with melena",
   "description": "Black tarry stools",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Syncope",
   "description": "Presentation with syncope",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",

 ],

 "score_range": "0–23",
 "interpretation": [

  },

   "score_range": "1–2",
   "meaning": "Low risk. Consider outpatient management with close follow-up."
  },
  {

  }
 ],
```

#### E128 · Rockall Score for Upper GI Bleeding (Rockall)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L10497–L10524 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L6699, L10497) · merged naming variants: Full Rockall Score -->
```json
{
 "name": "Rockall Score for Upper GI Bleeding",
 "acronym": "Rockall",
 "subcategory": "gastrointestinal bleeding",
 "purpose": "Predicts mortality after upper GI bleeding using clinical and endoscopic findings. Requires endoscopy for complete scoring.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Age",
   "description": "Age in years",
   "unit": "years",
   "range_or_options": "<60 = 0; 60–79 = 1; ≥80 = 2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Shock",
   "description": "Hemodynamic status",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "No shock = 0; HR>100, SBP>100 = 1; SBP<100 = 2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Comorbidity",
   "description": "Significant comorbidities",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "None = 0; CHF, IHD = 2; Renal failure, liver failure, disseminated malignancy = 3",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Diagnosis (endoscopic)",
   "description": "Endoscopic finding",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Mallory-Weiss = 0; No lesion/srce seen, erosive disease = 1; Upper GI malignancy = 2; All other = 0",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Major stigmata of recent hemorrhage",
   "description": "Active bleeding, visible vessel, or adherent clot at endoscopy",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "None/dark spot = 0; Blood in upper GI, adherent clot, visible vessel, spurting = 2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Rockall = Age(0–2) + Shock(0–2) + Comorbidity(0–3) + Diagnosis(0–2) + Stigmata(0–2)\n\nPre-endoscopy score = Age + Shock + Comorbidity (range 0–7)\nFull score = all 5 components (range 0–11)",
 "score_range": "0–11 (full score); 0–7 (pre-endoscopy)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Pre-endoscopy 0",
   "meaning": "Very low mortality risk. Consider early discharge from ED."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Full score 0–2",
   "meaning": "Low mortality risk (~0–2%). Low rebleeding risk."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Full score 3–4",
   "meaning": "Low-moderate risk (~3–5% mortality)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Full score 5–7",
   "meaning": "Moderate-high risk (~10–15% mortality)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Full score ≥8",
   "meaning": "High mortality risk (~25–40%+)."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with upper GI bleeding in UK hospitals",
 "original_citation": "Rockall TA, Logan RFA, Devlin HB, et al. Risk assessment after acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Gut. 1996;38(3):316-321. PMID: 8675081",
 "additional_validation": "Vreeburg EM, et al. Gastrointest Endosc. 2000;51:59-63; Das A, et al. Gastrointest Endosc. 2003;57:872-879",
 "limitations": "Requires endoscopy for complete scoring (endoscopic variables unavailable at presentation). Mortality prediction is better than rebleeding prediction. Comorbidity categories are imprecise (where does 'significant' begin?). Does not capture antiplatelet/anticoagulant use. Subjective endoscopic assessment (inter-observer variability). GBS is preferred for pre-endoscopy risk stratification.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high",
 "merge_note": "Merge discrepancy: a dropped duplicate copy (source L6699) listed endoscopic stigmata as 0–3 points and full-score range 0–12; the kept copy matches the published full Rockall (stigmata 0–2; total 0–11; pre-endoscopy 0–7). Verify against Rockall TA et al., Gut 1996 before promoting to ready."
}
```

```json
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator"

  {

   "unit": "×10⁹/L",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator"
  }
 ],

 "interpretation": [

  },

  },

   "meaning": "High probability of advanced fibrosis (≥F3). Specificity ~97%. Refer to hepatologist."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with chronic hepatitis C (derivation) and subsequently NAFLD/NASH",
 "original_citation": "Sterling RK, Lissen E, Clumeck N, et al. Development of a simple noninvasive index to predict significant fibrosis in patients with HIV/HCV coinfection. Hepatology. 2006;43(6):1317-1325. PMID: 16729309",

 "limitations": "Less accurate in the indeterminate zone (1.3–2.67). Affected by acute hepatitis flare (AST/ALT fluctuate). Not reliable in HCV-HIV coinfection with very low CD4 counts.  "copyright_status": "public domain",
```

```json
   "unit": "ratio",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "+0.66 × log(AST/ALT)"

   "range_or_options": "continuous",

  }

{
```

```json
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "AST",
   "description": "Aspartate aminotransferase (IU/L)",
   "unit": "IU/L",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "numerator"
  },
  {
   "variable": "AST upper limit of normal",
   "description": "ULN for AST at local laboratory (typically 40 IU/L)",
   "unit": "IU/L",
   "range_or_options": "typically 40 IU/L",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Platelet count",
   "description": "Platelet count (×10⁹/L)",
   "unit": "×10⁹/L",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "denominator"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "APRI = [(AST / ULN_AST) / Platelet_count(×10⁹/L)] × 100",
 "score_range": "Continuous (typically 0–5+)",
 "interpretation": [

  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with chronic hepatitis C; extensively validated in >40 studies across multiple liver diseases",
 "original_citation": "Wai CT, Greenson JK, Fontana RJ, et al. A simple noninvasive index can predict both significant fibrosis and cirrhosis in patients with chronic hepatitis C. Hepatology. 2003;38(2):518-526. PMID: 12883497",
```

```json
{
 "name": "MELD-Sodium Score",
 "acronym": "MELD-Na",
 "subcategory": "liver transplant allocation",
 "purpose": "Refined MELD score incorporating serum sodium to improve mortality prediction in cirrhosis. Current standard for liver transplant allocation in the US.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Serum bilirubin",
   "description": "Total bilirubin (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",

  },
  {
   "variable": "INR",
   "description": "International Normalized Ratio",
   "unit": "ratio",
   "range_or_options": "continuous",
   "points_or_coefficient": "as per MELD"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Serum creatinine",
   "description": "Serum creatinine (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "continuous (min 1.0, max 4.0)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "as per MELD"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Serum sodium",
   "description": "Serum sodium (mEq/L)",
   "unit": "mEq/L",
   "range_or_options": "125–137 mEq/L (constrained range)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "incorporated via formula"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Dialysis",
   "description": "≥2 dialysis sessions in past week",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "creatinine set to 4.0"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "MELD-Na = MELD + 1.32 × (137 − Na) − 0.033 × MELD × (137 − Na)\n\nWhere:\n- MELD is calculated as above (minimum MELD = 1, maximum MELD used in calculation capped at 40 in the non-linear version)\n- Na is constrained between 125 and 137 mEq/L\n- If Na <125, use 125; if Na >137, use 137\n- MELD score minimum = 1; maximum for Na interaction = 11 in the UNOS version\n\nUNOS implementation (post-2016): MELD-Na replaces MELD with a floor of MELD = 1 and ceiling adjustments. Verify current UNOS policy for latest coefficients.",
 "score_range": "6–40 (effectively)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Same MELD thresholds, but scores are generally 1–3 points higher with Na correction",
   "meaning": "Higher scores with hyponatremia → higher transplant priority"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Na <125 with high MELD",
   "meaning": "Significantly worse prognosis. Sodium <125 adds substantial mortality risk."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "US liver transplant candidates in the UNOS/OPTN database",
 "original_citation": "Kim WR, Biggins SW, Kremers WK, et al. Hyponatremia and mortality among patients on the liver-transplant waiting list. N Engl J Med. 2008;359(10):1018-1026. PMID: 18768945; MELD-Na: Leise MD, et al. Hepatology. 2014;60:284-292",
 "additional_validation": "Heuman DM, et al. Hepatology. 2004;40:802-809; Myers RP, et al. Gut. 2006;55:1258-1264; OPTN policy change 2016",
 "limitations": "Sodium may be affected by diuretic use, fluid status, and measurement technique. Diuretic-adjusted MELD-Na has been proposed but not universally adopted. MELD-Na may disadvantage patients on aggressive diuretic therapy (iatrogenic hyponatremia). Changes to UNOS policy (MELD 3.0) may further refine scoring. Not validated for acute liver failure.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use, check for commercial app — used by UNOS/OPTN",
```

#### E134 · Model for End-Stage Liver Disease Score (MELD)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L10192–L10218 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L8141, L10192) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Model for End-Stage Liver Disease Score",
 "acronym": "MELD",
 "subcategory": "liver transplant allocation",
 "purpose": "Predicts 3-month mortality in patients with chronic liver disease. Used for prioritizing liver transplant allocation.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Serum bilirubin",
   "description": "Total bilirubin (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "continuous (minimum 1.0 mg/dL for calculation)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "3.78 × ln(bilirubin)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "INR",
   "description": "International Normalized Ratio",
   "unit": "ratio",
   "range_or_options": "continuous (minimum 1.0)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "11.20 × ln(INR)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Serum creatinine",
   "description": "Serum creatinine (mg/dL)",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "continuous (minimum 1.0; max 4.0 or with dialysis = 4.0)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "9.57 × ln(creatinine)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Dialysis",
   "description": "Whether patient received ≥2 dialysis sessions in the prior week",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "if yes, creatinine set to 4.0 mg/dL"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "MELD = 3.78 × ln(bilirubin mg/dL) + 11.20 × ln(INR) + 9.57 × ln(creatinine mg/dL) + 6.43\n\nMinimum value for each variable = 1.0\nMaximum creatinine = 4.0 mg/dL (or set to 4.0 if on dialysis)\nAll values set to minimum of 1.0 if below 1.0\nResult rounded to nearest integer\nAdd +1 point if within 30 days of prior calculation (to ensure lab re-checks)\nAdd 10 points if hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exception applies (T2 HCC in original system, now variable by region)",
 "score_range": "6–40 (theoretical maximum; scores >40 capped at 40 in practice)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<9",
   "meaning": "~2% 3-month mortality"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–19",
   "meaning": "~6% 3-month mortality"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "20–29",
   "meaning": "~20% 3-month mortality"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "30–39",
   "meaning": "~53% 3-month mortality"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥40",
   "meaning": "~71% 3-month mortality. Highest priority for transplant."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients undergoing TIPS procedure at Mayo Clinic (derivation); validated in patients with cirrhosis across US transplant centers",
 "original_citation": "Kamath PS, Wiesner RH, Malinchoc M, et al. A model to predict survival in patients with end-stage liver disease. Hepatology. 2001;33(2):464-470. PMID: 11172350",
 "additional_validation": "Said A, et al. Liver Transpl. 2009;15:1266-1272; Wiesner R, et al. Gastroenterology. 2003;124:91-96 (MELD for UNOS allocation)",
 "limitations": "Does not capture hyponatremia (addressed by MELD-Na). Creatinine may be affected by muscle mass, AKI, or hepatorenal syndrome. Bilirubin and INR affected by cholestasis and warfarin, respectively. Does not include portal hypertension severity or encephalopathy. MELD exceptions (HCC, hepatopulmonary syndrome) introduce subjectivity. Not validated in acute liver failure (different pathophysiology). Dialysis creatinine rule is crude.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use, check for commercial app — used by UNOS/OPTN",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4 each arm"
  },
  {
   "variable": "6a/6b. Motor leg (L/R)",
   "description": "Leg drift (5 seconds)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = no drift; 1 = drift before 5s; 2 = some effort against gravity; 3 = no effort against gravity; 4 = no movement; UN = amputation/joint fusion",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4 each leg"
  },
  {
   "variable": "7. Limb ataxia",
   "description": "Finger-nose-finger and heel-shin testing",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = absent; 1 = present in one limb; 2 = present in two limbs",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "8. Sensory",
   "description": "Pin-prick sensation face/arm/leg",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = normal; 1 = mild-moderate loss; 2 = severe-total loss",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "9. Best language",
   "description": "Describes picture, names items, reads sentences",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = no aphasia; 1 = mild-moderate; 2 = severe; 3 = mute/global aphasia",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "10. Dysarthria",
   "description": "Speech clarity",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = normal; 1 = mild-moderate; 2 = severe/anarthric; UN = intubated/physical barrier",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "11. Extinction/inattention",
   "description": "Simultaneous bilateral stimulation",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = no abnormality; 1 = partial (one modality); 2 = complete (two modalities)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "NIHSS = sum of all 15 items (1a + 1b + 1c + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5a + 5b + 6a + 6b + 7 + 8 + 9 + 10 + 11)\n\nTotal range 0–42",
 "score_range": "0–42",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "No neurological deficit (normal neurological exam)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1–4",
   "meaning": "Minor stroke"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5–15",
   "meaning": "Moderate stroke. tPA eligible if within time window."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "16–20",
   "meaning": "Moderate-severe stroke"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "21–42",
   "meaning": "Severe stroke. High mortality risk. Consider mechanical thrombectomy if large vessel occlusion."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS) tPA trial; validated in thousands of stroke studies worldwide",
 "original_citation": "Brott T, Adams HP Jr, Olinger CP, et al. Measurements of acute cerebral infarction: a clinical examination scale. Stroke. 1989;20(7):864-870. PMID: 2749846",
 "additional_validation": "Lyden PD, et al. Stroke. 1994;25:2216-2219 (training and certification); Kasner SE, et al. Stroke. 1999;30:2339-2341; Goldstein LB, Simberkopf Neurology. 2001;57:1344-1345",
 "limitations": "Requires trained assessor (standardized training and certification recommended). Inter-rater variability exists, especially for items 5 (motor) and 8 (sensory). Score of 0 does not exclude significant stroke (posterior circulation stroke may have NIHSS 0). Does not capture posterior circulation deficits well (no cerebellar/brainstem specific items). Not a diagnostic tool — diagnosis requires imaging. Ceiling effect at higher scores.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
```

#### E142 · Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L8966–L8991 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Expanded Disability Status Scale",
 "acronym": "EDSS",
 "subcategory": "multiple sclerosis",
 "purpose": "Standardized neurological examination-based scale quantifying disability in multiple sclerosis patients.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Functional systems",
   "description": "Eight functional systems assessed: Pyramidal, Cerebellar, Brainstem, Sensory, Bowel/Bladder, Visual, Cerebral, Other",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Each FS graded 0–5 or 0–6 depending on system",
   "points_or_coefficient": "used to derive EDSS step"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Ambulation",
   "description": "Walking ability and distance",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "EDSS 0–3: based on functional systems; 4.0–9.5: primarily based on ambulation milestones (unilateral/bilateral assistive device, wheelchair, bed-bound)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "single EDSS step 0–9.5"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "EDSS is a composite rating based on neurological examination of 8 functional systems. No simple formula — assigned by trained neurologist based on the Kurtzke system:\n0 = Normal neurological exam\n1.0–3.5 = Minimal to moderate disability (based on FS scores, no or minimal walking impairment)\n4.0–5.5 = Increasing ambulatory disability (distance-based)\n6.0–6.5 = Requires walking aid\n7.0–7.5 = Wheelchair-bound\n8.0–8.5 = Bed-bound with some arm function\n9.0 = Helpless bed-bound\n9.5 = Death due to MS\n10 = Death due to MS (by definition)",
 "score_range": "0–10",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "Normal neurological exam"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1.0–3.5",
   "meaning": "Fully ambulatory with mild-moderate disability"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4.0–5.5",
   "meaning": "Limited walking distance without aid"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "6.0–6.5",
   "meaning": "Requires cane/crutch to walk"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "7.0–7.5",
   "meaning": "Wheelchair-bound"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "8.0–9.5",
   "meaning": "Bed-bound"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "MS patients globally; standard outcome measure in MS clinical trials since 1980s",
 "original_citation": "Kurtzke JF. Rating neurologic impairment in multiple sclerosis: an expanded disability status scale (EDSS). Neurology. 1983;33(11):1444-1452. PMID: 6685237",
 "additional_validation": "Cutter GR, et al. Mult Scler. 1999;5:173-177; Meyer-Moock S, et al. PLoS One. 2014;9:e103631",
 "limitations": "Non-linear (the difference between EDSS 4 and 6 is not the same as between 0 and 2). Relies heavily on walking in the middle ranges (6.0–7.0). Subject to inter-rater variability. Relatively insensitive to upper extremity/cognitive changes. Not ordinal in a statistical sense. Requires trained neurologist.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use, check for commercial app",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
{

 "input_variables": [

  },
```

```json
   "score_range": "4–5",

  }
 ],
```

```json
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Speech changes",
   "description": "Speech disturbance (NIHSS item 9 combined)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "0 = normal; 1 = mild aphasia; 2 = severe aphasia; 3 = mute/global",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {

   "range_or_options": "0 = normal; 1 = partial gaze palsy; 2 = forced deviation",

   "range_or_options": "0 = absent; 1 = partial; 2 = complete",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"

 ],

{
```

```json
 ],
 "formula": "Fisher Grade (original):\n1 = No subarachnoid blood detected\n2 = Diffuse or thin (<1mm) vertical layers of SAH\n3 = Localized thick clots and/or vertical layers ≥1mm thick\n4 = Intracerebral or intraventricular clot with diffuse or no SAH\n\nModified Fisher Scale (Frontera 2006):\n0 = No SAH or IVH\n1 = Thin SAH, no IVH\n2 = Thin SAH with IVH\n3 = Thick SAH, no IVH\n4 = Thick SAH with IVH",
 "score_range": "1–4 (original); 0–4 (modified Fisher)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Fisher 3 (original) / Modified Fisher 3–4",
   "meaning": "Highest risk of symptomatic vasospasm (~30–70% of cases in older studies). Prophylactic nimodipine and monitoring for vasospasm essential."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Fisher 1–2 (original) / Modified Fisher 0–2",
   "meaning": "Lower vasospasm risk (~10–20%)."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with aneurysmal SAH from multiple neurosurgical centers",
 "original_citation": "Fisher CM, Kistler JP, Davis JM. Relation of cerebral vasospasm to subarachnoid hemorrhage visualized by computerized tomographic scanning. Neurosurgery. 1980;6(1):1-6. PMID: 7354892; Modified Fisher: Frontera JA, et al. Stroke. 2006;37:1389-1396",
 "additional_validation": "Claassen J, et al. Neurosurgery. 2006;58:217-223; Dupont SA, et al. Neurocrit Care. 2010;13:199-203",
 "limitations": "Subjective (inter-rater variability in clot thickness measurement). Original Fisher scale does not account for IVH as a separate category (addressed in Modified Fisher). CT timing matters (very early or late scans may misgrade). Does not capture intracerebral hemorrhage well in original version.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
 "formula": "Staging algorithm:\n\nStage 0 (Very early): Single ≤2cm, CTP A, PS 0 → Resection or ablation\nStage A (Early): Single or ≤3 nodules each ≤3cm, CTP A-B, PS 0 → Resection, transplant, or ablation\nStage B (Intermediate): Multinodular, no vascular invasion/extrahepatic, CTP A-B, PS 0 → TACE\nStage C (Advanced): Vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread, CTP A-B, PS 1–2 → Systemic therapy\nStage D (Terminal): Any tumor, CTP C, PS 3–4 → Best supportive care",
 "score_range": "0 / A / B / C / D",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0 (Very early)",
   "meaning": "5-year survival ~50–70% with treatment"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "A (Early)",
   "meaning": "5-year survival ~50% (transplant) or ~30% (resection/ablation)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "B (Intermediate)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~20 months with TACE"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C (Advanced)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~11 months with systemic therapy (sorafenib, lenvatinib, atezolizumab+bevacizumab)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "D (Terminal)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~3 months. Best supportive care."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with HCC at Barcelona Clinic and validated in international HCC cohorts",
 "original_citation": "Llovet JM, Brú C, Bruix J. Prognosis of hepatocellular carcinoma: the BCLC staging classification. Semin Liver Dis. 1999;19(3):329-338. PMID: 10518312; updated: Forner A, Reig ME, de Lope CR, Bruix J. Hepatology. 2018;67:1694-1705",
 "additional_validation": "Marrero JA, et al. Hepatology. 2018;67:1694-1705 (AASLD guidelines); EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines 2018",
 "limitations": "Not all patients fit neatly into BCLC stages (e.g., large single tumor CTP A — BCLC A vs B). Treatment recommendations may not reflect local expertise or resources. Does not capture tumor biology (AFP, differentiation, molecular profile). Portal hypertension criterion is imprecise (HVPG ≥10 mmHg difficult to measure routinely). Staging and treatment allocation are combined — some prefer separation.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic guideline",

}
```

```json
 ],
```

```json
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Gleason Score = Primary pattern + Secondary pattern (e.g., 3+4=7 or 4+3=7)\n\nISUP Grade Groups (2014 WHO):\nGrade Group 1: Gleason score ≤6 (3+3)\nGrade Group 2: Gleason score 3+4=7\nGrade Group 3: Gleason score 4+3=7\nGrade Group 4: Gleason score 8 (4+4, 3+5, 5+3)\nGrade Group 5: Gleason score 9–10 (4+5, 5+4, 5+5)",

  },
  {

  },

  }

 "additional_validation": "Epstein JI, et al. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2016;140:49-57; Pierorazio PM, et al. Eur Urol. 2013;63:870-879",
```

```json
 "limitations": "Severity classification is somewhat subjective (mental status component). Bicarbonate and pH may be discordant (venous vs arterial). Anion gap may be normal in hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis (post-resuscitation). DKA with euglycemia (glucose <250 mg/dL) is a distinct entity not captured well. Concurrent illness (sepsis, MI) complicates management. Classification doesn't directly predict specific outcomes (mortality, ICU length of stay).",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic guideline",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

#### E163 · 4Ts Score for Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (4Ts)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L9392–L9416 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L9392, L11065) · merged naming variants: 4Ts Score for HIT -->
```json
{
 "name": "4Ts Score for Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia",
 "acronym": "4Ts",
 "subcategory": "heparin-induced thrombocytopenia",
 "purpose": "Pre-test clinical scoring system estimating the probability of HIT to guide diagnostic testing and management decisions.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Thrombocytopenia",
   "description": "Degree of platelet count fall from baseline",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "2 = >50% fall AND nadir ≥20K; 1 = 30–50% fall or nadir 10–19K; 0 = <30% fall or nadir <10K",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Timing of platelet fall",
   "description": "Timing of platelet fall relative to heparin exposure",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "2 = Days 5–10 onset (or ≤1 day if recent heparin in past 30 days); 1 = Day 5–10 (unclear) or >10 days; 0 = ≤4 days without recent exposure",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Thrombosis or other sequelae",
   "description": "New thrombosis, skin necrosis, or acute systemic reaction after IV heparin bolus",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "2 = new confirmed thrombosis or skin necrosis or acute systemic reaction; 1 = progressive/recurrent thrombosis or suspected thrombosis; 0 = none",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Other causes of thrombocytopenia",
   "description": "Presence of other explanations for platelet fall",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "2 = no other cause evident; 1 = possible other cause; 0 = definite other cause present",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0, 1, or 2"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "4Ts = Thrombocytopenia(0–2) + Timing(0–2) + Thrombosis(0–2) + Other_causes(0–2)",
 "score_range": "0–8",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–3",
   "meaning": "Low probability of HIT (~5% positive HIT antibodies). HIT testing may not be needed."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4–5",
   "meaning": "Intermediate probability (~14%). Send HIT antibodies (PF4/heparin ELISA). If positive, confirm with functional assay."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "6–8",
   "meaning": "High probability (~64%). Stop all heparin immediately. Start non-heparin anticoagulant (argatroban, bivalirudin). Send HIT antibodies urgently."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with suspected HIT from multiple clinical settings",
 "original_citation": "Lo GK, Juhl D, Warkentin TE, et al. Evaluation of pretest clinical score (4 T's) for the diagnosis of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in two clinical settings. J Thromb Haemost. 2006;4(4):759-765. PMID: 16634744",
 "additional_validation": "Cuker A, et al. J Thromb Haemost. 2010;8:2681-2686; Denys B, et al. J Thromb Haemost. 2008;6:1603-1606",
 "limitations": "Scoring requires careful clinical assessment (timing, alternative causes). Intermediate score (4–5) requires lab testing. Low scores do not completely exclude HIT (5% false negative). Not applicable to patients on heparin flushes only. Inter-rater variability possible. HIT antibody testing has high sensitivity but low specificity.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

```json
{
 "name": "Revised International Prognostic Scoring System for MDS",
 "acronym": "IPSS-R",
```
