 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Cytogenetic risk category",
   "description": "Karyotype-based risk grouping",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Very good (del(11q), -Y), Good (normal, del(20q), del(5q), +8), Intermediate, Poor (complex 3 abnormalities, chromosome 7 abnormalities), Very poor (complex ≥3 abnormalities)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4 points"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Bone marrow blast percentage",
   "description": "Percentage of blasts in bone marrow aspirate",
   "unit": "%",
   "range_or_options": "≤2% = 0; 3–5% = 1; 6–10% = 2; 11–20% = 3; >20% = 4",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hemoglobin",
   "description": "Hemoglobin level (g/dL)",
   "unit": "g/dL",
   "range_or_options": "≥10 = 0; 8–9.9 = 1; <8 = 1.5",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1.5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Platelet count",
   "description": "Platelet count (×10⁹/L)",
   "unit": "×10⁹/L",
   "range_or_options": "≥100 = 0; 50–99 = 0.5; <50 = 1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "ANC (absolute neutrophil count)",
   "description": "ANC (×10⁹/L)",
   "unit": "×10⁹/L",
   "range_or_options": "≥0.8 = 0; <0.8 = 0.5",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–0.5"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "IPSS-R = Cytogenetics(0–4) + BM_blasts(0–4) + Hemoglobin(0–1.5) + Platelets(0–1) + ANC(0–0.5)\n\nTotal = 0–9 points (maximum theoretically 4+4+1.5+1+0.5=11 but in practice ≤9)",
 "score_range": "0–9 (very low ≤1.5; low 2–3; intermediate 3.5–4.5; high 5–6; very high ≥6.5; cutoffs slightly vary)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Very low (≤1.5)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~8.8 years. AML transformation risk low (~4% at 5 years)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Low (2–3)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~5.3 years. AML transformation risk ~10% at 5 years."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Intermediate (3.5–4.5)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~3.0 years. AML risk ~25% at 5 years."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "High (5–6)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~1.6 years. AML risk ~55% at 5 years."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Very high (≥6.5)",
   "meaning": "Median survival ~0.8 years. AML risk ~85% at 5 years. Transplant evaluation recommended."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "International MDS database from 7,012 patients with primary MDS",
 "original_citation": "Greenberg PL, Tuechler H, Schanz J, et al. Revised international prognostic scoring system for myelodysplastic syndromes. Blood. 2012;120(12):2454-2465. PMID: 22740453",
 "additional_validation": "Della Porta MG, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2015;33:1743-1751; Neukirchen J, et al. Leuk Res. 2014;38:630-636",
 "limitations": "Cytogenetics require skilled cytogeneticist and may take 1–2 weeks. Some patients have insufficient metaphases. Does not incorporate somatic mutations (IPSS-M adds molecular data). At diagnosis only — does not capture disease evolution over time. Thresholds for treatment decisions (e.g., transplant at high/very high) are expert consensus, not empirically derived.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain",

   "points_or_coefficient": "×0.06"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Patient global (VAS)",
   "description": "Patient global assessment of disease activity (0–10 cm)",
   "unit": "cm",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "×0.11"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Duration of morning stiffness (VAS)",
   "description": "Morning stiffness duration (0–10 cm)",
   "unit": "cm",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "×0.06"

   "unit": "mg/L",
   "range_or_options": "≥0.2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "×0.58 × ln(CRP+1) or ×0.07 × ESR"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "ASDAS-CRP = 0.121 × back pain + 0.058 × duration of morning stiffness + 0.110 × patient global + 0.073 × peripheral pain/swelling + 0.579 × ln(CRP+1)\n\nASDAS-ESR = 0.113 × back pain + 0.086 × duration of morning stiffness + 0.069 × patient global + 0.051 × peripheral pain/swelling + 0.075 × ESR\n\nCRP used: mg/L (raw, not log-transformed before formula)",
 "score_range": "~0–5+",
 "interpretation": [

  },
  {
   "score_range": "1.3–<2.1",
   "meaning": "Moderate disease activity"
  },
  {

  },
  {

   "meaning": "Very high disease activity"
  },
  {

  },

   "score_range": "MCID (change in state): ≥0.9",
   "meaning": "Change in disease activity state"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "AxSpA patients from the OASIS cohort and multiple international validation studies",

 "additional_validation": "Machado P, et al. Ann Rheum Dis. 2011;70:440-447; Pedersen SJ, et al. J Rheumatol. 2013",

Does not capture peripheral spondyloarthritis features well. May not reflect MRI findings (sacroiliitis on MRI may be active despite low ASDAS).",

{
 "name": "Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index",

 "subcategory": "axial spondyloarthritis activity",
 "purpose": "Patient-reported disease activity measure for ankylosing spondylitis and axial spondyloarthritis. Assesses fatigue, spinal pain, peripheral joint pain, enthesitis, and morning stiffness.",
 "input_variables": [

   "variable": "Q1: Fatigue/tiredness",

  },
  {

   "unit": "VAS",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw score 0–10"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Q3: Peripheral joint pain/swelling",
   "description": "How much pain/swelling in joints other than neck/back/hips?",
   "unit": "VAS",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw score 0–10"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Q4: Enthesitis",
   "description": "How much tenderness/pain at insertion of tendons/ligaments (excluding hips)?",
   "unit": "VAS",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw score 0–10"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Q5: Severity of morning stiffness",
   "description": "How severe is your morning stiffness from awakening?",
   "unit": "VAS",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw score 0–10"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Q6: Duration of morning stiffness",
   "description": "How long does your morning stiffness last from awakening?",
   "unit": "VAS",
   "range_or_options": "0 (0 hours) – 10 (≥2 hours)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw score 0–10"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "BASDAI = (Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + (Q5+Q6)/2) / 5\nMean of 5 components (Q5 and Q6 averaged before inclusion since both measure morning stiffness)",
 "score_range": "0–10",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<4",
   "meaning": "Low disease activity / inactive disease"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥4",
   "meaning": "Active disease — commonly used threshold for biologic initiation in AS"
  },
  {

   "meaning": "Minimum clinically important improvement"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "AS and axSpA patients across multiple international cohorts. First developed in 1994.",
 "original_citation": "Garrett S, Jenkinson T, Kennedy LG, et al. A new approach to defining disease status in ankylosing spondylitis: the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI). J Rheumatol. 1994;21(12):2286-2291. PMID: 7699630",

ASDAS (incorporating CRP/ESR) preferred for objective assessment. Peripheral spondyloarthritis may not be well captured.",

}

   "variable": "Patient Global Assessment (VAS)",
   "description": "Patient global assessment of disease activity on visual analog scale (0–100 mm)",
   "unit": "mm",
   "range_or_options": "0–100",
   "points_or_coefficient": "×0.014 (ESR version) or ×0.014 (CRP version)"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "DAS28-ESR = 0.56×√(TJC28) + 0.28×√(SJC28) + 0.70×ln(ESR) + 0.014×(Patient GA)\nDAS28-CRP = 0.56×√(TJC28) + 0.28×√(SJC28) + 0.36×ln(CRP+1) + 0.014×(Patient GA) + 0.96",
 "score_range": "0–9.4 (approximately); remission\n\n<2.6",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<2.6",
   "meaning": "Remission"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "2.6–3.2",
   "meaning": "Low disease activity"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3.2–5.1",
   "meaning": "Moderate disease activity"
  },
  {
   "score_range": ">5.1",
   "meaning": "High disease activity"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Patients with rheumatoid arthritis, validated in multiple international cohorts. Originally derived from pre-DMARD era patients by Prevoo et al.",
 "original_citation": "Prevoo ML, van 't Hof MA, Kuper HH, et al. Modified disease activity scores that include twenty-eight-joint counts. Development and validation in a prospective longitudinal study of patients with rheumatoid arthritis. Arthritis Rheum. 1995;38(1):44-48. PMID: 7818570",
 "additional_validation": "Fransen J, et al. Rheumatology. 2003;42:135-142 (DAS28-CRP); Wells GA, et al. J Rheumatol. 2009;36:1009-1025",
 "limitations": "28-joint count excludes feet (MTP, ankle) — may underestimate activity with predominantly lower extremity disease. Patient global VAS introduces subjectivity. ESR influenced by age, sex, anemia. CRP version tends to yield slightly lower scores. Remission defined as DAS28 <2.6 does not always equate to absence of residual disease (Boolean remission by ACR/EULAR preferred). Inability to distinguish synovitis from osteoarthritis in assessed joints.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic tool",
 "confidence": "high"
}

#### E178 · Simplified Disease Activity Index (SDAI)

{
 "name": "Simplified Disease Activity Index",
 "acronym": "SDAI",
 "subcategory": "rheumatoid arthritis activity",
 "purpose": "Composite RA disease activity index similar to CDAI but includes CRP. Slightly more robust than CDAI due to inclusion of acute phase reactant.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Tender Joint Count (TJC28)",
   "description": "Number of tender joints out of 28",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–28",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw count"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Swollen Joint Count (SJC28)",
   "description": "Number of swollen joints out of 28",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–28",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw count"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Patient Global Assessment (VAS)",
   "description": "Patient global assessment (0–10 cm)",
   "unit": "cm",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw value"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Physician Global Assessment (VAS)",
   "description": "Physician global assessment (0–10 cm)",
   "unit": "cm",
   "range_or_options": "0–10",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw value"
  },
  {
   "variable": "CRP (mg/dL)",
   "description": "C-reactive protein in mg/dL",
   "unit": "mg/dL",
   "range_or_options": "0–10+",
   "points_or_coefficient": "raw value (mg/dL)"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "SDAI = TJC28 + SJC28 + Patient Global (0–10) + Physician Global (0–10) + CRP (mg/dL)",
 "score_range": "0–86",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "≤3.3",
   "meaning": "Remission"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3.4–11.0",
   "meaning": "Low disease activity"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "11.1–26.0",
   "meaning": "Moderate disease activity"
  },
  {
   "score_range": ">26.0",
   "meaning": "High disease activity"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "RA patients from clinical trials and observational cohorts",
 "original_citation": "Smolen JS, Breedveld FC, Schiff MH, et al. A simplified disease activity index for rheumatoid arthritis for use in clinical practice. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2003;42(2):244-257. PMID: 12595618",
 "additional_validation": "Aletaha D, Smolen JS. Arthritis Rheum. 2005;52:1749-1759",
 "limitations": "Requires CRP measurement — though simple, adds one more lab test compared to CDAI. CRP units must be in mg/dL for formula (conversion needed if reported in mg/L).  "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic tool",

### rheumatoid arthritis classification

#### E179 · ACR/EULAR 2010 Rheumatoid Arthritis Classification Criteria (ACR/EULAR 2010)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L11626–L11649 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "ACR/EULAR 2010 Rheumatoid Arthritis Classification Criteria",
 "acronym": "ACR/EULAR 2010",
 "subcategory": "rheumatoid arthritis classification",
 "purpose": "Classification criteria for rheumatoid arthritis designed for early identification of patients with RA who would benefit from early DMARD therapy. Replaced 1987 ACR criteria.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Joint involvement",
   "description": "Number and size of involved joints (tender and/or swollen). Large joints: shoulders, elbows, hips, knees, ankles; Small joints: MCP, PIP (2nd–5th), thumb IP, MTP 2–5, wrists; Distal interphalangeal joints, 1st CMC, 1st MTP excluded",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "1 large joint=0, 2–10 large joints=1, 1–3 small joints=2, 4–10 small joints=3, >10 joints (at least 1 small)=5",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Serology",
   "description": "RF and/or anti-CCP (ACPA)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Negative=0, Low-positive (≤3× ULN)=2, High-positive (>3× ULN)=3",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3 (highest of RF or ACPA)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Acute phase reactants",
   "description": "CRP and/or ESR",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Normal CRP and ESR=0, Abnormal CRP or ESR=1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Duration of symptoms",
   "description": "Patient-reported duration of signs/symptoms",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "<6 weeks=0, ≥6 weeks=1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Total = Joint involvement (0–5) + Serology (0–3) + Acute phase (0–1) + Duration (0–1)\nScore ≥6/10 = definite RA classification\nScore <6 = 'undifferentiated' — may evolve to RA",
 "score_range": "0–10",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "≥6/10",
   "meaning": "Classified as definite rheumatoid arthritis (with synovitis in ≥1 joint, no alternative diagnosis)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "<6",
   "meaning": "Does not meet criteria — 'undifferentiated arthritis.' May develop RA over time."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Derivation: 3 early arthritis cohorts (Leiden, Wichita, Kansas City). Validation: 3 additional cohorts. Patients with new-onset inflammatory arthritis.",
 "original_citation": "Aletaha D, Neogi T, Silman AJ, et al. 2010 Rheumatoid arthritis classification criteria: an American College of Rheumatology/European League Against Rheumatism collaborative initiative. Arthritis Rheum. 2010;62(9):2569-2581. PMID: 20872595",
 "additional_validation": "Berglin E, et al. Arthritis Res Ther. 2011;13:R198; Brito-Zerón P, et al. Rheumatology. 2014",
 "limitations": "Classification criteria, not diagnostic criteria — designed for research to identify homogeneous RA populations. Requires exclusion of alternative diagnoses. Joint involvement assessment requires clinical examination. Serology (RF, ACPA) may take time to result. Duration threshold of 6 weeks is arbitrary. Some RA patients (seronegative with few joints) may not meet threshold. Not validated in established RA — only early arthritis. Specificity in non-rheumatology settings unknown.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published jointly by ACR and EULAR",
 "confidence": "high"
}

#### E181 · British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Index 2004 (BILAG-2004)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L11511–L11540 · parse: clean -->

{
 "name": "British Isles Lupus Assessment Group Index 2004",
 "acronym": "BILAG-2004",
 "subcategory": "systemic lupus erythematosus activity",
 "purpose": "Organ-specific disease activity index for SLE that grades each system from A (severe activity) to E (never affected). Unlike SLEDAI, captures improvement and worsening within systems. Preferred by some for treatment decision-making.",

   "variable": "General",
   "description": "Constitutional symptoms: fever, weight loss, lymphadenopathy, fatigue",
   "unit": "ordinal",

   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Mucocutaneous",
   "description": "Rash, alopecia, mucosal ulcers",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "A–E",
   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Neurological",
   "description": "CNS lupus: seizures, psychosis, cranial neuropathy, myelitis, etc.",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "A–E",
   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Musculoskeletal",
   "description": "Arthritis, myositis",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "A–E",
   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Cardiorespiratory",
   "description": "Serositis, myocarditis, endocarditis, pulmonary hypertension, ILD",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "A–E",
   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Renal",
   "description": "Proteinuria, hematuria, casts, renal function, biopsy class",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "A–E",
   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Vasculitis",
   "description": "Vasculitic lesions, DVT, PE, thrombosis attributed to vasculitis (not APS alone)",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "A–E",
   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hematology",
   "description": "Thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, hemolytic anemia, PTT prolongation",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "A–E",
   "points_or_coefficient": "A=9, B=3, C=1, D=0, E=0"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Each of 8 systems scored independently: A (9), B (3), C (1), D (0), E (0)\nTotal BILAG-2004 = sum of 8 system scores (0–72)\nScoring based on treatment decision approach:\n- A = Severe activity requiring steroids/cytotoxics\n- B = Moderate activity requiring steroids/antimalarials/NSAIDs\n- C = Mild activity requiring no treatment change\n- D = Previously active, improving\n- E = System never affected by SLE",
 "score_range": "0–72 (numerical sum); individual systems: A/B/C/D/E",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Any system A",
   "meaning": "Severe activity in that organ — typically requires systemic corticosteroids and/or immunosuppression"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Any system B",
   "meaning": "Moderate activity — requires treatment increase or close monitoring"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Only C/D/E",
   "meaning": "Mild or inactive disease — may maintain current therapy"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Numerical total",
   "meaning": "Higher total = more global activity; A=9 scoring means any 'A' system dominates total"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "SLE patients from multiple UK and international cohorts. BILAG-2004 replaced original BILAG-1988.",
 "original_citation": "Isenberg DA, Rahman A, Allen E, et al. BILAG 2004. Development and initial validation of an updated version of the British Isles Lupus Assessment Group's disease activity index for patients with systemic lupus erythematosus. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2005;44(7):902-906. PMID: 15814579",
 "additional_validation": "Yee CS, et al. Rheumatology. 2011;50:367-372; Stoll T, et al. J Rheumatol. 2013",
 "limitations": "Complex scoring — requires trained assessor reviewing detailed organ-specific definitions for each of 8 systems. Treatment-based decision approach (A = treat aggressively) may differ between centers. Some organ systems overlap (vasculitis vs. general). D grade (improving) captures response but may not reflect current activity. Training materials available but learning curve is steeper than SLEDAI. No widely agreed-upon numerical cut-offs for remission/flares.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — University College London",
 "confidence": "high"
}

  },

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "≥4 criteria (with ≥1 clinical AND ≥1 immunologic)"
  }
 ],

 "interpretation": [

   "score_range": "≥4 criteria (≥1 clinical + ≥1 immunologic)",
   "meaning": "Classified as SLE"

  }
 ],

 "input_variables": [

  },
  {

   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Blood pressure",
   "description": "SBP <90 mmHg or DBP ≤60 mmHg",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"

  {

   "unit": "boolean",

   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CRB-65 = Confusion(1) + RR≥30(1) + BP_low(1) + Age≥65(1)",
 "score_range": "0–4",

   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "Low risk (<1% mortality). Consider home management."

  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Derived from BTS guidelines and multiple European CAP cohorts",

{
 "name": "Pneumonia Severity Index / PORT Score",

 "acronym": "Garden Classification",

  }
 ],
 "formula": "Garden Type I: Incomplete fracture (valgus impacted)\nGarden Type II: Complete fracture without displacement\nGarden Type III: Complete fracture with partial displacement (distal fragment externally rotated)\nGarden Type IV: Complete fracture with full displacement (fragments not in contact)",
 "score_range": "I–IV",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "I",
   "meaning": "Incomplete/valgus impacted — generally stable, good prognosis. Internal fixation (cannulated screws or sliding hip screw). AVN risk ~10%."
  },

   "score_range": "II",
   "meaning": "Complete but undisplaced — internal fixation. AVN risk ~15%."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "III",

  },

  }
 ],

Radiograph quality significantly affects classification accuracy. Does not account for patient age, bone quality, or functional status.",

 "limitations": "Guidelines, not a validated numerical score. Subject to interpretation and clinical judgment. 2017 revision changed recommendations significantly from 2005 version. Does not fully account for ground-glass component growth rate. Different from Lung-RADS (screening context). Patient preference and comorbidity should influence decisions.",

{
 "name": "STOP-BANG Questionnaire",
 "acronym": "STOP-BANG",

 "purpose": "Screens for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) risk in surgical and general populations.",
 "input_variables": [
  {

   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {

   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "BMI >35 kg/m²",
   "description": "Body mass index over 35",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Age >50 years",
   "description": "Age over 50",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Neck circumference >40 cm",
   "description": "Neck circumference >40 cm (16 inches)",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Male sex",
   "description": "Male sex",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "STOP-BANG = Snoring(1) + Tired(1) + Observed_apnea(1) + Pressure_HTN(1) + BMI>35(1) + Age>50(1) + Neck>40cm(1) + Male(1)",
 "score_range": "0–8",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–2",
   "meaning": "Low risk of OSA (AHI <5: sensitivity 34–70%)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3–4",
   "meaning": "Intermediate risk (AHI ≥5: sensitivity 70–88%)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5–8",

  }
 ],

 "original_citation": "Chung F, Yegneswaran B, Liao P, et al. STOP questionnaire: a tool to screen patients for obstructive sleep apnea. Anesthesiology. 2008;108(5):812-821. PMID: 18431116; Chung F, et al. Anesthesiology. 2012;116:895-904 (STOP-BANG)",
 "additional_validation": "Nagappa M, et al. Can J Anaesth. 2015;62:251-264 (meta-analysis); Chiu HY, et al. J Clin Sleep Med. 2017;13:453-463",
 "limitations": "Sensitivity varies by AHI threshold — good for ruling out severe OSA but may miss moderate OSA. Specificity is modest (many false positives in surgical populations). Age >50 and male sex are non-modifiable risk factors that increase score in many surgical patients. Does not replace polysomnography for diagnosis. BMI cutoff >35 may be too high for Asian populations (>25–30 may be more appropriate).",

#### E197 · Gustilo-Anderson Classification of Open Fractures (Gustilo-Anderson)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L11802–L11828 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Gustilo-Anderson Classification of Open Fractures",
 "acronym": "Gustilo-Anderson",
 "subcategory": "open fracture severity",
 "purpose": "Classification of open (compound) fractures based on wound size, soft tissue injury, contamination, and fracture pattern. Guides antibiotic selection, surgical debridement urgency, and predicts infection risk.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Wound size",
   "description": "Size of the open wound communicating with the fracture",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "<1 cm, 1–10 cm, >10 cm",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Grade I, II, III respectively"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Soft tissue damage",
   "description": "Degree of soft tissue injury, periosteal stripping, and muscle damage",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Minimal, Moderate, Severe/Extensive",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Grade I, II, III"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Contamination",
   "description": "Degree of contamination with dirt, debris, foreign bodies",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Clean, Moderate, Heavy",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Higher grade with more contamination"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Vascular injury",
   "description": "Arterial injury requiring repair",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Automatic Type IIIC if present"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Type I: Wound <1 cm, minimal soft tissue injury, clean, low-energy fracture\nType II: Wound 1–10 cm, moderate soft tissue damage, moderate contamination\nType IIIA: Wound >10 cm, extensive soft tissue damage but adequate bone coverage (may be closed), high-energy mechanism, segmental/comminuted fracture\nType IIIB: Wound >10 cm, extensive soft tissue loss with periosteal stripping, bone exposed, requires flap coverage\nType IIIC: Any open fracture with arterial injury requiring repair",
 "score_range": "I, II, IIIA, IIIB, IIIC",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "I",
   "meaning": "Infection risk ~2%. Cefazolin (first-gen cephalosporin). Debridement and irrigation, primary closure possible."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "II",
   "meaning": "Infection risk ~5%. Cefazolin. Debridement, irrigation, delayed primary closure."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IIIA",
   "meaning": "Infection risk ~10%. Cefazolin + aminoglycoside. Aggressive debridement, soft tissue coverage within 72 hours."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IIIB",
   "meaning": "Infection risk ~20–50%. Cefazolin + aminoglycoside. Aggressive debridement, requires flap coverage (muscle or rotational flap)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IIIC",
   "meaning": "Infection risk ~25–50%, amputation risk ~50%. Cefazolin + aminoglycoside + penicillin (or clindamycin for clostridial coverage). Vascular repair required. High amputation rate."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally described by Gustilo and Anderson in 1976, expanded by Gustilo, Mendoza, and Williams in 1984. Used worldwide for >40 years.",
 "original_citation": "Gustilo RB, Anderson JT. Prevention of infection in the treatment of 1,025 open fractures of long bones. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1976;58(4):453-458. PMID: 773941; Gustilo RB, Mendoza RM, Williams DN. Problems in the management of type III (severe) open fractures. J Trauma. 1984;24(8):742-746. PMID: 6471139",
 "additional_validation": "Bowen TR, Widmaier JC. Injury. 2005;36:1159-1164; Kim PH, Leopold SS. Clin Orthop Relat Res. 2012",
 "limitations": "Classification typically performed in operating room (final determination during surgery, not in ED). Interobserver reliability moderate (particularly II vs. IIIA, and IIIA vs. IIIB). Does not account for mechanism of injury, contamination time, or patient factors (diabetes, immunosuppression). Wound size alone doesn't capture underlying muscle/soft tissue viability. Retrograde contamination (through muscle) may be underestimated. Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS) may be more useful for amputation decisions in IIIC injuries. Does not guide fixation method.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic classification",
 "confidence": "high"
}

{
 "name": "European Society of Cardiology Risk Stratification for PE (2019)",
 "acronym": "ESC PE Risk / sPESI+Biomarkers",
 "subcategory": "pulmonary embolism",
 "purpose": "Stepwise algorithm integrating clinical risk (sPESI), cardiac biomarkers (troponin, BNP), and imaging (RV dysfunction) to classify PE into low, intermediate-low, intermediate-high, and high risk.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "sPESI score",
   "description": "Simplified Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (clinical risk)",
   "unit": "points",
   "range_or_options": "0–6",
   "points_or_coefficient": "see sPESI entry"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Cardiac biomarkers",
   "description": "Troponin (I or T) and/or BNP/NT-proBNP",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Elevated or normal",
   "points_or_coefficient": "positive = worse prognosis"
  },
  {
   "variable": "RV dysfunction on imaging",
   "description": "Echocardiographic or CTPA evidence of RV dysfunction",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "present = worse prognosis"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Hemodynamic status",
   "description": "Hypotension or shock",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "SBP <90 for ≥15 min or vasopressors",
   "points_or_coefficient": "defines high risk"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Stepwise algorithm:\n1. Hemodynamically unstable = High risk → reperfusion (systemic thrombolysis/surgery/catheter-directed therapy)\n2. Hemodynamically stable: compute sPESI. sPESI = 0 = low risk → consider early discharge/home treatment. sPESI ≥1 = intermediate risk → check biomarkers and imaging.\n3. Intermediate risk: Both biomarkers negative = intermediate-low risk → consider early discharge. Biomarker(s) positive = intermediate-high risk → monitor closely in HDU.\n4. RV dysfunction + elevated biomarkers = intermediate-high risk.",
 "score_range": "Categorical: high / intermediate-high / intermediate-low / low",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "High risk (hemodynamic instability)",
   "meaning": "Immediate reperfusion therapy. Mortality >25%."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Intermediate-high (sPESI ≥1 + RV dysfunction + elevated biomarkers)",
   "meaning": "Monitor in HDU. Consider escalation if deterioration. Mortality ~5–10%."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Intermediate-low (sPESI ≥1 + normal biomarkers OR negative imaging)",
   "meaning": "Hospital ward monitoring. Can consider early discharge if stable."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Low risk (sPESI = 0)",
   "meaning": "Outpatient management or early discharge. Mortality <1%."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Multiple international PE registries and prospective studies",
 "original_citation": "Konstantinides SV, Meyer G, Becattini C, et al. 2019 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J. 2020;41(4):543-603. PMID: 31504429",
 "additional_validation": "Becattini C, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2016;67:736-744 (HESTIA criteria complement); Dentali F, et al. Thromb Haemost. 2010;104:978-983",
 "limitations": "Algorithm, not a simple numerical score. Requires multiple steps and data points. Biomarker thresholds vary by assay. RV imaging assessment varies by modality and reader. Hemodynamic criteria may be difficult to capture precisely (sustained hypotension vs transient). Not all intermediate-high risk patients need reperfusion — clinical judgment essential.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic guideline",

}

{

  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "No osteoarthritis"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1",
   "meaning": "Doubtful OA — possible early changes"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "2",
   "meaning": "Mild OA — definite osteophytes, minimal JSN"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3",
   "meaning": "Moderate OA — definite JSN, osteophytes, sclerosis"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4",
   "meaning": "Severe OA — near bone-on-bone, large osteophytes, deformity"
  }

Grade 2 (definite osteophytes but 'possible JSN') is particularly problematic — combines patients with osteophytes-only and those with JSN. ### spinal cord injury

#### E201 · ASIA Impairment Scale for Spinal Cord Injury (AIS)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L11944–L11970 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "ASIA Impairment Scale for Spinal Cord Injury",
 "acronym": "AIS",
 "subcategory": "spinal cord injury",
 "purpose": "International standard for neurological classification of spinal cord injury. Grades severity of injury, determines level of injury, and predicts functional outcomes. Published by the American Spinal Injury Association (ASIA) and International Spinal Cord Society (ISCoS).",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Motor examination (key muscles)",
   "description": "5 key upper extremity muscles (C5-T1) and 5 key lower extremity muscles (L2-S1) graded 0–5 bilaterally. C5: elbow flexors, C6: wrist extensors, C7: elbow extensors, C8: finger flexors (FDP to middle finger), T1: finger abductors (ADM). L2: hip flexors, L3: knee extensors, L4: ankle dorsiflexors, L5: long toe extensors, S1: ankle plantar flexors",
   "unit": "MRC grade",
   "range_or_options": "0–5 per muscle (0=total paralysis, 5=normal)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–50 upper, 0–50 lower"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Sensory examination",
   "description": "Light touch and pin prick at 28 dermatomes (C2-S4-5) bilaterally. Each scored 0 (absent), 1 (impaired), 2 (normal). S4-5 deep anal pressure assessed as present/absent.",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0, 1, 2 per dermatome bilaterally",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–112 per modality (224 total sensory)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Deep anal pressure (DAP)",
   "description": "Sensation of deep anal pressure — determines motor/sensory completeness",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Key determinant of completeness"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Voluntary anal contraction (VAC)",
   "description": "Ability to voluntarily contract anal sphincter",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Key determinant of motor completeness"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Neurological Level of Injury (NLI): Most caudal level with normal motor AND sensory function bilaterally\n\nAIS Grade:\nA (Complete): No motor or sensory function in S4-S5 (no DAP, no VAC)\nB (Sensory Incomplete): Sensory but not motor function below NLI including S4-S5 (DAP present, no VAC)\nC (Motor Incomplete): Motor function preserved below NLI, >half key muscles below NLI have grade <3 (VAC may or may not be present)\nD (Motor Incomplete): Motor function preserved below NLI, at least half key muscles below NLI grade ≥3\nE (Normal): Normal motor and sensory examination (typically used for recovered patients)\n\nZone of Partial Preservation: Dermatomes/myotomes caudal to NLI that are partially innervated (AIS A only)\n\nMotor Level: Most caudal key muscle with grade ≥3, provided all segments above have grade 5\nSensory Level: Most caudal dermatome with normal (2/2) light touch AND pin prick",
 "score_range": "AIS A, B, C, D, E",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "AIS A",
   "meaning": "Complete injury — no motor or sensory function in S4-S5. <5% chance of walking recovery at 1 year. High risk of complications (UTI, pressure ulcers, autonomic dysreflexia)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "AIS B",
   "meaning": "Sensory incomplete — sensory preserved at S4-5 but no motor. ~33% chance of walking recovery at 1 year."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "AIS C",
   "meaning": "Motor incomplete — motor function preserved below NLI, majority of muscles below <3/5. Walking possible with braces/aids. ~75% may achieve ambulation with assistive devices."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "AIS D",
   "meaning": "Motor incomplete — majority of muscles below NLI grade ≥3/5. Most will walk independently. Good prognosis for functional recovery."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "AIS E",
   "meaning": "Normal neurological exam. Used when documenting recovery."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "ASIA standards established 1982, revised multiple times (most recent ISNCSCI revision 2019). Used in >10,000 studies worldwide. National Spinal Cord Injury Database, EMSCI, Rick Hansen SCI Registry.",
 "original_citation": "American Spinal Injury Association. Standards for Neurological Classification of Spinal Cord Injury. Revised 2019. Kirshblum SC, et al. J Spinal Cord Med. 2011;34(6):535-546 (ISNCSCI); Kirshblum SN, et al. Spinal Cord. 2014;52:65-70 (revision)",
 "additional_validation": "Fawcett JW, et al. Spinal Cord. 2007;45:190-205; Steeves JD, et al. Spinal Cord. 2007;45:206-221; van Middendorp JJ, et al. PLoS Med. 2011 (prediction models)",
 "limitations": "Requires standardized examination protocol — training required. Spinal shock may mask true injury severity in acute period (ASIA exam should be repeated after resolution). Cognitive impairment, pain, or sedation may limit cooperation. Motor examination only covers specific key muscles — doesn't capture all motor function. Zone of partial preservation (in complete injuries) may influence prognosis. Does not capture autonomic function (use ISAFSCI — International Standards for Autonomic Assessment). Doesn't account for cause of injury, imaging findings, or comorbidities.",
 "copyright_status": "ASIA — free for clinical use with proper attribution",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

 "validation_population": "Expert panel consensus with clinical validation in >1,000 thoracolumbar injury patients",
 "original_citation": "Vaccaro AR, Lehman RA Jr, Hurlbert RJ, et al. A new classification of thoracolumbar injuries: the importance of injury morphology, the integrity of the posterior ligamentous complex, and neurologic status. Spine. 2005;30(20):2325-2333. PMID: 16227897",
 "additional_validation": "Patel AA, et al. Spine. 2008;33:2651-2658; Joaquim AF, et al. Spine J. 2014;14:2671-2677",
 "limitations": "Validated primarily for T11-L2 injuries — may not apply equally to thoracic (T1-T10) or lumbar (L3-L5) fractures. PLC integrity assessment can be difficult on CT (MRI preferred). Morphology categorization can be ambiguous for burst + distraction combination injuries. Doesn't account for patient age, bone quality (osteoporosis), or mechanism. Translation/rotation and distraction are specific and may be missed on initial imaging. Doesn't guide specific surgical approach (anterior vs. posterior vs. combined). Some authors advocate for sub-classifications not captured by TLICS.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic tool",
 "confidence": "high"
}

 ],

{
 "name": "CAGE Questionnaire",

 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "C: Cut down",

   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0 or 1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "A: Annoyed",
   "description": "Have people annoyed you by criticizing your drinking?",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0 or 1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "G: Guilty",
   "description": "Have you ever felt bad or guilty about your drinking?",

   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0 or 1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "E: Eye-opener",
   "description": "Have you ever had a drink first thing in the morning to steady nerves or get rid of a hangover?",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0 or 1"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CAGE = Number of 'Yes' answers (0–4)",
 "score_range": "0–4",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–1",
   "meaning": "Low likelihood of alcohol dependence (but 1 may warrant further inquiry)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥2",
   "meaning": "Positive screen for alcohol use disorder. Sensitivity 43–94%, specificity 70–96% at this threshold."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥2 lifetime 'Yes' (ever)",
   "meaning": "More sensitive than past-year questions"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥3",
   "meaning": "Strongly suggestive of alcohol dependence"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally validated in general hospital patients. Used in >3,000 studies across medical, surgical, psychiatric, and community settings.",
 "original_citation": "Ewing JA. Detecting alcoholism: the CAGE questionnaire. JAMA. 1984;252(14):1905-1907. PMID: 6471323",
 "additional_validation": "Dhalla S, Kopec JA. J Stud Alcohol Drugs. 2007;68:311-320; Dhalla S, et al. J Gen Intern Med. 2009",
 "limitations": "Screening tool only — doesn't assess severity, quantity, or frequency. Binary yes/no doesn't capture nuance. Lower sensitivity for hazardous drinking (not just dependence). Questions are 'ever' — may detect past problems rather than current drinking. Doesn't distinguish between current and historical alcohol problems. Cultural sensitivity varies. Lower sensitivity in women, elderly, and non-white populations. Being 'annoyed by criticism' (A) may be less specific — could relate to other issues. Superseded by AUDIT and AUDIT-C for most screening purposes. Gender-neutral questions may miss gender-specific patterns of alcohol misuse.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic tool",

}

  },

  },

   "range_or_options": "0–1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1"

  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Over 20,000 studies. Validated in millions of patients across >100 languages. Original validation in 206 patients (Folstein et al., 1975).",
 "original_citation": "Folstein MF, Folstein SE, McHugh PR. 'Mini-mental state'. A practical method for grading the cognitive state of patients for the clinician. J Psychiatr Res. 1975;12(3):189-198. PMID: 1202204",

#### E207 · Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12266–L12296 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Montreal Cognitive Assessment",
 "acronym": "MoCA",
 "subcategory": "cognitive screening",
 "purpose": "Brief 30-point clinician-administered cognitive screening test designed to detect mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and early dementia. More sensitive than MMSE for MCI, with better executive function and attention assessment.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Visuospatial/Executive (5 points)",
   "description": "Trail-making test (alternating numbers and letters), cube copy, clock drawing",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–5",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 per correct element"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Naming (3 points)",
   "description": "Name lion, rhinoceros, camel from pictures",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–3",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 per correct naming"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Memory (0 points, but tested for recall)",
   "description": "5-word immediate and delayed recall (2 trials + delayed recall). Scored on recall section below.",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–5 recall",
   "points_or_coefficient": "See recall below"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Attention (6 points)",
   "description": "Forward/backward digit span, tapping on letter A (list read aloud), serial 7 subtraction",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–6",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Various"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Language (3 points)",
   "description": "Repeat 2 sentences, fluency (name ≥11 words beginning with F in 1 minute)",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–3",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 per sentence, 1 for fluency ≥11"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Abstraction (2 points)",
   "description": "Similarities (e.g., train-bicycle = transportation; watch-ruler = measuring instrument)",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 per correct pair"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Delayed Recall (5 points)",
   "description": "Recall the 5 words from earlier (free recall scored, with multiple-choice cue if needed)",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–5",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 per word recalled (no cue)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Orientation (6 points)",
   "description": "Date, month, year, day, place, city",
   "unit": "count",
   "range_or_options": "0–6",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1 per correct"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "MoCA = Visuospatial(5) + Naming(3) + Attention(6) + Language(3) + Abstraction(2) + Recall(5) + Orientation(6) = 30\n+1 point added for ≤12 years of education (maximum score remains 30)",
 "score_range": "0–30",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "≥26",
   "meaning": "Normal cognitive function"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "18–25",
   "meaning": "Mild cognitive impairment"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–17",
   "meaning": "Moderate cognitive impairment"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "<10",
   "meaning": "Severe cognitive impairment"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Education adjustment:",
   "meaning": "+1 point for ≤12 years of education (to reduce false positives in low-education populations)"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Validated in >5,000 studies. Original validation in 94 MCI patients, 93 mild AD patients, and 90 controls.",
 "original_citation": "Nasreddine ZS, Phillips NA, Bédirian V, et al. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment, MoCA: a brief screening tool for mild cognitive impairment. J Am Geriatr Soc. 2005;53(4):695-699. PMID: 15817019",
 "additional_validation": "Rossetti HC, et al. J Gen Intern Med. 2011;26:661-667; Trzepacz PT, et al. Am J Geriatr Psychiatry. 2015",
 "limitations": "Takes ~10 minutes to administer — longer than MMSE. Education bias (partially addressed by +1 adjustment). Not suitable for telephone administration (requires visual/spatial components). Trail-making test and cube copy affected by motor impairment. Cultural and language adaptation needed for different populations. Copyright restrictions (www.mocatest.org — free for clinical use but registration required). May have floor effect in severe dementia. Serial 7s affected by math anxiety. May not be sensitive to very early or preclinical Alzheimer's. Higher false-positive rate in some populations (elderly without cognitive complaints).",
 "copyright_status": "Ziad Nasreddine — free for clinical and research use with registration at mocatest.org",
 "confidence": "high"
}

### psychiatric illness severity and improvement

#### E211 · Clinical Global Impression (CGI)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12324–L12347 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Clinical Global Impression",
 "acronym": "CGI",
 "subcategory": "psychiatric illness severity and improvement",
 "purpose": "Brief clinician-rated global assessment of psychiatric illness severity (CGI-S) and change from baseline (CGI-I). Widely used in psychiatric clinical trials as a reference standard for measuring treatment response.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "CGI-Severity (CGI-S)",
   "description": "Considering your total clinical experience with this particular population, how mentally ill is this patient at this time?",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "1=Normal, not at all ill, 2=Borderline mentally ill, 3=Mildly ill, 4=Moderately ill, 5=Markedly ill, 6=Severely ill, 7=Among the most extremely ill",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–7"
  },
  {
   "variable": "CGI-Improvement (CGI-I)",
   "description": "Compared to the patient's condition at admission/start of treatment, how much has the patient changed?",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "1=Very much improved, 2=Much improved, 3=Minimally improved, 4=No change, 5=Minimally worse, 6=Much worse, 7=Very much worse",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–7"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CGI-S: Single-item clinician rating 1–7\nCGI-I: Single-item clinician rating 1–7\n\nClinical utility index: CGI-S × CGI-I (used in some analyses)\nResponse commonly defined as CGI-I ≤2 (much or very much improved)",
 "score_range": "CGI-S: 1–7; CGI-I: 1–7",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "CGI-S",
   "meaning": "1=Normal, 2=Borderline, 3=Mild, 4=Moderate, 5=Marked, 6=Severe, 7=Extreme illness"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "CGI-I 1–2",
   "meaning": "Much or very much improved — treatment response"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "CGI-I 3",
   "meaning": "Minimally improved — partial response"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "CGI-I 4–7",
   "meaning": "No change to much worse — treatment non-response"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Used in >5,000 psychiatric clinical trials. Originally developed for NIMH psychopharmacology research.",
 "original_citation": "Guy W (ed). ECDEU Assessment Manual for Psychopharmacology — Revised. DHEW Pub. No. (ADM) 76-338. Rockville, MD: NIMH, 1976. Pages 218-222",
 "additional_validation": "Kadouri A, et al. Int Clin Psychopharmacol. 2007;22:273-278; Busner J, Targum SD. Psychiatry. 2007;4:28-37",
 "limitations": "Single-item measure — may not capture all aspects of illness. Clinician-rated — subjective and depends on assessor experience. Lacks specificity — doesn't identify which symptoms are changing. Anchor definitions rely on clinician's 'total clinical experience' with the population — varies by clinician. CGI-I requires comparison to baseline — different from absolute severity. No patient perspective incorporated. Inter-rater reliability moderate (ICC 0.65–0.80). Doesn't differentiate between domains (e.g., mood vs. anxiety vs. psychosis). Sensitive to expectation bias (clinician may rate improvement based on knowledge of treatment assignment).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — NIMH tool",
 "confidence": "high"
}

 "additional_validation": "Laughon SK, et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol. 2011;204:335.e1-335.e7 (validation of modified Bishop); Crane JM. J Reprod Med. 2006",
 "limitations": "Subjective — interobserver variability is significant, particularly for effacement, station, and consistency. Doesn't account for parity, gestational age, or fetal weight. Original described in low-risk nulliparous women — validation in modern populations limited. Modified Bishop (assigning 0–3 to each category equally) is most commonly used but not the original. Digital examination may be unreliable in obese patients. Doesn't predict cesarean delivery rate directly. Station assessment may vary depending on engagement vs. head position.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic tool",
 "confidence": "high"
}

#### E214 · APGAR Score (APGAR)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12378–L12405 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L6579, L12378) · merged naming variants: Modified APGAR Score -->
```json
{
 "name": "APGAR Score",
 "acronym": "APGAR",
 "subcategory": "neonatal assessment",
 "purpose": "Rapid standardized assessment of newborn status at 1 and 5 minutes after birth. Guides need for resuscitation and predicts neonatal outcomes. APGAR is also a backronym: Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, Respiration.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Appearance (skin color)",
   "description": "Color of newborn",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Blue/pale all over=0, Body pink/extremities blue=1, Completely pink=2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Pulse (heart rate)",
   "description": "Newborn heart rate",
   "unit": "bpm",
   "range_or_options": "Absent=0, <100 bpm=1, ≥100 bpm=2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Grimace (reflex irritability)",
   "description": "Response to stimulation (nasal catheter, foot slap)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "No response=0, Grimace/weak response=1, Cry/cough/sneeze=2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Activity (muscle tone)",
   "description": "Limb flexion and activity",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Limp/flaccid=0, Some flexion=1, Active motion=2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Respiration",
   "description": "Breathing effort",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Absent=0, Irregular/weak cry=1, Strong cry/regular breathing=2",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "APGAR = Appearance (0–2) + Pulse (0–2) + Grimace (0–2) + Activity (0–2) + Respiration (0–2)\nScored at 1 minute and 5 minutes after birth\nIf 5-minute score <7, repeat every 5 minutes up to 20 minutes",
 "score_range": "0–10",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "7–10",
   "meaning": "Normal newborn transition — no intervention needed"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4–6",
   "meaning": "Moderately depressed — may need stimulation, suctioning, oxygen, or positive-pressure ventilation"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "0–3",
   "meaning": "Severely depressed — immediate resuscitation (intubation, medications, chest compressions)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1-minute <7, 5-minute ≥7",
   "meaning": "Good recovery — common and generally favorable prognosis"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5-minute <7 persisting to 10–20 min",
   "meaning": "Associated with increased risk of neurological morbidity and neonatal mortality"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Used universally since 1953 in all delivery settings worldwide. Trillions of newborns assessed.",
 "original_citation": "Apgar V. A proposal for a new method of evaluation of the newborn infant. Curr Res Anesth Analg. 1953;32(4):260-267. PMID: 13083014",
 "additional_validation": "Casey BM, et al. N Engl J Med. 2001;344:467-471; Iliodromiti S, et al. BMJ. 2014;349:g5782",
 "limitations": "Subjective — interobserver variability. APGAR affected by gestational age (preterm infants score lower), maternal medications (sedatives, anesthetics), and resuscitation interventions performed before scoring. Not designed to predict long-term neurological outcomes. A low score at 1 minute is common and not necessarily pathological. 5-minute score has better prognostic value. Doesn't guide specific resuscitation steps (NRP algorithm more useful). Not a substitute for blood gas analysis or clinical assessment of neonatal well-being. Score 7 doesn't distinguish between well-perfused and mildly compromised infants.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — named after Virginia Apgar, Anesthesiologist",

}

{
 "name": "Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale",
 "acronym": "EPDS",
 "subcategory": "postpartum depression screening",
 "purpose": "10-item self-report questionnaire specifically designed to screen for postnatal depression in the first year after delivery. Avoids somatic symptoms that overlap with normal postpartum experiences.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "10 items about feelings in the past 7 days",
   "description": "Each item scored 0–3 based on frequency. Items: able to laugh, enjoyment, self-blame, anxiety/worry, fear/panic, things getting on top, difficulty sleeping (sadness), feeling sad/miserable, crying, self-harm thoughts",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0=No, not at all to 3=Yes, most of the time (for most items; some items reversed)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3 per item"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "EPDS = Sum of 10 items (each 0–3)\nMaximum = 30\nSome items are reverse-scored\nItem 10 (self-harm thoughts) scored: 0=Never, 1=Hardly ever, 2=Sometimes, 3=Yes, quite often",
 "score_range": "0–30",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<10",
   "meaning": "Depression unlikely — standard postnatal care"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–12",
   "meaning": "Possible depression — repeat in 2 weeks, clinical assessment if persistent"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥13",
   "meaning": "Probable depression — clinical interview recommended, consider treatment referral"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Item 10 >0",
   "meaning": "Any endorsement of self-harm thoughts requires immediate further assessment regardless of total score"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally validated in 84 postpartum women in Edinburgh. Used in >6,000 studies in >60 languages across postpartum and antenatal settings.",
 "original_citation": "Cox JL, Holden JM, Sagovsky R. Detection of postnatal depression: development of the 10-item Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale. Br J Psychiatry. 1987;150:782-786. PMID: 3651732",
 "additional_validation": "Levis B, et al. JAMA. 2020;323:1517-1528; Gibson J, et al. BJOG. 2009 (antenatal use)",
 "limitations": "Screening tool, not diagnostic — positive screen requires clinical interview. Self-reported — may underreport symptoms due to stigma, fear of judgment, or normalization of symptoms. May miss atypical presentations of postpartum depression (anger, irritability, bonding difficulties). Somatic items excluded by design — but may miss depression primarily presenting with somatic symptoms. Threshold score debated (10, 11, 12, or 13 used in different studies). Doesn't distinguish postpartum depression from postpartum psychosis or anxiety disorders. Cultural variation in symptom expression. Not validated in antenatal populations (though used antenatally in practice). Doesn't assess social support, history of mental illness, or psychosocial risk factors.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic tool by Cox JL",
 "confidence": "high"
}

{
 "name": "VBAC Success Prediction (Grobman Calculator)",

 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Maternal age",

  {

   "unit": "kg/m²",
   "range_or_options": "15–60+",

  },
  {

   "description": "Self-reported race/ethnicity",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "African American, Hispanic, White, Asian, Other",
   "points_or_coefficient": "categorical covariate (note: ethically debated)"

  },
  {
   "variable": "Indication for prior cesarean",
   "description": "Reason for index cesarean (arrest of dilation, arrest of descent, non-reassuring fetal status, other)",
   "unit": "categorical",

   "points_or_coefficient": "arrest disorders decrease success probability"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Preterm delivery",
   "description": "Gestational age at delivery <37 weeks",
   "unit": "boolean",
   "range_or_options": "Yes/No",
   "points_or_coefficient": "preterm increases success probability"
  }
 ],

 "score_range": "0–100% (estimated probability of VBAC success)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "≥70%",
   "meaning": "High probability of VBAC success — TOLAC reasonable option"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "50–69%",
   "meaning": "Moderate probability — shared decision-making, consider individual factors"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "<50%",
   "meaning": "Low probability — elective repeat cesarean may be preferred, but not absolute contraindication to TOLAC"
  },
  {

  }
 ],

 "original_citation": "Grobman WA, Lai Y, Landon MB, et al. Development of a nomogram for prediction of vaginal birth after cesarean delivery. Obstet Gynecol. 2007;109(4):806-812. PMID: 17400840",

Doesn't include factors like cervical status at admission, estimated fetal weight, indication for repeat cesarean, or interdelivery interval. Accuracy moderate (AUC ~0.75) — not highly discriminatory. External validation shows overestimation in some populations. Should inform but not replace clinical judgment and patient preferences.  ],

### surgical risk prediction

#### E219 · Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity (POSSUM / P-POSSUM)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12487–L12510 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Physiological and Operative Severity Score for the enUmeration of Mortality and Morbidity",
 "acronym": "POSSUM / P-POSSUM",
 "subcategory": "surgical risk prediction",
 "purpose": "Comprehensive risk prediction model for surgical morbidity and mortality incorporating both patient physiological parameters and operative severity. P-POSSUM is Portsmouth modification calibrated for mortality prediction.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Physiological Score (12 variables)",
   "description": "Age, cardiac signs, respiratory signs, ECG, systolic BP, pulse rate, Glasgow Coma Score, Hb, WBC, urea, sodium, potassium",
   "unit": "various",
   "range_or_options": "1–8 per variable",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Each scored 1, 2, 4, or 8"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Operative Severity Score (6 variables)",
   "description": "Operative severity, number of procedures, blood loss, peritoneal contamination, malignancy status, timing (elective/urgent/emergency)",
   "unit": "various",
   "range_or_options": "1–8 per variable",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Each scored 1, 2, 4, or 8"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Physiological Score (PS) = sum of 12 physiological variables (each 1, 2, 4, or 8)\nOperative Severity Score (OS) = sum of 6 operative variables (each 1, 2, 4, or 8)\n\nPOSSUM Morbidity: ln(R/(1-R)) = -5.91 + (0.16 × PS) + (0.19 × OS)\nP-POSSUM Mortality: ln(R/(1-R)) = -9.065 + (0.1692 × PS) + (0.1550 × OS)\nwhere R = predicted risk",
 "score_range": "PS: 12–88; OS: 6–48; R: 0–100%",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Predicted mortality",
   "meaning": "Calculated from regression equation — R value represents percentage mortality risk"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "POSSUM morbidity equation",
   "meaning": "Predicts overall complication rate including minor and major complications"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Low risk (PS + OS)",
   "meaning": "Low predicted mortality — standard perioperative care"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "High risk (PS + OS)",
   "meaning": "Elevated predicted mortality — enhanced monitoring, HDU/ICU planning, shared decision-making"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally validated in >10,000 general surgical patients. P-POSSUM (Portsmouth modification) calibrated in >15,000 patients. Used in >3,000 studies.",
 "original_citation": "Copeland GP, Jones D, Walters M. POSSUM: a scoring system for surgical audit. Br J Surg. 1991;78(3):355-360. PMID: 2021854; Whiteley MS, et al. Br J Surg. 1996;83:391-394 (P-POSSUM)",
 "additional_validation": "Prytherch DR, et al. Br J Surg. 1998;85:1090-1096; Neary WD, et al. Br J Surg. 2003;90:1385-1391 (V-POSSUM for vascular)",
 "limitations": "Requires 18 variables — complex data collection. Operative variables only available postoperatively (limits preoperative use). POSSUM overpredicts mortality in low-risk patients (P-POSSUM corrects this). Doesn't predict specific complications (only overall morbidity). Validated primarily in general/vascular surgery — accuracy varies by specialty. Physiological variables may change rapidly (e.g., pre-op resuscitation). Emergency surgery has highest weight but lowest accuracy. Doesn't capture surgical skill, hospital volume, or process quality.",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic tool",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

## C.18 — Toxicology / Poisoning (2 entries)


### acetaminophen overdose

#### E222 · Rumack-Matthew Nomogram for Acetaminophen Toxicity (Rumack-Matthew)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12667–L12691 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Rumack-Matthew Nomogram for Acetaminophen Toxicity",
 "acronym": "Rumack-Matthew",
 "subcategory": "acetaminophen overdose",
 "purpose": "Treatment nomogram used to determine which patients with acute acetaminophen (paracetamol) overdose require N-acetylcysteine (NAC) treatment based on serum acetaminophen level plotted against time from ingestion.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Serum acetaminophen level",
   "description": "Serum acetaminophen concentration drawn at least 4 hours post-ingestion",
   "unit": "µg/mL or µmol/L",
   "range_or_options": "Variable",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Plotted on nomogram"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Time from ingestion",
   "description": "Exact time from acute single ingestion to blood draw",
   "unit": "hours",
   "range_or_options": "4–24 hours",
   "points_or_coefficient": "X-axis of nomogram"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Treatment line (original): Connects 200 µg/mL at 4 hours to 50 µg/mL at 16 hours (semilogarithmic plot)\n\nTreatment line (Matthew modification): Connects 150 µg/mL at 4 hours to 37.5 µg/mL at 16 hours (used in USA, most centers)\n\nAbove treatment line at time point → NAC indicated\nBelow treatment line → NAC not indicated (in acute single ingestion with reliable history)\n\nKey conversion: 200 µg/mL = 1320 µmol/L; 150 µg/mL = 990 µmol/L",
 "score_range": "Above line (treat) vs. Below line (observe)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Above treatment line",
   "meaning": "NAC treatment indicated — initiate NAC protocol (21-hour IV protocol or 72-hour oral protocol). Risk of hepatotoxicity ~60% without treatment."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Below treatment line",
   "meaning": "NAC not indicated (in acute single ingestion with known time). Risk of hepatotoxicity minimal. Discharge if clinically well."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Unknown time or staggered ingestion",
   "meaning": "Nomogram NOT applicable — treat with NAC empirically and check acetaminophen level, LFTs"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Time >24 hours post-ingestion",
   "meaning": "Nomogram NOT applicable — treat based on clinical status (ALT, INR, acetaminophen level)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Modified Rumack-Matthew (UK)",
   "meaning": "UK uses 100-line (treatment line starting at 100 µg/mL at 4 hours) — more conservative"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Derived from >10,000 acetaminophen overdose cases. Validated in >50 years of clinical use worldwide. Most extensively validated toxicology nomogram.",
 "original_citation": "Rumack BH, Matthew H. Acetaminophen poisoning and toxicity. Pediatrics. 1975;55(6):871-876. PMID: 1134884; Rumack BH. Pediatrics. 1978;62(5 Pt 2 Suppl):898-903",
 "additional_validation": "Dart RC, et al. J Toxicol Clin Toxicol. 2003;41:711-719; Daly FF, et al. Med J Aust. 2008;188:296-301",
 "limitations": "Only valid for acute single ingestion with known exact time — not applicable for staggered/chronic ingestion. Requires serum level drawn at least 4 hours post-ingestion (earlier levels may be falsely reassuring). Time of ingestion must be reliably known — unreliable history makes nomogram unusable. High-risk patients (chronic alcoholism, malnutrition, enzyme inducers, fasting) may be at risk below the treatment line — some guidelines recommend treating these populations at lower thresholds. Does not account for co-ingestants (particularly those that delay absorption). Late presentation (>24 hours) requires clinical assessment rather than nomogram. Different treatment lines used internationally (150-line in US vs. 100-line in UK/Australia) — don't interchange.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic nomogram",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```

  }

Doesn't quantify severity — grading system (mild/moderate/severe) is separate. May be difficult to distinguish from NMS (different mechanism) in patients on antipsychotics AND serotonergic agents. Cyproheptadine (5-HT antagonist) effectiveness is based on case reports only — no RCTs. Doesn't guide specific treatment decisions beyond stopping serotonergic agents. ### burn fluid resuscitation

#### E224 · Parkland Formula for Burn Fluid Resuscitation (Parkland Formula)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12746–L12769 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Parkland Formula for Burn Fluid Resuscitation",
 "acronym": "Parkland Formula",
 "subcategory": "burn fluid resuscitation",
 "purpose": "Estimates crystalloid fluid requirements in the first 24 hours after major burn injury. Guides initial fluid management to prevent burn shock.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Body weight",
   "description": "Patient's weight in kilograms (pre-burn weight if possible)",
   "unit": "kg",
   "range_or_options": "Any",
   "points_or_coefficient": "continuous"
  },
  {
   "variable": "%TBSA burned",
   "description": "Percentage total body surface area of 2nd and 3rd degree burns (Rule of 9s or Lund-Browder)",
   "unit": "percent",
   "range_or_options": "1–100%",
   "points_or_coefficient": "continuous"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Total fluid in first 24 hours = 4 mL × body weight (kg) × %TBSA burned\n\nTiming:\n- First 8 hours (from time of injury, not from presentation): give 50% of total\n- Next 16 hours: give remaining 50%\n\nFluid type: Lactated Ringer's (preferred) or normal saline\n\nExample: 70 kg, 40% TBSA → 4 × 70 × 40 = 11,200 mL total → 5,600 mL in first 8 hrs, 5,600 mL in next 16 hrs\n\nNote: This is an ESTIMATE — must be titrated to urine output (target 0.5–1 mL/kg/hr in adults, 1–2 mL/kg/hr in children)",
 "score_range": "Variable (depends on weight and TBSA)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Calculated volume",
   "meaning": "Total 24-hour fluid requirement — 50% in first 8 hours, 50% in next 16 hours (from time of injury)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Urine output target",
   "meaning": "Adults: 0.5–1.0 mL/kg/hr. Children: 1.0–2.0 mL/kg/hr. Adjust fluid rate to maintain UOP."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Inadequate resuscitation",
   "meaning": "UOP <0.5 mL/kg/hr despite calculated fluids — increase rate. Consider escharotomy if circumferential burns."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Excessive resuscitation",
   "meaning": "UOP >1.0 mL/kg/hr — may need to slow fluids. Complications of over-resuscitation: compartment syndrome, ARDS, abdominal compartment syndrome."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally described by Baxter and Shires at Parkland Hospital (Dallas) in 1968. Standard of care in burn resuscitation worldwide since then.",
 "original_citation": "Baxter CR, Shires T. Physiological response to crystalloid resuscitation of severe burns. Ann N Y Acad Sci. 1968;150(3):874-894. PMID: 5246049",
 "additional_validation": "Baxter CR. Probl Gen Surg. 1990;7:450-459; Chung KK, et al. J Trauma. 2010;69:S71-S75 (modified Brooke formula comparison)",
 "limitations": "Overestimates fluid requirements in many patients (up to 50% of patients develop fluid overload). Formula is a starting point — must be titrated to urine output. Doesn't account for inhalation injury (increases fluid requirements 30-50%). Doesn't account for delay in resuscitation, electrical burns (greater internal injury), or patient comorbidities (CHF, CKD). Lactated Ringer's preferred — NS may cause hyperchloremic acidosis. Colloid controversial in first 24 hours (some guidelines add albumin after 12-18 hours). Modified Brooke formula (2 mL × kg × %TBSA) is alternative with similar outcomes. Burn depth estimation affects %TBSA calculation accuracy. Children require different UOP targets and maintenance fluids in addition to resuscitation fluids.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — standard medical knowledge",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```


### burns body surface area

#### E225 · Rule of Nines for Burns (Rule of 9s)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12722–L12744 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Rule of Nines for Burns",
 "acronym": "Rule of 9s",
 "subcategory": "burns body surface area",
 "purpose": "Rapid estimation of total body surface area (TBSA) affected by burns in adults. Used in emergency settings to guide fluid resuscitation (Parkland formula), triage, and transfer decisions.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Body region burned",
   "description": "Percentage of each body region affected by second- and third-degree burns only (superficial/partial-thickness and full-thickness). First-degree burns excluded.",
   "unit": "percent BSA",
   "range_or_options": "Head: 9%, Each arm: 9%, Anterior trunk: 18%, Posterior trunk: 18%, Each leg: 18%, Perineum: 1%",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Multiples of 9%"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Adult Rule of Nines:\nHead & neck = 9%\nEach upper extremity = 9%\nAnterior trunk = 18%\nPosterior trunk = 18%\nEach lower extremity = 18%\nPerineum/external genitalia = 1%\nTotal = 99% (100% with rounding)\n\nTBSA = Σ (region % × fraction burned in that region)\n\nPediatric modification (14 years and younger): Head = 18%, Each leg = 14% (increasing with age toward adult proportions)\n\nQuick check: Patient's palm (including fingers) ≈ 1% TBSA (useful for scattered/irregular burns)",
 "score_range": "0–100% TBSA",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "<10% TBSA (adult)",
   "meaning": "Minor burn — can be managed at experienced burn center if no other factors"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–20% TBSA",
   "meaning": "Moderate burn — requires IV fluid resuscitation (Parkland formula: 4 mL × kg × %TBSA in first 24 hours, half in first 8 hours)"
  },
  {
   "score_range": ">20% TBSA",
   "meaning": "Major burn — requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, burn center transfer. Consider intubation for >40% TBSA."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Special considerations",
   "meaning": "Any full-thickness >5%, burns involving face/hands/feet/genitalia/joints, circumferential burns, inhalation injury, electrical burns, chemical burns — all require burn center referral"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally described by Wallace in 1951 (modification of earlier Berkow formula). Standard of care for burn assessment since the 1950s.",
 "original_citation": "Wallace AB. The exposure treatment of burns. Lancet. 1951;1(6653):501-504. PMID: 14812587",
 "additional_validation": "Berry MG, et al. Burns. 2006;32:718-722; Knaysi GA, et al. Surg Gynecol Obstet. 1968;126:101-104",
 "limitations": "Overestimates TBSA in obese patients. Overestimates in children <14 years (head/leg proportions differ) — use Lund-Browder chart instead. Only applies to 2nd and 3rd degree burns (exclude 1st degree). Rapid estimation is inherently inaccurate — ±5-10% error common. Doesn't capture depth of burn (superficial partial vs. deep partial vs. full thickness). Doesn't account for burn mechanism, patient age, or comorbidities. Lund-Browder chart is more accurate for children and obese adults. Palm method (1% per palm) useful for small scattered burns but inaccurate for large areas.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — taught in all burn/trauma training programs",
 "confidence": "high"
}

{

  }

 "formula": "1 = Very Fit: Robust, active, energetic, motivated, fit. Regularly exercise. Fittest for age.\n2 = Well: No active disease symptoms, less fit than category 1. Occasional vigorous activity.\n3 = Managing Well: Medical problems well-controlled, not regularly active beyond walking.\n4 = Vulnerable: Not dependent on others for daily help but symptoms limit activities. 'Slowed up'.\n5 = Mildly Frail: Need help with high-order IADLs (finances, transportation, heavy housework, medications).\n6 = Moderately Frail: Need help with all outside activities and housekeeping. May need assistance with dressing/bathing.\n7 = Severely Frail: Completely dependent for personal care, stable condition unlikely to deteriorate rapidly.\n8 = Very Severely Frail: Completely dependent, approaching end of life. Could recover from acute illness.\n9 = Terminally Ill: Approaching end of life, not expected to recover from current illness (life expectancy <6 months).",
 "score_range": "1–9",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "1–3",
   "meaning": "Non-frail. Low perioperative risk. Standard surgical/anesthesia approach."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4",
   "meaning": "Vulnerable/pre-frail. Increased risk. Consider prehabilitation."
  },
  {

   "meaning": "Mild-moderate frailty. Higher perioperative morbidity/mortality. Goals-of-care discussion recommended. Consider less invasive approaches."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "7–8",
   "meaning": "Severe-very severe frailty. High perioperative mortality. Consider conservative management. Goals-of-care discussion essential."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "9",
   "meaning": "Terminal illness. Comfort care. Not expected to recover from acute event."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "COVID-19",
   "meaning": "CFS ≥5 associated with significantly higher mortality in COVID-19 patients (used in triage guidelines internationally)"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally developed by Rockwood et al. in 2005. Validated in >100 studies including >500,000 older adults across surgical, medical, and critical care settings.",
 "original_citation": "Rockwood K, Song X, MacKnight C, et al. A global clinical measure of fitness and frailty in elderly people. CMAJ. 2005;173(5):489-495. PMID: 16129869",
 "additional_validation": "Church S, et al. Anaesthesia. 2020;75:932-938 (COVID-19); Bagshaw SM, et al. CMAJ. 2014;186:E57-E65 (ICU); Hewitt J, et al. Lancet. 2019;394:1365-1375 (perioperative)",
 "limitations": "Single-item clinician assessment — subject to inter-rater variability (moderate agreement, kappa ~0.6). Assessment based on patient/caregiver report of baseline function — may be inaccurate. Doesn't capture specific comorbidities, nutritional status, or cognitive impairment directly. Thresholds for treatment decisions not universally agreed upon. CFS 8 ('approaching end of life, could recover') distinction from CFS 7 ('stable, unlikely to deteriorate rapidly') can be subjective. Training materials available but not universally used. Doesn't replace comprehensive geriatric assessment. Validated primarily in older adults — not applicable to younger populations. 2-week baseline assessment may be difficult to determine in acute admissions.",
 "copyright_status": "Canadian Geriatrics Society — free for clinical use with proper attribution",

 "formula": "Grade 0: Fully active, able to carry on all pre-disease performance without restriction\nGrade 1: Restricted in physically strenuous activity but ambulatory and able to carry out work of a light or sedentary nature\nGrade 2: Ambulatory and capable of all self-care but unable to carry out any work activities; up and about more than 50% of waking hours\nGrade 3: Capable of only limited self-care; confined to bed or chair more than 50% of waking hours\nGrade 4: Completely disabled; cannot carry out any self-care; totally confined to bed or chair\nGrade 5: Dead",
 "score_range": "0–5",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "Fully active — eligible for all treatments including clinical trials"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1",
   "meaning": "Restricted strenuous activity — usually eligible for most treatments"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "2",
   "meaning": "Ambulatory, self-care, no work — may be eligible for some treatments depending on cancer type"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3",
   "meaning": "Limited self-care — most oncologists avoid cytotoxic chemotherapy. Focus shifts to palliative approaches."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4",
   "meaning": "Completely disabled — palliative/comfort care"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≥2",
   "meaning": "Generally associated with worse prognosis across most cancer types"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally described by Zubrod et al. in 1960. Standard performance status measure used in >30,000 oncology clinical trials.",
 "original_citation": "Zubrod CG, Schneiderman M, Frei E, et al. Appraisal of methods for the study of chemotherapy of cancer in man: comparative therapeutic trial of nitrogen mustard and triethylene thiophosphoramide. J Chronic Dis. 1960;11:7-33; Oken MM, et al. Am J Clin Oncol. 1982;5:649-655",
 "additional_validation": "Jang RW, et al. J Clin Oncol. 2010;28:2582-2588; West HJ, Jin JO. JAMA Oncol. 2015;1:99-100",
 "limitations": "Clinician-assessed — subject to inter-rater variability. Simple but may miss nuances (ECOG 2 includes a wide range of function). Binary thresholds between grades may not capture gradual decline. Patient and clinician assessments frequently disagree. Doesn't capture cognitive impairment, symptom burden, or psychological status. Cancer-specific — may not generalize to non-oncology populations. Doesn't predict treatment toxicity directly. Preference for ECOG vs. KPS varies by institution and clinical trial.",
