#### E228 · Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12772–L12796 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L9067, L12772) · merged naming variants: Karnofsky Performance Status Scale -->
```json
{
 "name": "Karnofsky Performance Status",
 "acronym": "KPS",
 "subcategory": "functional status / oncology",
 "purpose": "Clinician-assessed measure of functional status and ability to perform activities of daily living. Used in oncology to assess prognosis, guide treatment decisions (e.g., chemotherapy eligibility), and assess palliative care needs.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Functional capacity",
   "description": "Clinician assessment of patient's ability to carry on normal activity and perform self-care",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (dead) to 100 (normal, no complaints) in 10-point intervals",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–100"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "100: Normal, no complaints, no evidence of disease\n90: Able to carry on normal activity, minor signs/symptoms\n80: Normal activity with effort, some signs/symptoms\n70: Cares for self, unable to carry on normal activity\n60: Requires occasional assistance, cares for most needs\n50: Requires considerable assistance and frequent medical care\n40: Disabled, requires special care and assistance\n30: Severely disabled, hospitalization indicated\n20: Very sick, hospitalization necessary, active supportive treatment\n10: Moribund, fatal processes progressing rapidly\n0: Dead",
 "score_range": "0–100",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "100–80",
   "meaning": "Able to carry on normal activity. Usually eligible for clinical trials and active treatment."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "70–60",
   "meaning": "Unable to work, can live at home, cares for most personal needs. May still be eligible for some treatments."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "50–40",
   "meaning": "Requires considerable assistance. Palliative care referral recommended. Active treatment benefit-risk must be carefully weighed."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "30–20",
   "meaning": "Hospitalization indicated, severely disabled. Focus on comfort and symptom management."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10",
   "meaning": "Moribund. Comfort care and end-of-life planning."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Prognostic significance",
   "meaning": "KPS <50-60 generally associated with <6-month median survival in advanced cancer (varies by tumor type)"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally described by Karnofsky in 1949 for nitrogen mustard therapy. Used in >50,000 oncology studies. Most widely used performance status tool in oncology.",
 "original_citation": "Karnofsky DA, Burchenal JH. The clinical evaluation of chemotherapeutic agents in cancer. In: MacLeod CM (ed). Evaluation of Chemotherapeutic Agents. New York: Columbia University Press, 1949:191-205",
 "additional_validation": "Mor V, et al. J Chronic Dis. 1984;37:635-643; Yates JW, et al. Cancer. 1980;45:2220-2224",
 "limitations": "Clinician-assessed — subject to observer bias and variability (ICC ~0.6–0.7). 10-point intervals may not capture subtle changes. Ceiling effect (most patients cluster at 60-80). Different assessors may classify the same patient differently. Patient self-assessment often differs from clinician assessment. Not validated for all conditions equally (strongest in oncology). Doesn't capture cognitive function or psychological well-being. Functional status alone may not predict treatment tolerance or toxicity. Superseded in some settings by ECOG (simpler, 6 categories) or Palliative Performance Scale (PPS). Doesn't account for disease-specific symptoms.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic tool",
 "confidence": "high"
}

   "range_or_options": "See PPS levels",

   "range_or_options": "See PPS levels",

  {

   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "See PPS levels",

  },
  {

   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "See PPS levels",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Part of composite level"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "PPS levels: 100%, 90%, 80%, 70%, 60%, 50%, 40%, 30%, 20%, 10%\n\n100%: Normal activity, full ambulation, full self-care, normal intake, full consciousness\n90%: Normal activity with effort, full ambulation, full self-care, normal intake, full consciousness\n80%: Normal activity with effort, full ambulation, full self-care, normal or reduced intake, full consciousness\n70%: Reduced activity, unable to do normal job/work, full ambulation, full self-care, normal or reduced intake, full consciousness\n60%: Reduced activity, unable to do hobby/housework, occasional assistance needed, normal or reduced intake, full consciousness or confusion/drowsy\n50%: Reduced activity, unable to do hobby/housework, considerable assistance needed, normal or reduced intake, full consciousness or confusion/drowsy\n40%: Unable to do most activities, mainly sit/lie, mainly dependent for self-care, reduced or minimal intake, full consciousness or confusion/drowsy\n30%: Unable to do most activities, mainly in bed, mainly dependent, minimal intake, full consciousness or confusion/drowsy\n20%: Unable to do any activity, totally bedbound, totally dependent, mouth care only, full consciousness or confusion/drowsy\n10%: Totally bedbound, totally dependent, mouth care only, full consciousness or confusion or comatose\n0%: Dead",
 "score_range": "0–100%",

  {
   "score_range": "60–40%",
   "meaning": "Requires assistance, disease dominant. Median survival days to weeks."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "30–10%",
   "meaning": "Mainly bedbound, dependent. Median survival days. Focus on comfort care."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "PPS ≤50%",

  }
 ],

 "additional_validation": "Lau F, et al. J Pain Symptom Manage. 2001;22:694-703; Myers J, et al. J Palliat Med. 2008;11:637-642",

Doesn't capture specific symptoms (pain, dyspnea, nausea). Cultural variation in reporting intake and activity. Doesn't incorporate psychological, spiritual, or social domains of palliative care. Validated primarily in cancer populations — may not be as accurate for non-cancer conditions. Cut-off for hospice referral (PPS ≤50%) may be too late for some conditions. {
 "name": "Palliative Prognostic Score",

 "input_variables": [

   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1.5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "KPS",

   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "10-20=2.5, 30-40=1.5, 50-60=0.5, 70-100=0",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2.5"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Clinical prediction of survival (CPS)",
   "description": "Clinician's best estimate of survival",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": ">12 weeks=0, 11-12 weeks=2, 7-10 weeks=2.5, 5-6 weeks=4.5, 3-4 weeks=6, 1-2 weeks=8",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–8"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Total WBC count",
   "description": "White blood cell count",
   "unit": "×10³/µL",
   "range_or_options": "4.8-8.5=0, 8.5-11=0.5, <4.8 or >11=1",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–1"
  },
  {

   "description": "Lymphocyte percentage of total WBC",
   "unit": "percent",
   "range_or_options": "20-40%=0, 12-19.9% or >40%=1, <12%=2.5",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–2.5"
  }
 ],

 "score_range": "0–17",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–5.5",
   "meaning": "Group A: 30-day survival probability >70%. Better prognosis — consider ongoing disease-directed therapy if appropriate."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5.6–11.0",
   "meaning": "Group B: 30-day survival probability 30-70%. Uncertain prognosis — consider best supportive care with possible targeted interventions."
  },

   "meaning": "Group C: 30-day survival probability <30%. Poor prognosis — focus on comfort care, symptom management, end-of-life planning."
  }
 ],

 "original_citation": "Pirovano M, Maltoni M, Nanni O, et al. A new palliative prognostic score: a first step for the staging of terminally ill cancer patients. J Pain Symptom Manage. 1999;17(4):231-239. PMID: 10203875",

Laboratory values (WBC, lymphocytes) may be affected by infection, medications, and cancer treatment. Subjective symptoms (dyspnea, anorexia) vary by reporting. Doesn't capture specific cancer type, treatment history, or molecular markers. Doesn't account for psychosocial or spiritual factors. <!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12962–L12985 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Hurtado Criteria for Q Fever Endocarditis",
 "acronym": "Hurtado Criteria",
 "subcategory": "infective endocarditis (specific pathogen)",
 "purpose": "Diagnostic criteria specifically for Q fever endocarditis caused by Coxiella burnetii. Modified Duke criteria may miss Q fever endocarditis — these criteria incorporate serological testing.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Serology (Phase I IgG)",
   "description": "Anti-Coxiella burnetii Phase I IgG antibody titer",
   "unit": "titer",
   "range_or_options": "≥1:800 by IFA = major criterion",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Major criterion"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Echocardiography",
   "description": "Valve vegetations, abscess, new regurgitation, prosthetic valve dehiscence",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Major criterion if positive"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Clinical features",
   "description": "Fever, new cardiac murmur, embolic phenomena, immunological phenomena (Roth spots, Osler nodes), vascular phenomena",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Various",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Minor criteria"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Diagnosis of Q fever endocarditis:\n1 definite: IgG Phase I ≥1:800 + histological/immunohistochemical evidence of C. burnetii on valve\n1 possible + 1 minor = diagnosis:\n- IgG Phase I ≥1:800 (major) + echocardiogram positive (minor)\n- OR IgG Phase I ≥1:800 + ≥1 minor clinical criterion",
 "score_range": "Definite/Possible/Rejected (criterion-based)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Definite",
   "meaning": "Pathological evidence or IgG Phase I ≥1:800 + positive echo OR IgG ≥1:800 + fever + valve involvement"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Possible",
   "meaning": "IgG Phase I ≥1:800 but insufficient additional criteria"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Rejected",
   "meaning": "Criteria not met or alternative diagnosis established"
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Based on cohort of Q fever endocarditis patients from the French National Reference Center",
 "original_citation": "Hurtado A, Carrion-Nessi F, Buitrago D, et al. Proposed modification of the Duke criteria for the diagnosis of infective endocarditis with Coxiella burnetii. J Infect. 2017;74:485-491; Raoult D, et al. Am J Med. 1991;91:401-405",
 "additional_validation": "Edouard S, et al. Clin Microbiol Infect. 2018",
 "limitations": "Specific to Q fever — not applicable to other causes of endocarditis. Phase I IgG ≥1:800 may not be available in all laboratories. Chronic Q fever serology takes weeks to evolve — early infection may be missed. IgG titer of ≥1:800 may also be present in chronic Q fever without endocarditis. Requires specialized laboratory (serology, PCR). Clinical presentation can be subtle (fever may be absent). Prosthetic valve involvement may be difficult to detect on echo. Treatment requires prolonged antibiotics (doxycycline + hydroxychloroquine for ≥18 months).",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic criteria",
 "confidence": "moderate"
}

<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L12934–L12960 · parse: clean -->

{
 "name": "Modified McGeer Criteria for Infection Surveillance in Long-Term Care",
 "acronym": "McGeer Criteria",
 "subcategory": "long-term care infection surveillance",
 "purpose": "Standardized surveillance definitions for infections in long-term care facilities (LTCF). Revised in 2012 (Stone criteria) to improve specificity and applicability. Used for infection surveillance, outbreak detection, and quality improvement.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "URI criteria",
   "description": "Upper respiratory infection: ≥2 of cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea AND ≤7 days duration",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Specific criteria per infection type",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Criterion-based"
  },
  {
   "variable": "LRI criteria",
   "description": "Lower respiratory infection: ≥3 of cough, new/increased sputum, fever, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, crackles/bronchial breath sounds; OR ≥2 with CXR showing new infiltrate",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Specific criteria",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Criterion-based"
  },
  {
   "variable": "UTI criteria",
   "description": "Urinary tract infection: ≥1 of dysuria, urgency, frequency, suprapubic pain with positive UA; OR ≥2 of fever, new/increased urinary symptoms, costovertebral tenderness, change in mental status with positive UA + significant bacteriuria",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Specific criteria",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Criterion-based"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Skin/soft tissue criteria",
   "description": "Skin infection: purulent drainage or ≥2 of redness, warmth, swelling, tenderness",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Specific criteria",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Criterion-based"
  },
  {
   "variable": "GI illness criteria",
   "description": "Gastrointestinal: ≥2 of diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Specific criteria",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Criterion-based"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Conjunctivitis criteria",
   "description": "Eye redness with mucopurulent drainage",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Specific criteria",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Criterion-based"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "No numerical score — diagnostic criteria met if specific clinical features and laboratory findings are present:\n\nURI: ≥2 of 4 symptoms (cough, sore throat, nasal congestion, rhinorrhea) lasting ≤7 days\nLRI: ≥3 of 6 symptoms; OR ≥2 + CXR infiltrate\nUTI: Complex criteria depending on catheter status; requires positive UA + bacteriuria (≥10⁵ CFU/mL in non-catheterized, ≥10² in catheterized). NOTE: Asymptomatic bacteriuria should NOT be treated.\nSkin/SSTI: Purulence or ≥2 inflammatory signs\nGI: ≥2 GI symptoms\nFever: Temperature >37.8°C (100°F) or >1.1°C above baseline",
 "score_range": "Met/Not Met (criterion-based diagnosis)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Criteria met",
   "meaning": "Surveillance definition of infection satisfied — report for infection surveillance, consider treatment"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Criteria not met",
   "meaning": "Does not meet surveillance definition — clinical judgment still applies"
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Key point",
   "meaning": "Surveillance definitions ≠ clinical diagnosis. Clinicians may treat based on clinical judgment even when surveillance criteria are not met."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally proposed by McGeer in 1991. Revised by Stone et al. in 2012. Validated in >50 long-term care studies.",
 "original_citation": "McGeer A, Campbell B, Emori TG, et al. Definitions of infection for surveillance in long-term care facilities. Am J Infect Control. 1991;19(1):1-7. PMID: 1850575; Stone ND, et al. Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol. 2012;33:965-977 (revised)",
 "additional_validation": "Loeb M, et al. Clin Infect Dis. 2003;36:1140-1145; Juthani-Mehta M, et al. Clin Infect Dis. 2009",
 "limitations": "Designed for surveillance, not clinical diagnosis — may miss early or atypical infections. UTI criteria complicated by asymptomatic bacteriuria (extremely common in LTCF — up to 50% of women). Change in mental status as UTI symptom is controversial and poorly specific. Doesn't capture healthcare-associated or device-associated infections specific to LTCF. Culture data often unavailable in LTCF — criteria require clinical judgment. Staff training needed for reliable application. Different criteria for different infection types — no unified scoring system. May miss infections in patients with communication difficulties (dementia).",
 "copyright_status": "free for clinical use — published academic tool",
 "confidence": "high"
}

### renal mass surgical planning

#### E243 · RENAL Nephrometry Scoring System (R.E.N.A.L.)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13308–L13333 · parse: clean -->

{
 "name": "RENAL Nephrometry Scoring System",
 "acronym": "R.E.N.A.L.",
 "subcategory": "renal mass surgical planning",
 "purpose": "Standardized anatomical scoring system for renal masses to characterize surgical complexity. Predicts likelihood of successful partial nephrectomy vs. need for radical nephrectomy. Facilitates communication among surgeons and comparison across studies.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "R (Radius)",
   "description": "Maximal diameter of the renal mass",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "≤4 cm (1 point), >4 cm and ≤7 cm (2 points), >7 cm (3 points)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "E (Exophytic/endophytic)",
   "description": "Degree of endophytic growth (percentage of mass not exophytic)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "≥50% exophytic (1 point), 50% exophytic (2 points), ≥50% endophytic (3 points)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "N (Nearness to collecting system or sinus)",
   "description": "Closest distance of mass to the collecting system or renal sinus",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "≥7 mm (1 point), 4–7 mm (2 points), ≤4 mm (3 points)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "A (Anterior/posterior)",
   "description": "Location relative to coronal plane of the kidney",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "A (anterior), P (posterior), X (no clear predominance)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Descriptive suffix (not scored)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "L (Location relative to polar lines)",
   "description": "Location of mass relative to the polar lines of the kidney",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Entirely above upper or below lower polar line (1 point), Crosses polar line (2 points), >50% across polar line or crosses axial midline (3 points), Entirely between polar lines (suffix 'h' for hilar, touching renal sinus)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–3 (±suffix)"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "R.E.N.A.L. Score = R + E + N + L (sum of 4 components, range 4–12)\nSuffix: A, P, or X (anterior/posterior)\nSuffix: h (hilar — touching renal sinus, applied to L component)\n\nTotal = R + E + N + L = 4–12\n\nLow complexity: 4–6\nModerate complexity: 7–9\nHigh complexity: 10–12",
 "score_range": "4–12",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "4–6 (Low complexity)",
   "meaning": "Favorable anatomy for partial nephrectomy. High likelihood of successful nephron-sparing surgery. Consider partial nephrectomy as standard approach."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "7–9 (Moderate complexity)",
   "meaning": "Partial nephrectomy feasible but technically more challenging. Experienced surgeon recommended. Discuss risks/benefits of partial vs. radical nephrectomy."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–12 (High complexity)",
   "meaning": "Very challenging partial nephrectomy. Consider radical nephrectomy vs. partial nephrectomy by experienced surgeon. Higher risk of complications (urine leak, hemorrhage, warm ischemia time >25 min)."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Validated across >500 renal mass resections in multiple urology centers. Correlated with operative times, warm ischemia times, and complications.",
 "original_citation": "Kutikov A, Uzzo RG. The R.E.N.A.L. nephrometry score: a comprehensive standardized system for quantitating renal tumor size, location and depth. J Urol. 2009;182(3):844-853. PMID: 19616235",
 "additional_validation": "Waldert M, et al. Eur Urol. 2010;58:674-680; Long JA, et al. BJU Int. 2012;110:1364-1370; Hew MN, et al. Eur Urol. 2015;68:509-515",
 "limitations": "Does not incorporate patient factors (comorbidities, renal function, age, CKD stage). Does not account for tumor histology (oncocytoma vs. RCC — imaging cannot reliably distinguish). 3D anatomy not fully captured (score is 2D-based). Does not predict oncologic outcomes (positive margins, recurrence). Inter-observer variability exists (especially for E and N components). Hilar tumors (suffix h) may be more complex than score suggests. Does not incorporate RENAL component into final number. CT acquisition protocol affects measurement. Does not incorporate tumor growth kinetics or patient preference. Centrally located tumors may be underestimated. Emerging: PADUA score, C-index, DAP score as alternative systems.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic scoring system",
 "confidence": "high"
}

### chronic venous disease classification

#### E245 · Clinical, Etiologic, Anatomic, Pathophysiologic Classification (CEAP)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13420–L13449 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Clinical, Etiologic, Anatomic, Pathophysiologic Classification",
 "acronym": "CEAP",
 "subcategory": "chronic venous disease classification",
 "purpose": "Standardized classification system for chronic venous disorders. Provides comprehensive clinical, etiologic, anatomic, and pathophysiologic description. Used for clinical practice, research standardization, and treatment planning.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Clinical (C)",
   "description": "Clinical severity based on visible signs",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "C0: No visible signs; C1: Telangiectasias or reticular veins; C2: Varicose veins; C3: Edema; C4: Skin changes (C4a: pigmentation/eczema, C4b: lipodermatosclerosis/atrophie blanche); C5: Healed venous ulcer; C6: Active venous ulcer",
   "points_or_coefficient": "C0–C6"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Etiologic (E)",
   "description": "Cause of venous disease",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Ec: Congenital; Ep: Primary; Es: Secondary (post-thrombotic); En: No venous cause identified",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Ec/Ep/Es/En"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Anatomic (A)",
   "description": "Anatomic distribution of disease",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "As: Superficial; Ap: Perforator; Ad: Deep; An: No venous location identified",
   "points_or_coefficient": "As/Ap/Ad/An"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Pathophysiologic (P)",
   "description": "Hemodynamic abnormality",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Pr: Reflux; Po: Obstruction; Pr,o: Reflux and obstruction; Pn: No venous pathophysiology identified",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Pr/Po/Pr,o/Pn"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CEAP = C + E + A + P\n\nExample: C6 Ep As,d Pr\n(Active venous ulcer, primary etiology, superficial and deep veins, reflux)\n\nBasic CEAP: Uses only the most relevant descriptor for each component.\nFull CEAP: Uses all applicable descriptors for each component.",
 "score_range": "Multidimensional (C0–C6, E, A, P)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "C0",
   "meaning": "No visible or palpable signs of venous disease. May have symptoms (heavy legs, pain)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C1",
   "meaning": "Telangiectasias/reticular veins. Cosmetic concern. Compression optional."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C2",
   "meaning": "Varicose veins. Consider compression stockings, endovenous ablation, or sclerotherapy if symptomatic."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C3",
   "meaning": "Venous edema. Compression therapy indicated. Investigate deep and superficial venous system."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C4a",
   "meaning": "Skin changes (pigmentation, eczema). Aggressive compression, consider intervention."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C4b",
   "meaning": "Lipodermatosclerosis/atrophie blanche. Advanced disease. Compression + specialist referral."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C5",
   "meaning": "Healed venous ulcer. Lifelong compression to prevent recurrence."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C6",
   "meaning": "Active venous ulcer. Multimodal wound care + compression + venous intervention."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "International consensus by American Venous Forum and Union Internationale de Phlébologie. Updated in 2004 and 2020. Used in >2,000 published studies.",
 "original_citation": "Eklöf B, Rutherford RB, Bergan JJ, et al. Revision of the CEAP classification for chronic venous disorders: consensus statement. J Vasc Surg. 2004;40(6):1248-1252. PMID: 15622385; Lurie F, et al. J Vasc Surg Venous Lymphat Disord. 2020;8:152-160",
 "additional_validation": "Meissner MH, et al. J Vasc Surg. 2007;45:1055-1064; Rabe E, et al. Phlebology. 2018;33:128-144",
 "limitations": "CEAP is descriptive — it does not directly guide treatment decisions. Requires detailed clinical assessment including duplex ultrasound for accurate classification. C2 (varicose veins) is highly prevalent and heterogeneous — wide range of severity. C classification is ordinal but not linear (difference between C1→C2 ≠ C5→C6). Does not incorporate patient-reported outcomes (use VCSS, VEINES-QOL). Anatomic classification requires imaging (duplex ultrasound). Does not predict response to treatment. Primary vs. secondary etiology distinction not always clear. Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS) is more suitable for tracking treatment outcomes. Not validated in pediatric venous disease. Doesn't address pelvic venous insufficiency (may cause C2-C3 without lower extremity disease).",
 "copyright_status": "American Venous Forum — free for clinical and academic use",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```


### chronic venous disease severity tracking

#### E246 · Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13489–L13521 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Venous Clinical Severity Score",
 "acronym": "VCSS",
 "subcategory": "chronic venous disease severity tracking",
 "purpose": "Clinician-assessed severity scoring system for chronic venous disease. Designed to track changes over time and assess treatment response. Complements CEAP classification (which is static and descriptive) by providing a dynamic, quantifiable measure.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Pain",
   "description": "Venous-related pain",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (none), 1 (occasional, not restricting activity), 2 (daily, limiting some activities), 3 (daily, limiting most activities, requiring chronic analgesics)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Varicose veins",
   "description": "Size and extent of varicose veins",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (none), 1 (few scattered), 2 (multiple, involving below-knee GSV), 3 (extensive, above and below knee)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Venous edema",
   "description": "Presence of venous edema",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (none), 1 (foot/ankle only), 2 (below knee), 3 (above knee or involving entire leg)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Skin pigmentation",
   "description": "Extent of hyperpigmentation",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (none), 1 (limited to perimalleolar area), 2 (diffuse, lower third of calf), 3 (extensive, above lower third of calf)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Inflammation",
   "description": "Eczema, cellulitis related to venous disease",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (none), 1 (limited to perimalleolar area), 2 (diffuse, lower third of calf), 3 (extensive, above lower third of calf)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Skin induration",
   "description": "Lipodermatosclerosis, atrophie blanche",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (none), 1 (limited to perimalleolar area), 2 (diffuse, lower third of calf), 3 (extensive, above lower third of calf)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Active ulcers",
   "description": "Number and duration of active ulcers",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (none), 1 (1 ulcer &lt;/think&gt;�<1cm, present &lt;/think&gt;�<3 months), 2 (1 ulcer >1cm or 2–3 ulcers, or present 3–12 months), 3 (>3 ulcers or present >12 months)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Ulcer size",
   "description": "Diameter of largest active ulcer",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (no ulcer), 1 (&lt;/think&gt;�<2cm), 2 (2–6cm), 3 (>6cm)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Ulcer duration",
   "description": "Duration of longest active ulcer",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (no ulcer), 1 (&lt;/think&gt;�<3 months), 2 (3–12 months), 3 (>12 months)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Compression therapy",
   "description": "Patient compliance with compression",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "0 (not applicable), 1 (intermittent use), 2 (wears most days), 3 (full compliance with stockings/bandages",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–3"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "VCSS = Sum of all 10 items (each 0–3)\nRange: 0–30",
 "score_range": "0–30",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0–5",
   "meaning": "Mild venous disease."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "6–10",
   "meaning": "Moderate venous disease."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "11–15",
   "meaning": "Severe venous disease."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "16–20",
   "meaning": "Very severe venous disease."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "21–30",
   "meaning": "Extreme venous disease."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Validated in >1,000 patients across multiple venous disease registries and clinical trials",
 "original_citation": "Rutherford RB, Padberg FT, Comerota AJ, et al. Venous severity scoring: an adjunct to venous outcome assessment. J Vasc Surg. 2000;31(6):1307-1312. PMID: 10842165; Vasquez MA, et al. J Vasc Surg. 2010;51:1326-1331 (revised VCSS)",
 "additional_validation": "Passman MA, et al. J Vasc Surg. 2006;44:1041-1047; Marston WA, et al. J Vasc Surg. 2011;53:751-757",
 "limitations": "Clinician-assessed — subject to inter-observer variability. Designed to complement CEAP, not replace it. Requires clinical expertise for accurate scoring. Compression compliance score (item 10) conflates treatment with severity. Pain is subjective. Not validated as a standalone diagnostic tool. Sensitivity to change may be insufficient for small differences (floor/ceiling effects). Not validated for superficial venous disease alone (designed for deep and superficial). May overestimate severity in patients with concomitant arterial disease. Not validated for pediatric venous disease. Recommended to score at baseline and follow-up (minimum 3-month intervals). Different scoring versions exist (original 2000 vs. revised 2010) — specify which version used.",
 "copyright_status": "American Venous Forum — free for clinical and academic use",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```


### facial nerve function grading

#### E247 · House-Brackmann Facial Nerve Grading System (HB)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13525–L13552 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "House-Brackmann Facial Nerve Grading System",
 "acronym": "HB",
 "subcategory": "facial nerve function grading",
 "purpose": "Standardized grading of facial nerve function, particularly in the context of Bell's palsy, acoustic neuroma surgery, temporal bone trauma, and other facial nerve injuries. Accepted as the standard by the American Academy of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery (AAO-HNS).",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Gross facial function",
   "description": "Overall assessment of facial movement at rest and with effort",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Grade I (normal) through Grade VI (total paralysis)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "I–VI"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Forehead movement",
   "description": "Ability to raise eyebrows, wrinkle forehead",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Normal/weak/absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Component of grading"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Eye closure",
   "description": "Ability to close eye completely",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Complete/with effort/incomplete",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Component of grading"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Mouth symmetry",
   "description": "Symmetry of mouth at rest and with movement (smile, pucker)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Symmetric/asymmetric/gross asymmetry",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Component of grading"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "House-Brackmann Grade:\n\nGrade I: Normal facial function in all areas\nGrade II: Mild dysfunction (slight weakness noticeable on close inspection; slight synkinesis; normal symmetry at rest; forehead — moderate to good function; eye — complete closure with minimal effort; mouth — slight asymmetry)\nGrade III: Moderate dysfunction (obvious but not disfiguring difference between sides; noticeable synkinesis/contracture; normal symmetry at rest; forehead — slight to moderate movement; eye — complete closure with effort; mouth — slightly weak with maximum effort)\nGrade IV: Moderately severe dysfunction (obvious disfiguring weakness; normal symmetry at rest; forehead — no motion; eye — incomplete closure; mouth — asymmetric with maximum effort)\nGrade V: Severe dysfunction (barely perceptible motion; asymmetry at rest; forehead — no motion; eye — incomplete closure; mouth — slight movement)\nGrade VI: Total paralysis (no movement)",
 "score_range": "I–VI",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "I",
   "meaning": "Normal. No intervention needed."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "II",
   "meaning": "Mild dysfunction. Good prognosis. Monitor."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "III",
   "meaning": "Moderate dysfunction. Consider corticosteroids (if Bell's palsy). Prognosis generally good."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IV",
   "meaning": "Moderately severe dysfunction. Corticosteroids ± antivirals. Consider electromyography (EMG) to assess prognosis."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "V",
   "meaning": "Severe dysfunction. Aggressive medical therapy. Consider surgical decompression in select cases."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "VI",
   "meaning": "Total paralysis. Surgical exploration/decompression may be indicated. EMG/ENoG essential."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Adopted by AAO-HNS in 1985. Used universally in facial nerve research and clinical practice. Validated across >10,000 patients with facial nerve disorders.",
 "original_citation": "House JW, Brackmann DE. Facial nerve grading system. Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 1985;93(2):146-147. PMID: 3921901",
 "additional_validation": "Kanerva M, et al. Otol Neurotol. 2008;29:684-689; Lee HY, et al. Clin Exp Otorhinolaryngol. 2015;8:304-308",
 "limitations": "Only 6 grades — relatively coarse scale. May miss subtle changes (especially between grades II and III). Inter-observer variability exists (especially for grades III–V). Does not capture synkinesis severity independently. Does not include specific functional domains (corneal exposure risk, speech/eating difficulty, social impact). Newer systems (Facial Nerve Grading Scale 2.0 — FNGS 2.0, Sydney, Sunnybrook) offer more granularity. Not validated for bilateral facial paralysis. Doesn't capture dynamic changes over time without serial measurements. Subjective assessment — depends on examiner experience. May not detect partial paresis in specific nerve branches. Does not incorporate patient-reported quality of life. Some patients with HB Grade III have significant functional impairment (incomplete eye closure) that is underweighted.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic grading system",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```


### hearing aid outcome measurement

#### E248 · Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit (APHAB)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13609–L13636 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit",
 "acronym": "APHAB",
 "subcategory": "hearing aid outcome measurement",
 "purpose": "Patient-reported questionnaire measuring hearing aid benefit across four listening situations. Used to quantify benefit from hearing aid fitting in clinical practice and research. Assesses both unaided and aided difficulty.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "24 items across 4 subscales",
   "description": "Each item rated on a 7-point scale (1=always, 7=never) for unaided and aided conditions",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "1 (always a problem) to 7 (never a problem)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Percent scores for each subscale"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Ease of communication (EC)",
   "description": "Communication in favorable listening conditions (6 items)",
   "unit": "percent",
   "range_or_options": "0–100% difficulty",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Subscale score"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Reverberation (RV)",
   "description": "Listening in reverberant environments (6 items)",
   "unit": "percent",
   "range_or_options": "0–100% difficulty",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Subscale score"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Background noise (BN)",
   "description": "Listening in background noise (6 items)",
   "unit": "percent",
   "range_or_options": "0–100% difficulty",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Subscale score"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Aversiveness of sounds (AV)",
   "description": "Negative reactions to environmental sounds (6 items)",
   "unit": "percent",
   "range_or_options": "0–100% difficulty",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Subscale score"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "For each subscale:\nScore = (Mean of 6 items - 1) / 6 × 100\n\nBenefit = Unaided score - Aided score (for EC, RV, BN only — AV excluded from benefit calculation)\n\nGlobal benefit = Mean of EC, RV, and BN benefit scores\n\nMCID for benefit: ≥5 percentage points",
 "score_range": "0–100% difficulty per subscale; benefit = unaided – aided",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Benefit >10%",
   "meaning": "Substantial hearing aid benefit. Successful fitting."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Benefit 5–10%",
   "meaning": "Moderate benefit. Clinically meaningful improvement."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Benefit &lt;/think&gt;�<5%",
   "meaning": "Minimal benefit. May need adjustment of hearing aid programming or counseling."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Aided EC/RV/BN >50%",
   "meaning": "Persistent difficulty even with hearing aid. Consider alternative technology or aural rehabilitation."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "AV aided >50%",
   "meaning": "Sounds are too loud/uncomfortable. May need compression adjustment or loudness discomfort management."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Validated in >1,500 hearing aid users across multiple clinical settings",
 "original_citation": "Cox RM, Alexander GC. The Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit. Ear Hear. 1995;16(2):176-186. PMID: 7789673",
 "additional_validation": "Cox RM, et al. Am J Audiol. 2016;25:238-244; Humes LE, et al. Ear Hear. 2017;38:466-477",
 "limitations": "Patient-reported — subjective. Does not measure speech intelligibility directly. AV subscale cannot be used for benefit calculation (different direction). Does not capture directional microphone benefit or noise reduction algorithms specifically. Self-report bias (social desirability, expectation). Not validated for cochlear implant outcomes. Does not capture all listening situations (e.g., music appreciation, telephone). Different versions exist (APHAB-1995 vs. updated). Not validated in all languages. May be affected by cognitive status of respondent. Does not account for unilateral vs. bilateral hearing aid benefit separately.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — freely available for clinical and research use",
 "confidence": "high"
}

### hearing classification in vestibular schwannoma

#### E249 · AAO-HNS Hearing Classification for Acoustic Neuroma (AAO-HNS Class)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13582–L13606 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "AAO-HNS Hearing Classification for Acoustic Neuroma",
 "acronym": "AAO-HNS Class",
 "subcategory": "hearing classification in vestibular schwannoma",
 "purpose": "Standardized hearing classification system for reporting hearing outcomes in patients with vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma). Classifies hearing based on pure-tone average (PTA) and speech discrimination score (SDS).",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Pure-tone average (PTA)",
   "description": "Average of air conduction thresholds at 500, 1000, 2000, and 3000 Hz",
   "unit": "dB HL",
   "range_or_options": "Continuous (typically 0–120 dB HL)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Component of classification"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Speech discrimination score (SDS)",
   "description": "Percentage of words correctly identified at suprathreshold levels",
   "unit": "%",
   "range_or_options": "0–100%",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Component of classification"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "AAO-HNS Hearing Class:\n\nClass A: PTA ≤30 dB AND SDS ≥70%\nClass B: PTA >30 dB and ≤50 dB AND SDS ≥50%\nClass C: PTA ≥50 dB AND SDS ≥50%\nClass D: PTA any level AND SDS &lt;/think&gt;�<50%\nClass E: No measurable hearing (dead ear)",
 "score_range": "A, B, C, D, E",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "A",
   "meaning": "Good hearing. Serviceable hearing preserved."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "B",
   "meaning": "Useful hearing. Serviceable hearing preserved."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "C",
   "meaning": "Non-serviceable hearing (can detect speech but poor discrimination). Hearing preservation not expected."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "D",
   "meaning": "Non-serviceable hearing. Poor speech understanding."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "E",
   "meaning": "Dead ear. No functional hearing."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Adopted by AAO-HNS in 1995. Used universally in vestibular schwannoma surgery and radiosurgery outcome reporting.",
 "original_citation": "Committee on Hearing and Equilibrium. Committee on Hearing and Equilibrium guidelines for the evaluation of hearing preservation in acoustic neuroma (vestibular schwannoma). Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg. 1995;113(3):179-180. PMID: 7675485",
 "additional_validation": "Kanzaki J, et al. Skull Base Surg. 2003;13:51-57; Stangerup SE, et al. Otol Neurotol. 2008;29:382-386",
 "limitations": "Does not capture tinnitus, aural fullness, or vestibular symptoms. Uses 3000 Hz in PTA calculation (less commonly tested than 4000 Hz). Class A and B together represent 'serviceable' hearing — class C–E is 'non-serviceable.' Class C may have useful hearing for some patients (heterogeneous group). Does not incorporate patient-reported hearing handicap. No distinction between class D and E functionally (both non-serviceable). SDS testing methodology varies (word lists, presentation levels). Doesn't capture bimodal hearing or cochlear implant candidacy. Newer systems (Gardner-Robertson, Tokyo, AAO-HNS 2012 update) exist but AAO-HNS remains most widely used. Not validated for other causes of hearing loss.",
 "copyright_status": "AAO-HNS — free for clinical use",
 "confidence": "high"
}
```


### peripheral arterial disease screening and severity

#### E250 · Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13337–L13364 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Ankle-Brachial Index",
 "acronym": "ABI",
 "subcategory": "peripheral arterial disease screening and severity",
 "purpose": "Non-invasive measurement of lower extremity arterial perfusion relative to upper extremity blood pressure. Used for diagnosis and severity assessment of peripheral arterial disease (PAD). ABI = systolic BP at ankle / systolic BP at arm (higher of two arms).",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Right ankle systolic BP",
   "description": "Higher of dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial artery systolic BP measured by Doppler",
   "unit": "mmHg",
   "range_or_options": "Continuous (typically 50–250 mmHg)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Numerator right"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Left ankle systolic BP",
   "description": "Higher of dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial artery systolic BP measured by Doppler",
   "unit": "mmHg",
   "range_or_options": "Continuous (typically 50–250 mmHg)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Numerator left"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Right brachial systolic BP",
   "description": "Systolic BP in right brachial artery measured by Doppler",
   "unit": "mmHg",
   "range_or_options": "Continuous (typically 80–200 mmHg)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Denominator right"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Left brachial systolic BP",
   "description": "Systolic BP in left brachial artery measured by Doppler",
   "unit": "mmHg",
   "range_or_options": "Continuous (typically 80–200 mmHg)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Denominator left"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Right ABI = Higher ankle BP (right) / Higher arm BP\nLeft ABI = Higher ankle BP (left) / Higher arm BP\n\nABI = max(DP systolic, PT systolic) / max(Right brachial, Left brachial)\n\nNote: If ABI >1.40, consider calcification (non-compressible arteries) — perform toe-brachial index (TBI).",
 "score_range": "Continuous (typically 0–1.4+)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": ">1.40",
   "meaning": "Non-compressible arteries (calcification). Consider TBI. Associated with diabetes, CKD, elderly."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1.00–1.40",
   "meaning": "Normal. No PAD."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "0.91–0.99",
   "meaning": "Borderline. Possible PAD — further evaluation with exercise ABI if symptomatic."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "0.41–0.90",
   "meaning": "Mild-to-moderate PAD. Claudication expected."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "0.00–0.40",
   "meaning": "Severe PAD. Critical limb ischemia (CLI) likely. Rest pain, tissue loss."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≤0.40 with tissue loss",
   "meaning": "Rutherford category 5–6 / Fontaine stage IV. Limb-threatening ischemia."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Extensively validated in >100,000 participants across multiple large cohorts (ARIC, MESA, Rotterdam Study, Edinburgh Artery Study)",
 "original_citation": "Aboyans V, et al. 2017 ESC Guidelines on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Peripheral Arterial Diseases. Eur Heart J. 2018;39(9):763-816; AHA/ACC Guidelines on Management of PAD (2016)",
 "additional_validation": "Fowkes FG, et al. Lancet. 2013;382:1329-1340; Ankle Brachial Index Collaboration. JAMA. 2008;299:304-312",
 "limitations": "Falsely elevated ABI (>1.40) in diabetes, CKD, and elderly due to medial calcinosis (non-compressible tibial arteries). Measurement technique-dependent (Doppler probe angle, cuff width). ABI &lt;/think&gt;�<0.90 has high specificity but moderate sensitivity for angiographically significant stenosis. Does not localize level of disease. Exercise ABI more sensitive for mild disease. Toe-brachial index (TBI) better for patients with calcified arteries. Does not distinguish claudication from other causes of leg pain. Bilateral PAD may affect brachial BP (subclavian stenosis). Reproducibility affected by operator experience. Not validated as screening in asymptomatic low-risk populations. ABI has independent prognostic value for cardiovascular events (MI, stroke, CV death). ABI ≤0.90 associated with 2–3x increased cardiovascular mortality. Not applicable to acute limb ischemia (different assessment needed).",
 "copyright_status": "ESC/AHA Guidelines — free for clinical use",

}

### peripheral arterial disease severity

#### E251 · Rutherford Classification of Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia (Rutherford)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13367–L13391 · parse: clean -->
```json
{
 "name": "Rutherford Classification of Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia",
 "acronym": "Rutherford",
 "subcategory": "peripheral arterial disease severity",
 "purpose": "Standardized classification of chronic limb ischemia severity based on clinical symptoms and objective testing. Used alongside Fontaine classification for clinical trial design, treatment decision-making, and outcomes reporting.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Clinical symptoms",
   "description": "Walking ability, rest pain, and tissue loss",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Asymptomatic / Claudication / Ischemic rest pain / Minor tissue loss / Major tissue loss",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Category 0–6"
  },
  {
   "variable": "ABI / objective testing",
   "description": "Ankle systolic pressure, toe pressure, TcPO₂",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Normal / Borderline / Abnormal / Severely abnormal",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Confirms category"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Rutherford Category assigned by clinical presentation:\n\nCategory 0: Asymptomatic (objective PAD confirmed by ABI, duplex, or imaging)\nCategory 1: Mild claudication\nCategory 2: Moderate claudication\nCategory 3: Severe claudication\nCategory 4: Ischemic rest pain (ABI ≤0.40, ankle pressure &lt;/think&gt;�<50 mmHg, toe pressure &lt;/think&gt;�<30 mmHg)\nCategory 5: Minor tissue loss (non-healing ulcer, focal gangrene with diffuse pedal ischemia; ankle pressure &lt;/think&gt;�<60 mmHg, toe pressure &lt;/think&gt;�<40 mmHg)\nCategory 6: Major tissue loss (extending above transmetatarsal level; functional foot no longer salvageable)",
 "score_range": "0–6",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "Asymptomatic PAD. Medical management (antiplatelet, statin, risk factor modification, exercise program)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "1–3",
   "meaning": "Intermittent claudication. Supervised exercise therapy first line. Revascularization if lifestyle-limiting and refractory."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "4",
   "meaning": "Critical limb ischemia (CLI). Rest pain. Urgent revascularization indicated."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "5",
   "meaning": "CLI with minor tissue loss. Urgent revascularization. Wound care."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "6",
   "meaning": "CLI with major tissue loss. Major amputation may be inevitable. Revascularization attempt if any foot salvage possible."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Adopted by Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) and used in all major PAD revascularization trials (BASIL, BEST-CLI, IN.PACT, LEVANT)",
 "original_citation": "Rutherford RB, Baker JD, Ernst C, et al. Recommended standards for reports dealing with lower extremity ischemia: revised version. J Vasc Surg. 1997;26(3):517-538. PMID: 9308598",
 "additional_validation": "Conte MS, et al. J Vasc Surg. 2015;61:33S-61S; Norgren L, et al. J Vasc Surg. 2007;45:S5-S67 (TASC II)",
 "limitations": "Subjective categories for claudication severity (mild, moderate, severe) — not precisely defined. Category assignment may vary between clinicians. Does not incorporate anatomic level of disease (inflow vs. outflow). Fontaine classification is simpler but less granular. Tissue loss assessment requires clinical examination — subjective. Categories 5 and 6 overlap in clinical practice. Not validated for acute limb ischemia (different classification). Does not incorporate wound healing potential (WIfI classification now preferred for predicting outcomes). Revascularization decision depends on anatomy (TASC II) + comorbidities — Rutherford alone insufficient. Doesn't capture patient functional status or frailty. Rutherford 4 (rest pain) vs. 5 (minor tissue loss) distinction can be difficult in neuropathic patients (diabetes).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic classification",
 "confidence": "high"
}

{

   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Stage I (asymptomatic), Stage IIa (mild claudication, >200m), Stage IIb (moderate-severe claudication, ≤200m), Stage III (ischemic rest pain), Stage IV (ulceration/gangrene)",

  }
 ],
 "formula": "Fontaine Classification:\n\nStage I: Asymptomatic\nStage IIa: Intermittent claudication, walking distance >200 meters\nStage IIb: Intermittent claudication, walking distance ≤200 meters\nStage III: Ischemic rest pain (typically nocturnal, relieved by dependency)\nStage IV: Ischemic ulcers or gangrene of the foot/leg",
 "score_range": "I, IIa, IIb, III, IV",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "I",
   "meaning": "Asymptomatic PAD detected incidentally. Medical management."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IIa",
   "meaning": "Mild claudication. Exercise therapy, risk factor modification."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IIb",
   "meaning": "Disabling claudication. Exercise therapy, consider revascularization."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "III",
   "meaning": "Critical limb ischemia (rest pain). Urgent revascularization."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IV",
   "meaning": "Critical limb ischemia (tissue loss). Urgent revascularization, wound care, amputation risk."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Used internationally since 1954. Adopted by ESC, AHA, TASC, and SVS guidelines. Over 500 published studies use Fontaine classification.",
 "original_citation": "Fontaine R, Kim M, Kieny R. Die chirurgische Behandlung der peripheren Durchblutungsstörungen. Helvetica Chirurgica Acta. 1954;21:499-533",
 "additional_validation": "Norgren L, et al. J Vasc Surg. 2007;45:S5-S67 (TASC II); Aboyans V, et al. Eur Heart J. 2018;39:763-816",
 "limitations": "Walking distance is subjective and varies with effort, terrain, and patient motivation. Does not include objective measurements (ABI, toe pressure, TcPO₂). Stage IIa/IIb distinction is imprecise. Does not capture anatomy of disease (aortoiliac vs. femoropopliteal vs. tibial). Less granular than Rutherford classification. Not suitable for clinical trials (Rutherford preferred). Rest pain may be confounded by neuropathy in diabetics. Does not incorporate wound characteristics (WIfI preferred). Does not predict amputation risk. Stage IV is heterogeneous (small toe ulcer vs. extensive gangrene). Cultural and language differences affect interpretation of claudication distance. Bypassing stage III to IV can occur rapidly in some patients.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic classification",

Does not assess libido, ejaculatory dysfunction, or orgasmic function (use full IIEF-15). May underdiagnose ED in men who are not sexually active. Doesn't capture psychological causes vs. organic causes. Cultural sensitivity varies (some patients reluctant to disclose). Not validated for use in homosexual men or with specific populations. Does not differentiate vasculogenic, neurogenic, hormonal, or psychogenic ED. Cutoff scores may vary by population (age, comorbidities). Not suitable for evaluating Peyronie's disease specifically. No assessment of partner satisfaction.",

Doesn't incorporate machine perfusion parameters. Doesn't capture donor BMI-specific metabolic risk. Based on US donor population — may not be generalizable internationally. Percentile shifts annually based on donor pool. Doesn't predict individual kidney survival with certainty — population-level estimate. Some centers use KDPI >85% as 'extended criteria' threshold, but this is center-dependent. Doesn't account for recipient factors (use EPTS for recipient quality matching). Living donor kidneys do not have KDPI — use Living Donor Risk Index separately.",

{
 "name": "Banff Classification of Renal Allograft Pathology",

  },
  {

  },
  {
   "variable": "v (intimal arteritis)",
   "description": "Inflammatory cells in arteriole/artery intima",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "v0 (none), v1 (mild — &lt;/think&gt;�<25% of circumference), v2 (moderate — ≥25% of circumference), v3 (transmural arteritis/fibrinoid necrosis)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "v0–v3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "g (glomerulitis)",
   "description": "Inflammatory cells in glomerular capillaries",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "g0 (&lt;/think&gt;�<10% glomeruli), g1 (mild increase), g2 (moderate increase), g3 (severe increase)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "g0–g3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "ptc (peritubular capillaritis)",
   "description": "Inflammatory cells in peritubular capillaries",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "ptc0 (none), ptc1 (1–5 cells/ptc cross-section), ptc2 (6–10), ptc3 (>10)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "ptc0–ptc3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "C4d staining",
   "description": "Complement C4d deposition in peritubular capillaries by immunofluorescence or immunohistochemistry",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "C4d0 (negative), C4d1 (minimal — &lt;/think&gt;�<10%), C4d2 (focal — 10–50%), C4d3 (diffuse — >50%)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "C4d0–C4d3"
  },
  {

   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "ci0 (&lt;/think&gt;�<5%), ci1 (6–25%), ci2 (26–50%), ci3 (>50%)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "ci0–ci3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "ct (tubular atrophy)",
   "description": "Percentage of tubules that are atrophic",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "ct0 (&lt;/think&gt;�<5%), ct1 (6–25%), ct2 (26–50%), ct3 (>50%)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "ct0–ct3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "cv (vascular fibrous intimal thickening)",
   "description": "Fibrous thickening of arteriole/artery intima",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "cv0 (none), cv1 (mild — &lt;/think&gt;�<25% lumen narrowing), cv2 (moderate — 26–50%), cv3 (severe — >50%)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "cv0–cv3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "ah (arteriolar hyalinosis",
   "description": "Hyaline deposition in arterioles",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "ah0 (none), ah1 (mild), ah2 (moderate), ah3 (severe)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "ah0–ah3"
  },
  {
   "variable": "IFTA score",
   "description": "Combined interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "ci+ct combined: I (≤25%), II (26–50%), III (>50%)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Grade I–III"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Banff 2019 Diagnostic Categories:\n\n1. Normal\n2. Antibody-mediated changes (ABMR):\n   - Active ABMR: g>0 OR ptc>0 + C4d>0 OR molecular markers + DSA\n   - Chronic active ABMR: chronic glomerulopathy + active ABMR features\n   - Chronic (inactive) ABMR: chronic changes + C4d + no activity\n3. T-cell mediated rejection (TCMR):\n   - Borderline changes: i≥1 and/or t≥1 (i0t0 allowed if v>0)\n   - Acute TCMR:\n     IA: i≥2, t≥2 (significant i + moderate t)\n     IB: i≥2, t≥3 (significant i + severe t)\n     IIA: v1 (mild arteritis)\n     IIB: v2 (moderate arteritis)\n     III: v3 (severe transmural arteritis)\n   - Chronic active TCMR: TCMR features + chronic allograft arteriopathy\n4. IFTA (interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy) without specific etiology:\n   Grade I (ci1-2 + ct1-2), Grade II (ci2-3 + ct2), Grade III (ci3 + ct3)\n5. Other: Calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, BK nephropathy, recurrent disease, etc.",
 "score_range": "Categorical diagnostic classification (multiple categories)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "Borderline changes",
   "meaning": "Mild interstitial inflammation ± tubulitis. Consider subclinical rejection vs. other causes. May require treatment or monitoring."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IA (Acute TCMR)",
   "meaning": "Tubulo-interstitial rejection without vasculitis. Treat with pulse steroids."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IB (Acute TCMR)",
   "meaning": "Severe tubulo-interstitial rejection. Treat with pulse steroids, consider anti-thymocyte globulin."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IIA/IIB (Acute TCMR with vasculitis)",
   "meaning": "Arteritis present. Aggressive immunosuppression. Poorer prognosis than IA/IB."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "III (Acute TCMR)",
   "meaning": "Transmural arteritis/fibrinoid necrosis. Very poor prognosis. Aggressive treatment but graft loss common."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "Active ABMR",
   "meaning": "Antibody-mediated rejection. Treat with plasmapheresis, IVIG, rituximab, bortezomib, eculizumab, or complement inhibitors."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IFTA Grade I–III",
   "meaning": "Chronic allograft injury. Irreversible. Optimize remaining nephrons, adjust immunosuppression, manage risk factors."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "International consensus updated biennially. Applied to >100,000 renal transplant biopsies globally. Used in all transplant center registry reporting.",
 "original_citation": "Loupy A, Haas M, Roufosse C, et al. The Banff 2019 Kidney Meeting Report. Am J Transplant. 2020;20(3):587-603. PMID: 31943670; Racusen LC, et al. Kidney Int. 1999;55:713-723",
 "additional_validation": "Haas M, et al. Am J Transplant. 2014;14:2723-2730; Loupy A, et al. Am J Transplant. 2017;17:2766-2775",
 "limitations": "Requires experienced transplant pathologist for accurate scoring. Inter-observer variability exists (especially for i, t, g, ptc scores). C4d-negative ABMR now recognized — C4d alone insufficient. Molecular markers (gene expression, dd-cfDNA) increasingly important but not universally available. Biopsy sampling error (15-gauge needle may miss focal lesions). Category boundaries are somewhat arbitrary. Treatment algorithms based on Banff categories vary by center. Borderline changes management is debated. Chronic changes (IFTA) are irreversible — limited treatment options. Classification evolves with each Banff conference — not static. Some categories overlap. Does not capture recurrence of original disease. Does not fully address combined rejection and infection (e.g., BK + rejection). TCMR vs. ABMR distinction may be artificial (overlap exists).",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — international consensus, free for clinical use",
 "confidence": "high"
}

#### E261 · Full Outline of UnResponsiveness Score (FOUR Score)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L13977–L14004 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L10753, L13977) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Full Outline of UnResponsiveness Score",
 "acronym": "FOUR Score",
 "subcategory": "coma assessment in ICU (intubated patients)",
 "purpose": "Alternative to GCS for assessing level of consciousness in critically ill, intubated patients. Eliminates the verbal component of GCS (which cannot be assessed in intubated patients) and replaces it with brainstem reflexes and respiratory pattern. Developed for ICU use.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Eye response (E)",
   "description": "Eye opening and tracking",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "4 (eyelids open, tracking or blinking to command), 3 (eyelids open but not tracking), 2 (eyelids closed but open to loud voice), 1 (eyelids closed but open to pain), 0 (eyelids remain closed with pain)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Motor response (M)",
   "description": "Motor response to pain",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "4 (thumbs-up, fist, or peace sign to command), 3 (localizing to pain), 2 (flexion response to pain), 1 (extension response to pain), 0 (no response to pain or generalized myoclonus)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Brainstem reflexes (B)",
   "description": "Pupil, corneal, and cough reflexes",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "4 (pupils and corneal reflexes present), 3 (one pupil wide and fixed), 2 (pupils OR corneal reflexes absent), 1 (pupils AND corneal reflexes absent), 0 (absent pupil, corneal, and cough reflex",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Respiration (R)",
   "description": "Respiratory pattern (for intubated patients: breathing over ventilator rate, or triggering ventilator)",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "4 (not intubated, regular breathing), 3 (not intubated, Cheyne-Stokes breathing), 2 (not intubated, breathing irregularly or ataxic), 1 (breathes at ventilator rate or above), 0 (breathes below ventilator rate or apnea)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0–4"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "FOUR Score = E + M + B + R\nRange: 0–16",
 "score_range": "0–16",
 "interpretation": [

{
 "name": "Glasgow Coma Scale",

Originally developed for traumatic brain injury assessment but now used universally in emergency medicine, critical care, neurology, and prehospital care. Provides reproducible measurement of consciousness level for triage, prognostication, and clinical decision-making.",
 "input_variables": [

   "unit": "ordinal",

   "points_or_coefficient": "1–5"
  },
  {

   "description": "Best motor response",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "6 (obeys commands), 5 (localizes pain), 4 (withdrawal/flexion), 3 (abnormal flexion), 2 (extension), 1 (none)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–6"
  }
 ],

 "score_range": "3–15",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "15",
   "meaning": "Fully alert and oriented."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "13–14",

  },
  {
   "score_range": "9–12",
   "meaning": "Moderate brain injury. Requires close monitoring. CT imaging indicated."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3–8",
   "meaning": "Severe brain injury. Coma. Intubation usually indicated (GCS ≤8 = 'intubate'). Airway management critical."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "3",
   "meaning": "Deep coma/unresponsive. Most severe possible. Poor prognosis."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Used universally since 1974. Applied in >50,000 publications. Used in all major TBI guidelines (Brain Trauma Foundation, NICE, SIGN).",
 "original_citation": "Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness. A practical scale. Lancet. 1974;2(7872):81-84. PMID: 4136544; Teasdale G, Jennett B. Acta Neurochir Suppl (Wien). 1979;28:13-16",

Does not assess pupil reactivity, brainstem reflexes, or focal neurological deficits. Not validated in children &lt;/think&gt;�<2 years (use Pediatric GCS or AVPU). Confounded by sedation, paralysis, intoxication, intubation. Does not capture specific injury patterns (focal vs. diffuse). The FOUR Score is preferred in ICU for intubated patients (separates eye and motor responses from verbal). GCS 3 (minimum) is a category, not a single value (heterogeneous). Should be supplemented with pupil reactivity for prognostication. Not suitable for chronic consciousness assessment (use JFK Coma Recovery Scale). 15-point scale may have gaps (GCS 14 patients are heterogeneous). {

   "unit": "binary/ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "Normal (both arms move equally or not at all), Abnormal (one arm drifts down or does not move)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0 or 1"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Speech",
   "description": "Have patient repeat 'You can't teach an old dog new tricks.' Assess for slurred or inappropriate speech.",
   "unit": "binary/ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "Normal (clear speech with correct words), Abnormal (slurred speech, wrong words, or unable to speak)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "0 or 1"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CPSS = Number of abnormal findings (0–3)\nEach abnormal finding = 1 point",
 "score_range": "0–3",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "0",
   "meaning": "No stroke signs identified. Low probability of stroke. Continue assessment."
  },
  {

   "meaning": "Possible stroke. 72% probability of stroke diagnosis. Activate stroke protocol and transport to stroke center."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "2",

  },
  {

  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Derived from NIHSS data by Kothari et al. Validated in >1,500 prehospital and ED patients.",

 "additional_validation": "Kidwell CS, et al. JAMA. 2000;284:2078-2082; Bray JE, et al. Stroke. 2010;41:1869-1873",
 "limitations": "Screening tool only — does not quantify stroke severity or distinguish stroke subtypes. Does not identify large vessel occlusion (LVO) — use RACE, LAMS, FAST-ED, or NIHSS for LVO detection. Sensitivity varies by stroke location (posterior stroke often missed). Single arm drift may miss subtle findings (leg weakness, sensory loss, visual field defect). Does not assess for posterior circulation symptoms (vertigo, diplopia, ataxia). Prehospital use requires brief training. Limited to 3 binary findings — coarser than NIHSS. Negative CPSS does not rule out stroke (sensitivity ~60-70%). Doesn't capture time of symptom onset (critical for tPA eligibility). Not validated for TIA diagnosis. False negatives in patients with posterior circulation strokes, small lacunar strokes, or primarily sensory deficits. Does not replace comprehensive neurological assessment.",

### delirium screening (nursing and medical)

#### E267 · Confusion Assessment Method (CAM)
<!-- src: formulas,calculators,converters.md L14126–L14149 · parse: clean · 2 copies merged (src L12298, L14126) -->
```json
{
 "name": "Confusion Assessment Method",
 "acronym": "CAM",
 "subcategory": "delirium screening (nursing and medical)",
 "purpose": "Standardized bedside tool for detecting delirium in hospitalized patients. Most widely used delirium screening instrument internationally. Uses 4 criteria derived from DSM diagnostic criteria for delirium. Also has ICU version (CAM-ICU) for intubated/non-verbal patients.",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Feature 1: Acute onset and fluctuating course",
   "description": "Is there evidence of an acute change in mental status from baseline? Does the abnormal behavior fluctuate during the day (tends to come and go)?",
   "unit": "binary",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Feature 1 (required)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Feature 2: Inattention",
   "description": "Does the patient have difficulty focusing attention (e.g., easily distractible, difficulty keeping track of what is being said)?",
   "unit": "binary",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Feature 2 (required for diagnosis)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Feature 3: Disorganized thinking",
   "description": "Is the patient's thinking disorganized or incoherent (rambling, irrelevant conversation, unpredictable switching between subjects)?",
   "unit": "binary",
   "range_or_options": "Present/Absent",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Feature 3 (supporting)"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Feature 4: Altered level of consciousness",
   "description": "Is the patient's level of consciousness anything other than alert (vigilant, lethargic, stupor, coma, hypervigilant)?",
   "unit": "binary",
   "range_or_options": "Alert (normal) vs. Altered (vigilant, lethargic, stupor, coma)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "Feature 4 (supporting)"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "CAM positive (delirium present) = Feature 1 AND Feature 2 AND (Feature 3 OR Feature 4)\n\nAcute onset/fluctuating course (1) + Inattention (2) + Disorganized thinking (3) OR Altered consciousness (4) = Delirium\n\nCAM-ICU: Modified for ICU (uses sedation assessment first, then attention test, then organized thinking, then acute change)",
 "score_range": "Positive/Negative (binary)",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "CAM Positive",
   "meaning": "Delirium present. Identify and treat underlying cause(s) (infection, medications, metabolic derangement, pain, constipation, urinary retention, alcohol withdrawal, sleep deprivation). Ensure patient safety. Consider geriatric/psychiatry consult."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "CAM Negative",
   "meaning": "Delirium not detected. Continue routine monitoring. Reassess regularly (especially if risk factors present)."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally validated by Inouye et al. 1990 in 56 elderly medical patients. Since validated in >10,000 patients across hospital, ICU, ED, and long-term care settings.",
 "original_citation": "Inouye SK, van Dyck CH, Alessi CA, et al. Clarifying confusion: the Confusion Assessment Method. A new method for detection of delirium. Ann Intern Med. 1990;113(12):941-948. PMID: 2240918",
 "additional_validation": "Wei LA, et al. J Hosp Med. 2008;3:456-462; Wong CL, et al. J Gen Intern Med. 2010;25:878-887; Ely EW, et al. JAMA. 2001;286:2703-2710 (CAM-ICU)",
 "limitations": "Requires trained assessor for reliable application. Feature 1 (acute onset/fluctuating course) may be difficult to assess if baseline mental status unknown. Fluctuation requires serial assessments — single-time application may miss delirium. Subtypes (hyperactive, hypoactive, mixed) not distinguished — hypoactive delirium may be missed. Sensitivity varies by training level of assessor (47–94%). CAM-ICU requires RASS ≥-3 (deeply sedated patients cannot be assessed). Does not distinguish delirium from dementia (dementia is a risk factor). Requires at least 5 minutes to perform — may not be feasible in busy settings. Not validated in children (use pCAM-ICU or CAPD). Does not capture severity (use CAM-S for severity scoring). False negatives possible with hypoactive delirium. Not a substitute for comprehensive delirium evaluation. Does not identify the cause of delirium.",
 "copyright_status": "Dr. Sharon Inouye — free for clinical use (copyright retained)",
 "confidence": "high"
}

 "input_variables": [
  {

  },

   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "1 (constantly moist), 2 (very moist), 3 (occasionally moist), 4 (rarely moist)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Activity",
   "description": "Degree of physical activity",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "1 (bedfast), 2 (chairfast), 3 (walks occasionally), 4 (walks frequently)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–4"
  },
  {
   "variable": "Mobility",
   "description": "Ability to change and control body position",
   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "1 (completely immobile), 2 (very limited), 3 (slightly limited), 4 (no limitation",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–4"
  },
  {

   "unit": "ordinal",

  },

   "unit": "ordinal",
   "range_or_options": "1 (problem — requires moderate to maximum assistance, slides frequently), 2 (potential problem — moves feebly, requires some assistance), 3 (no apparent problem — moves in bed independently)",
   "points_or_coefficient": "1–3"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Braden Score = Sensory perception + Moisture + Activity + Mobility + Nutrition + Friction and shear\nRange: 6–23",
 "score_range": "6–23",
 "interpretation": [

   "score_range": "19–23",
   "meaning": "No risk / Very mild risk. Standard prevention protocols. Reassess on admission and with condition change."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "15–18",
   "meaning": "Mild risk. Pressure redistribution surface, turning schedule, nutrition optimization, skin assessment every shift."
  },
  {

   "meaning": "Moderate risk. Specialty pressure-redistributing surface (alternating pressure mattress), 2-hourly repositioning, nutrition consult."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "10–12",
   "meaning": "High risk. Advanced pressure-redistributing surface (low-air-loss or alternating pressure mattress), 2-hourly repositioning, heel elevation, nutrition support, moisture management."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "≤9",
   "meaning": "Very high risk. Critical care level prevention (air-fluidized bed or equivalent), frequent repositioning, comprehensive skin care, nutrition optimization, multidisciplinary approach."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Developed by Barbara Braden and Nancy Bergstrom in 1987. Validated in >50,000 patients across hospital, long-term care, and community settings.",
 "original_citation": "Bergstrom N, Demuth PJ, Braden BJ. A clinical trial of the Braden Scale for Predicting Pressure Sore Risk. Nurs Clin North Am. 1987;22(2):417-428. PMID: 3299494; Braden BJ, Bergstrom N. Nurs Res. 1987;36:205-210",
 "additional_validation": "Pancorbo-Hidalgo PL, et al. BMC Med Res Methodol. 2006;6:1-17; Garcia-Fernandez FP, et al. Int Wound J. 2014;11:354-372",
 "limitations": "Assessing 'sensory perception' and 'moisture' can be subjective. Not validated for all patient populations (neonates, pediatrics). Sensitivity and specificity vary by cutoff score and population. Does not capture all risk factors (skin condition, medication, perfusion status). Reassessment frequency varies by institutional protocol (minimum weekly and with condition change). Not suitable for predicting medical device-related pressure injuries. Overprediction of risk in low-risk populations (high false-positive rate). Underprediction in some high-risk groups (darkly pigmented skin — skin assessment challenges). Nutrition component is subjective (nurses may not accurately assess intake). Friction/shear is the hardest component to score reliably. Must be combined with clinical judgment — score alone is insufficient for prevention planning.",

{
 "name": "Mallampati Classification",

 "subcategory": "difficult airway prediction",
 "purpose": "Preoperative airway assessment tool to predict difficult laryngoscopy and intubation. Visual assessment of the oropharyngeal structures visible with maximal mouth opening and tongue protrusion. Part of comprehensive airway assessment (should not be used in isolation).",
 "input_variables": [
  {
   "variable": "Oropharyngeal view",
   "description": "Structures visible with patient seated, mouth maximally open, tongue protruding maximally (without phonation)",
   "unit": "categorical",
   "range_or_options": "Class I, II, III, IV",
   "points_or_coefficient": "I–IV"
  }
 ],
 "formula": "Mallampati Classification (Samsoon & Young modification):\n\nClass I: Soft palate, uvula, fauces, anterior and posterior pillars visible\nClass II: Soft palate, uvula, fauces visible\nClass III: Soft palate, base of uvula visible\nClass IV: Hard palate only visible (soft palate not visible)\n\nNote: Patient should be seated upright, mouth fully open, tongue maximally protruded. No phonation during assessment.",
 "score_range": "I–IV",
 "interpretation": [
  {
   "score_range": "I",
   "meaning": "Easy intubation expected. Full visualization of structures. Low probability of difficult intubation (~1%)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "II",
   "meaning": "Likely easy intubation. Most structures visible. Low probability (~5%)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "III",
   "meaning": "Potentially difficult intubation. Only soft palate and base of uvula visible. Moderate probability (~20%)."
  },
  {
   "score_range": "IV",
   "meaning": "Difficult intubation likely. Only hard palate visible. High probability (~35–50%). Prepare for difficult airway."
  }
 ],
 "validation_population": "Originally described by Mallampati et al. 1985. Modified by Samsoon & Young 1987. Validated in >50,000 patients across multiple studies.",
 "original_citation": "Mallampati SR, Gatt SP, Gugino LD, et al. A clinical sign to predict difficult tracheal intubation: a prospective study. Can Anaesth Soc J. 1985;32(4):429-434. PMID: 4027773; Samsoon GLT, Young JRB. Anaesthesia. 1987;42:487-490",
 "additional_validation": "Shiga T, et al. Anesthesiology. 2005;103:429-437; Lee A, et al. Anesthesiology. 2006;105:692-699",
 "limitations": "Subjective assessment — inter-rater variability. Single predictor of difficult intubation — must be combined with other factors (thyromental distance, neck mobility, mouth opening, upper lip bite test, body habitus). Poor positive predictive value (~50% of Mallampati IV are still intubatable). Patient cooperation required (pain, confusion, or altered consciousness limit assessment). Position affects grading (sniffing position vs. sitting). Phonation during assessment elevates the palate — may artificially improve grade. Obesity, large tongue, or macroglossia may limit view. Does not predict difficult mask ventilation (separate assessment needed). Not validated in pediatric populations (modified assessment needed). Mallampati I–II does not guarantee easy intubation. Difficult intubation is multifactorial — no single test is sufficient. High sensitivity but low specificity for difficult intubation prediction. No single airway assessment test has both high sensitivity and specificity.",
 "copyright_status": "public domain — published academic classification",

}

  },

  },

   "unit": "binary",

   "unit": "binary",
   "range_or_options": "No (0 points), Yes (1 point)",

  },

   "unit": "binary",
